SUMMARY: Design for the AI "brain" of the DeckView Hearthstone assistant: a grounded, streaming, Markdown chat backed by Gemini 2.5-flash (free tier) behind a swappable LLM abstraction. The controlling constraint is the established performance diagnosis — long Markdown answers froze the UI for up to 3.9s by blocking the main thread. Therefore the chat design is stability-first: (a) ALL network + SSE parsing + Markdown parsing happens off the UI thread on a background dispatcher; (b) responses stream token-by-token into a VIRTUALIZED chat list so no single giant view is ever inflated; (c) grounding is done deterministically — the recognized deck/board/hand is resolved against a bundled HearthstoneJSON card DB and injected as structured, verified context so the model describes the CURRENT game and cannot invent cards; (d) a clean LlmClient interface isolates Gemini so Claude or an on-device model can be swapped later; (e) graceful offline/degraded behavior (deterministic tracker keeps working; chat shows a clear "assistant offline" state and queues). Two important verified caveats: Gemini free-tier limits are tight (~10 RPM / ~250-500 req/day for 2.5-flash as of 2026, cut 50-80% in Dec 2025), and free-tier prompts/responses are used by Google for product improvement WITH HUMAN REVIEW — a real privacy problem because DeckView's context is derived from screen capture.
KEY FINDINGS: [high] The #1 chat-side stability risk is rendering the Markdown answer on the UI thread; the fix is to keep BOTH markdown parsing AND stream handling off the main thread and stream into a virtualized list. Concretely: OkHttp/Retrofit call on Dispatchers.IO -> parse each SSE chunk off-thread -> emit deltas via a cold Flow -> UI collects on Main and appends plain text to the streaming bubble; run the Markdown parse (Markwon/CommonMark) on a background dispatcher and post only the finished Spanned back to the view. Never inflate one bubble containing the whole answer; the streaming bubble grows incrementally and the completed message becomes one RecyclerView item. | [high] Grounding must be deterministic, not model-guessed. Pipeline: vision recognition returns card IDs/dbfIds + board state -> resolve each ID against a BUNDLED HearthstoneJSON cards.collectible.json (offline, versioned per patch) to get canonical name/cost/text/mechanics -> build a compact structured 'GAME STATE' block (your deck list + drawn/remaining, known opponent cards, mana, board minions, turn) -> inject as a system/context section each turn. The model is told to answer ONLY from that block. This keeps answers about the CURRENT game and prevents hallucinated cards because the card facts come from the DB, not the model. | [high] Gemini streaming is available over plain REST/SSE and is well-suited to Android with no SDK: POST to v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse with header x-goog-api-key. Each SSE line is a GenerateContentResponse whose text is at candidates[0].content.parts[0].text; concatenating the deltas yields the full answer, and Markdown is the model's natural output format. | [medium] Gemini free-tier limits are tight and volatile — plan for throttling, not abundance. For 2.5-flash in 2026, sources report ~10 RPM, ~250,000 TPM, and ~250-500 requests/day, after Google cut free-tier quotas 50-80% on 7 Dec 2025. The assistant must therefore be REQUEST-FRUGAL: do NOT call the model on every recognized frame. Trigger a model call only on (a) explicit user chat message, or (b) a meaningful discrete game event (turn start, key card played), debounced/coalesced, with a client-side rate limiter and 429 backoff. The deterministic tracker (deck/board display) must never depend on a model call. | [high] PRIVACY RISK requiring Ignacio's decision: on the Gemini FREE tier, prompts and responses are used to improve Google products and may undergo HUMAN REVIEW; only the PAID tier guarantees data is not used for training. DeckView's context is derived from live SCREEN CAPTURE, so recognized game state (and anything the vision layer captures) would be sent to Google under free-tier terms. Mitigations: send ONLY the minimal structured game-state block and the user's typed question (never raw screenshots to the chat model), strip any incidental PII, and flag to Ignacio that true privacy requires the paid tier (a >=$0.10 cost decision) or an on-device model. | [high] A thin LlmClient abstraction makes the model swappable (Gemini -> Claude -> on-device) without touching UI or grounding code. Define: interface LlmClient { fun streamChat(system: String, gameState: GameStateContext, history: List<Turn>, userMsg: String): Flow<Delta> }. GeminiClient maps this to streamGenerateContent+SSE; a future ClaudeClient maps to the Messages streaming API; a Null/OfflineClient returns a canned degraded response. Prompt assembly and Markdown rendering are provider-agnostic and live above the interface. | [medium] Context-window / conversation state should be a rolling, bounded structure: keep a short conversation history (last N user/assistant turns) PLUS a freshly-recomputed GAME STATE block each turn (the game state supersedes stale history, so old board states are dropped rather than accumulated). This keeps token usage low (protecting the TPM/RPD budget) and keeps the model anchored to the live game instead of a long transcript. Persist the session (Room/DataStore) so a process restart or the documented session-limit cutoff does not lose the chat.
RECOMMENDATIONS: Architect the chat as a unidirectional pipeline off the UI thread: OkHttp SSE call on Dispatchers.IO -> per-chunk parse -> Flow<Delta> -> UI appends plain text to a single streaming bubble; parse Markdown (Markwon) on a background dispatcher and post only the finished Spanned. This is the direct countermeasure to the 3.9s freeze diagnosis. | Render the chat in a RecyclerView (virtualized) with paging; the in-progress answer is ONE streaming item, completed answers are individual items. Never build a monolithic view holding an entire long answer. | Bundle a versioned HearthstoneJSON cards.collectible.json in-app for OFFLINE, deterministic card resolution; resolve recognized card IDs/dbfIds to canonical facts BEFORE prompting so the model never has to remember card data (kills the main hallucination vector). | Inject a compact structured GAME STATE block each turn and instruct the model to answer only from it; recompute it fresh rather than accumulating stale board history to save tokens. | Use REST streaming: gemini-2.5-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse with x-goog-api-key; read candidates[0].content.parts[0].text deltas. Avoid pulling the full SDK if a lean OkHttp client suffices for stability/size. | Be request-frugal: call the model ONLY on explicit user messages or debounced discrete game events, with a client-side rate limiter and exponential backoff on HTTP 429. Keep the deterministic deck/board tracker fully independent of any model call. | Put a swappable LlmClient interface (Flow<Delta> streaming) between the app and Gemini so Claude or an on-device model can be dropped in later without touching UI/grounding. | Design explicit degraded states: OfflineClient / no-network -> show 'Assistant offline, deck tracking still active' and queue the user question; on repeated 429 -> show 'rate-limited, retrying' with backoff; never crash or block on a failed model call. | Escalate the privacy decision to Ignacio: free-tier Gemini uses prompts+responses for training with human review. Send only minimal structured game state + typed questions (never raw screenshots to the chat model); note that true privacy needs the paid tier (a >=$0.10 authorization) or an on-device model. | Persist the chat session (Room/DataStore) so the assistant survives process death and the documented session-limit cutoffs; reload bounded history on restart.
RISKS: (high) Repeating the original defect: parsing a long Markdown answer or inflating a large chat view on the UI thread reintroduces multi-second freezes and violates the zero-crash/PDS Gold mandate. -> Mandate off-UI-thread SSE + Markdown parsing, incremental streaming into a virtualized RecyclerView, and a max-render-chunk cap; add a StrictMode/thread-time assertion in debug and a synthetic 'very long answer' test in the harness. | (high) Gemini free-tier quotas are tight (~10 RPM / ~250-500 RPD for 2.5-flash) and were cut 50-80% in Dec 2025; per-frame or chatty usage will hit 429s and make the assistant feel broken. -> Event-debounced, rate-limited requests with 429 backoff; deterministic tracker independent of the model; cache/reuse answers; surface a clear rate-limited UI state instead of hanging. | (high) Free-tier data policy: screen-capture-derived game state and user questions are sent to Google and may be used for training with human review — a privacy exposure for potentially sensitive screen content. -> Send only minimal structured state (no raw screenshots to the chat model); PII-strip; escalate paid-tier (>=$0.10) or on-device model choice to Ignacio as an explicit decision. | (medium) Hallucinated cards / wrong game facts erode trust in a competitive tool if the model is asked to recall card data or infer board state. -> Deterministic HearthstoneJSON resolution of all card facts before prompting; instruct model to answer only from the injected verified state and to say 'unknown' rather than guess; validate any card names the model emits against the DB before display. | (medium) Model/API drift: by 2026 Google shipped Gemini 3 / a newer Interactions API and deprecates preview model IDs; a hardcoded gemini-2.5-flash-preview endpoint may break. -> Isolate the endpoint/model ID behind the LlmClient and remote-config the model name; monitor for deprecation; the abstraction lets you move to a current model or Claude with one implementation change. | (low) Unbounded conversation history inflates token usage (blowing the TPM budget) and dilutes grounding with stale board states. -> Bounded rolling history (last N turns) + fresh game-state block each turn that supersedes old state; measure token usage against the live TPM limit and tune N.
OPEN Qs: Exact current free-tier limits for gemini-2.5-flash are project-specific and vary across 2026 sources (~10 RPM, ~250K TPM, ~250-500 RPD) — confirm the real numbers in the target project's Google AI Studio rate-limit view before finalizing the rate limiter. | Will Ignacio accept free-tier data-usage terms (training + human review of screen-derived context), or is paid tier / on-device required? This is a cost+privacy decision (>=$0.10 threshold). | Should DeckView adopt the newer Gemini 'Interactions API' (stateful) or stay on the classic streamGenerateContent endpoint for maximum control and a leaner Android footprint? | What is the target answer length/verbosity? A max-output-tokens cap directly bounds render cost and TPM usage and should be set deliberately given the freeze history. | Is vision (card recognition) using the SAME Gemini call as chat, or a separate pipeline? This affects request budgeting and whether screenshots ever reach the chat model.

=== YOUR ARCHITECTURE ANGLE: stability-lean ===
PRIORITY = ship-lean + maximum stability. Prefer the SIMPLEST thing that works: capture only a FEW frames per second (or on-demand snapshots), identify cards with CLOUD Gemini 2.5-flash vision on a background thread, keep an offline DECKSTRING-IMPORT fallback so the tracker works even if vision fails. Minimal moving parts. The AI chat is the star; live recognition is best-effort.

Design a complete END-TO-END architecture for DeckView from scratch under this angle. Be concrete: name the tech stack (Kotlin? Compose vs Views? DI? persistence?), the module breakdown under dev.lyai.deckview.*, the full data flow (capture -> recognition -> state store -> tracker UI + AI chat), the recognition approach, and EXACTLY how it prevents the diagnosed main-thread markdown freeze and guarantees crash-safety. Respect the free-API/cost constraints.

### **Claude** `01:01`

This is a planning-only design task and I have the full research digest and constraints in context, so I'll synthesize the architecture directly and return it via StructuredOutput.

### **You** `01:02`

PROJECT: DeckView — an Android app to be BUILT FROM SCRATCH (no existing source code exists). Product owner: Ignacio (LyAi Labs). Package namespace: dev.lyai.deckview.*

PRODUCT: A Hearthstone deck tracker with an integrated AI CHAT interface (assistant answers in Markdown).

CONFIRMED CORE INPUT MECHANISM (decided by product owner): real-time SCREEN CAPTURE via Android MediaProjection. Hearthstone runs on the SAME Android device; DeckView observes the game screen, recognizes cards / board / deck state via computer vision or AI, tracks the deck, and an AI chat comments and answers questions in Markdown.
WHY screen-capture (not log parsing): on Android you CANNOT read another app's files (sandbox), unlike PC trackers (Hearthstone Deck Tracker, Firestone) that parse Power.log. Screen capture + vision is the only viable on-device path.

ALREADY BUILT (prototype to reuse/learn from): dev.lyai.deckview.spike — a MediaProjection screen-capture harness. Captures 800x360 at ~33-60fps, logs per-frame proc_ms/inter_ms and process CPU, and dumps JPEG frames on jank (2 FPS "dataset" mode). It is effectively the prototype of the capture pipeline.

PERFORMANCE DIAGNOSIS (established with high confidence from real capture logs — bake these lessons into the plan):
- Per-frame processing is trivial (proc_ms ~2ms median). Not compute-bound.
- The app suffered multi-second UI FREEZES: inter-frame gaps up to 3.9s, costing 26-55% of wall-clock time in sessions where a LONG Markdown AI chat message was on screen.
- Capture-process CPU DROPS during freezes and an independent ~2s timer NEVER stalled -> the freeze is a BLOCKED render/UI thread waiting on something, NOT heavy compute and NOT OS suspension.
- Freezes correlated with rendering LONG Markdown chat messages, NOT with the capture/JPEG-dump machinery (the session that dumped the most frames was the SMOOTHEST).
- CONCLUSION: the #1 stability risk is MAIN-THREAD BLOCKING while rendering long Markdown chat messages. The architecture MUST parse/measure Markdown OFF the UI thread, virtualize the chat list, and stream/paginate incrementally.

HARD PRIORITY (product owner): STABILITY FIRST — zero crashes, smooth end-to-end (LyAi "PDS Gold Rule": no crashes in production, 99.99% uptime). Accuracy and features are secondary to never freezing/crashing.

LyAi ORGANIZATION CONSTRAINTS (must respect in every recommendation):
- Any action costing >= $0.10 requires explicit authorization from Ignacio.
- STRONGLY prefer FREE APIs: Gemini 2.5-flash (free) is the default for vision + chat. Avoid paid APIs (Imagen 4, Google Places, paid cloud vision) unless flagged as needing authorization.
- Privacy/on-device is a plus; screen contents may be sensitive.
- This exercise is PLANNING ONLY. No build/deploy. "Propuesta antes de aplicar."


=== CANDIDATE ARCHITECTURES ===
### DeckView — Stability-Lean Architecture
Thesis: Ship the smallest possible pipeline: throttled MediaProjection snapshots + cloud Gemini vision (best-effort) on background threads, with deckstring import as the authoritative offline tracker, so the grounded streaming AI chat is the star and the diagnosed main-thread Markdown freeze is engineered out from day one.
Stack: Language=Kotlin, UI framework=Jetpack Compose shell + AndroidView(Markwon) for chat bubbles, Chat list=LazyColumn with stable keys + @Immutable message models, Async=Coroutines + Flow (Dispatchers.IO for network/SSE, Dispatchers.Default for parsing), DI=Hilt, Networking=OkHttp (raw SSE), no Retrofit/SDK, LLM abstraction=interface LlmClient { fun streamChat(...): Flow<Delta> } with GeminiClient / OfflineClient, Capture=MediaProjection + VirtualDisplay + ImageReader in a mediaProjection foreground service on a HandlerThread, Recognition (fast path)=On-device luma-diff / 64-bit pHash change-detector, Recognition (identify)=Cloud Gemini 2.5-flash vision, background, best-effort, Card data=Bundled HearthstoneJSON cards.collectible.json + ported deckstring codec, Persistence=Room (chat turns, session, recognition cache) + DataStore (settings, API key, active deckstring), Markdown=Markwon 4.6.x with PrecomputedTextSetterCompat on a background Executor, Overlay (optional v2)=TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY tracker bubble, FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE, alpha<=0.8, Guardrails=StrictMode (debug) + JankStats/FrameMetrics + spike-harness inter_ms regression gate
Data flow: 1) Onboarding: user pastes a DECKSTRING -> decoded to 30 dbfIds -> resolved against bundled HearthstoneJSON -> written to GameStateStore as the authoritative deck. 2) User grants MediaProjection consent -> capture FGS starts VirtualDisplay->ImageReader at ~2fps on a HandlerThread. 3) onImageAvailable -> acquireLatestImage/copy/close -> throttle gate -> on-device change-detector; only "changed+stable" frames enqueue (drop-oldest, cap 1) a cropped JPEG. 4) Background recognition worker -> Gemini vision (timeout, cancellable, rate-limited, debounced to discrete events) -> dbfIds resolved via HearthstoneJSON; on offline/429/low-confidence it simply skips. 5) Results merged into GameStateStore (single-source-of-truth StateFlow) = deckstring minus observed drawn/played cards + best-effort board/opponent cards. 6) Tracker UI (Compose) collects the StateFlow and renders deck list/counts/board — driven ONLY by the deterministic store, never by a pending model call. 7) On explicit user chat message OR a debounced discrete game event, the chat layer assembles a compact structured GAME STATE block (canonical facts from the DB, not model memory) + bounded rolling history + the question -> GeminiChatClient streamGenerateContent?alt=sse on Dispatchers.IO -> Flow<Delta>. 8) UI appends plain text to the single streaming bubble (throttled 1/frame); on completion, parse Markdown off-thread -> cache Spanned -> swap into the AndroidView(Markwon) bubble. 9) Chat turns + session state persisted to Room so a process kill / session-limit cutoff loses nothing.
Recognition: Cloud-first, best-effort, gated. A sub-millisecond on-device change-detector (downscaled luma-diff or 64-bit perceptual hash) runs at the ~2fps capture rate purely to decide "scene changed AND stable (debounced)". Only then is a cropped/downscaled JPEG handed off — via a bounded drop-oldest queue (capacity 1) — to a background coroutine that calls Gemini 2.5-flash vision to identify the played card / board / mulligan. Returned card names/IDs are resolved deterministically against a BUNDLED HearthstoneJSON cards.collectible.json (offline, versioned per patch) to canonical dbfId + facts. No bundled pHash reference DB and no LiteRT classifier to maintain per expansion — cloud vision absorbs the open-set problem, which is the core lean bet. The load-bearing fallback: user imports their deck as a DECKSTRING (base64/varint decode, ported from hearthstone-deckstrings) giving a ground-truth 30-card set; the tracker is authoritative from the deckstring minus observed drawn/played cards, so it works fully even if vision returns nothing, is offline, or is rate-limited. Vision only refines/annotates; it is never on the critical path.
Stability: Two independent freeze surfaces, both engineered out. (1) CAPTURE/RECOGNITION never touches the UI thread: MediaProjection -> VirtualDisplay -> ImageReader(maxImages=2-3) lives in a FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MEDIA_PROJECTION service on a dedicated HandlerThread; every onImageAvailable does acquireLatestImage()+copy+close() in a finally block (missing close() is the classic ANR), throttle-gates to ~2fps, and drops frames via a capacity-1 drop-oldest queue so a slow Gemini round-trip can never back up the buffer or block anything. (2) The DIAGNOSED CHAT FREEZE (long Markdown blocking main thread for up to 3.9s) is killed by four rules: (a) SSE + Markdown parsing run OFF the main thread (Dispatchers.IO for the stream, Dispatchers.Default for CommonMark->Spanned); (b) the chat is a VIRTUALIZED LazyColumn with stable keys — the in-progress answer is ONE streaming item, completed answers are individual items, never a monolithic view holding the whole answer; (c) streaming appends plain text incrementally, throttled to at most one UI update per frame (Flow.sample ~33ms), and on completion the finished message is parsed to a Spanned off-thread, cached (LruCache by id+contentHash), and rendered via AndroidView(Markwon) using PrecomputedText so the UI thread only blocks at measure(); (d) incomplete Markdown delimiters are suppressed while streaming. CRASH-SAFETY: a MediaProjection state machine enforces the Android 14+ order (createScreenCaptureIntent -> consent -> startForeground -> getMediaProjection -> registerCallback -> createVirtualDisplay) and treats every onStop() cause (stop chip, screen lock, another projection, process death, single-use-token expiry) as graceful re-consent, never a crash; every vision/chat call is timeout-bounded, cancellable, with 429 backoff and offline fallback; the deterministic deckstring tracker survives with zero network. Guardrails from day one: StrictMode thread policy in debug, JankStats/FrameMetrics assertions, and the existing spike harness reused as a regression gate — any inter_ms > ~700ms during a scripted long-Markdown stream is a build failure.
Pros: Fewest moving parts: no on-device ML model to train, no pHash reference DB to regenerate every expansion — cloud Gemini vision absorbs open-set recognition, cutting maintenance to a per-patch HearthstoneJSON data drop.; Directly neutralizes the diagnosed freeze: off-thread SSE + Markdown parse, virtualized chat list, one-update-per-frame throttling, and PrecomputedText — with an automated spike-harness regression gate so it cannot silently regress.; Graceful degradation is built in: deckstring import makes the tracker authoritative and fully offline, so the product works even when vision is offline, rate-limited, or wrong — recognition is pure best-effort upside.; Free-tier only and cost-gated: change-detector + event-debouncing hold both vision and chat to a handful of calls per game, trivially under $0.10 and designed around the volatile free-tier RPD caps; deterministic tracker never depends on a model call.; The AI chat (the product star) is first-class: grounded on deterministic HearthstoneJSON facts (no hallucinated cards), streaming, Markdown, persisted, and swappable behind LlmClient (Gemini -> Claude -> on-device).; Crash-safety is structural: a MediaProjection state machine handles Android 14+ FGS ordering, single-use consent, and every onStop() cause as graceful re-consent; all network calls are timeout-bounded, cancellable, with 429 backoff.
Cons: Live recognition is online-only, latency-bound (0.7-3s per Gemini call), and hostage to volatile free-tier RPD caps — so real-time frame-accurate tracking is NOT delivered; recognition is laggy/best-effort and leans heavily on the deckstring fallback for correctness.; Privacy exposure needs an Ignacio decision: free-tier sends screen-derived cropped frames + game state to Google (used for training, human review); truly private operation requires the paid tier (>=$0.10) or an on-device model, neither of which this lean design ships.; Recognition accuracy is capped by Gemini reading low-res (~800x360) frames — small fanned hand cards may be misread, likely forcing selective higher-res ROI capture later (a stability/CPU tradeoff the lean v1 defers).; The experience degrades to mediocre without deckstring import; a fully 'blind' screen-only mode is weak, so onboarding effectively depends on the user pasting a deck code.; Vision and chat share ONE tight free-tier budget, so heavy chat use can starve recognition calls (and vice versa) — the rate limiter must arbitrate, and a single quota change from Google can degrade both at once.; AndroidView(Markwon) inside a Compose LazyColumn is an interop seam (measurement/recycling quirks, two UI paradigms) — a deliberate stability-over-purity compromise that adds a bit of glue and testing surface versus an all-Compose or all-Views stack.
Cost: Free-tier only. Gemini 2.5-flash serves BOTH vision recognition and chat; a cheap on-device change-detector gates vision so only a handful of calls fire per game (change+stable, debounced to discrete events), and chat calls fire only on explicit user messages or debounced game events with a client-side rate limiter + 429 backoff. An 800x360 frame is ~500 input tokens (~$0.00015) and media_resolution=LOW cuts it further, so per-call cost is trivially under the $0.10 authorization threshold — the real budget constraint is free-tier RPD (~250-500/day, volatile since the Dec-2025 cuts), not dollars. No paid APIs (no Imagen 4, no paid cloud vision), no on-device model to train/ship. PRIVACY COST-DECISION for Ignacio: free-tier prompts/responses are used for training with human review, and DeckView's context is screen-derived — mitigate by sending only cropped card ROIs to vision and minimal structured state to chat (never raw full screenshots); true privacy requires paid tier (>=$0.10) or an on-device model, flagged as an explicit Ignacio call.
Complexity: medium

### DeckView "Realtime Vision Engine" — on-device continuous recognition, off-thread everything
Thesis: A Kotlin single-Activity app where a foreground MediaProjection service feeds a fully off-thread on-device vision engine (change-detector → pHash/LiteRT/OpenCV template match against a bundled HearthstoneJSON art DB) that continuously tracks draws/plays/board into a single source-of-truth state store, with a virtualized Compose+AndroidView(Markwon) chat grounded on that state and streamed off the UI thread — maximizing recognition accuracy and real-time responsiveness while structurally making the diagnosed main-thread markdown freeze impossible.
Stack: Language=Kotlin (100%), coroutines + Flow, UI toolkit=Jetpack Compose for the overlay/tracker UI + Views interop (AndroidView) ONLY for the Markwon-rendered chat message bodies, Chat list virtualization=LazyColumn with stable keys (message.id) + @Immutable message models; trailing streaming bubble is one item, Markdown=Markwon 4.6.x with textSetter(PrecomputedTextSetterCompat.create(bgExecutor)); block-based append-only streaming, Capture=MediaProjection → VirtualDisplay → ImageReader(RGBA_8888, maxImages=3) on a dedicated HandlerThread, inside a FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MEDIA_PROJECTION service, Recognition — gating=Sub-ms on-device change-detector: downscaled luma frame-diff + 64-bit pHash, runs every captured frame; fires identification only on CHANGED+STABLE (debounced) frames, Recognition — phase=ROI fingerprint state machine (menu/mulligan/in-game/victory) as Stage-1 cheap classifier, Recognition — identify=Primary pHash(64-bit)+Hamming over fixed ROIs against bundled reference DB; LiteRT INT8 MobileNet embedding + OpenCV template match as art confirmer; ML Kit Text Recognition v2 (on-device, offline) for card names + mana/attack/health digits as disambiguator/number reader, Card DB=Bundled versioned HearthstoneJSON cards.collectible.json + precomputed reference pHash/embedding assets, keyed on dbfId; hearthstone-deckstrings decode for import, Cloud vision (fallback only)=Gemini 2.5-flash, event-gated, <30 calls/match, media_resolution=LOW, cropped ROI, cached by pHash, AI chat brain=Gemini 2.5-flash streamGenerateContent?alt=sse via lean OkHttp, behind a swappable LlmClient{ streamChat(...):Flow<Delta> } interface, State store=Single source of truth: a GameState StateFlow in a repository, updated only by the recognition engine via a bounded drop-oldest channel, DI=Hilt, Persistence=Room (chat history, session, imported decks) + DataStore (settings/API key/consent flags), Overlay=TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY (SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW), FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE, touch-passthrough, alpha≤0.8, Networking=OkHttp (SSE) on Dispatchers.IO; kotlinx.serialization
Data flow: CAPTURE (HandlerThread): MediaProjection→VirtualDisplay→ImageReader.onImageAvailable → acquireLatestImage → copy pixels → close() immediately (finally) → post copy to a capacity-1 drop-oldest channel. Continuous ~2 fps throttle (config 1-4). --> GATING (Dispatchers.Default worker): luma-diff + pHash on downscaled frame; if unchanged or unstable, drop. On CHANGED+STABLE: Stage-1 ROI phase classifier decides scene. --> IDENTIFY (Default worker): for the active phase run pHash+Hamming over fixed ROIs; confirm art via LiteRT embedding/OpenCV template match; read names/numbers via ML Kit OCR; fuse with confidence; below threshold → mark unknown (optionally escalate ONE gated Gemini call). Own-deck matches constrained to imported 30-card deckstring candidate set. --> STATE STORE: recognizer emits discrete EVENTS (card drawn, card played, minion entered/left board, turn changed, mana) → reducer updates GameState StateFlow (deck remaining, hand-known, board, opponent-seen, turn/mana). This is the deterministic tracker; it never touches network. --> TRACKER UI: Compose overlay + in-app screens collect GameState StateFlow and re-render the HUD reactively (fast, no blocking). --> AI CHAT: on explicit user message OR a debounced discrete game event, ChatController snapshots GameState → resolves dbfIds against bundled HearthstoneJSON to build a compact structured GAME STATE block → LlmClient.streamChat (OkHttp SSE on IO) → Flow<Delta> → UI appends plain text to the single streaming bubble; Markwon parses the trailing block off-thread (bgExecutor) and posts finished PrecomputedText back → completed message cached (LruCache by id+hash) and persisted (Room). Offline/429 → OfflineClient degraded state; tracker keeps running.
Recognition: Continuous on-device multi-signal fusion, event-gated for real-time cost. Every captured frame (~2 fps) hits a sub-ms change-detector (luma-diff + 64-bit pHash); only CHANGED+STABLE frames trigger identification. A Stage-1 ROI-fingerprint state machine classifies game phase (menu/mulligan/in-game/victory) and routes which recognizers run. Primary identifier is perceptual hashing (pHash + Hamming distance) over fixed screen ROIs against a bundled reference DB precomputed offline from HearthstoneJSON 256x/512x tile art, keyed on dbfId. Art matches are confirmed by a LiteRT INT8 MobileNet embedding (nearest-neighbor) and/or OpenCV template match; ML Kit Text Recognition v2 (offline) reads card names and mana/attack/health digits as a disambiguator and number source. Signals are fused with confidence scoring; below threshold the engine ABSTAINS ('unknown') rather than guessing, and may escalate a single gated Gemini 2.5-flash call on a cropped ROI. Prioritize LARGE unambiguous targets (played-card center animation, mulligan cards, board minions, mana gems) over small fanned hand cards, and detect draw/play as EVENTS. Deckstring import is a first-class onboarding feature: the user's own deck collapses recognition to a 30-card candidate set (huge accuracy+speed win); opponent tracking stays open-set from observed played cards. The 800x360 spike resolution is treated as a tunable dial — ROIs captured at higher selective resolution where card-art discrimination demands it, benchmarked on-device.
Stability: (duplicate key not allowed — see stabilityApproach above)
Pros: Highest accuracy of the angles: multi-signal on-device fusion (pHash + LiteRT embedding + OpenCV template + ML Kit OCR) with abstain-on-low-confidence and deckstring-constrained candidate sets.; True real-time responsiveness: continuous capture with a sub-ms change-detector gate, few-ms on-device inference, no network in the recognition hot path — works fully offline.; Freeze is impossible by construction: off-thread Markwon+PrecomputedText, block-based streaming, virtualized LazyColumn, coalesced token updates, plus CI regression gate via the existing spike harness.; Crash-safe MediaProjection state machine handling Android 14+ consent order, single-use token, and every onStop() path; back-pressure ANR prevented by acquireLatestImage()+close().; Deterministic tracker is fully decoupled from network/model — quota cuts, 429s, or offline never break or freeze deck tracking.; Cost- and privacy-aligned with LyAi: free on-device pipeline default, cloud gated far under $0.10 and free-tier RPD, minimal structured context sent (never raw screenshots).; Swappable LlmClient and updatable-as-data-drop card DB make it resilient to Gemini deprecation and Hearthstone set churn.; Reuses the proven spike capture harness as the eventing backbone and as the anti-jank regression gate.
Cons: Highest engineering complexity of the angles: LiteRT model + OpenCV templates + pHash DB + ML Kit fusion + confidence tuning is substantial build and maintenance surface.; Reference hash/embedding DB and LiteRT classifier rot on every Hearthstone expansion/nerf/new-art variant; needs a per-patch asset regeneration and versioning pipeline.; 800x360-class capture is likely too low for reliable fanned-hand card-art pHash; forces selective higher-res ROIs (more CPU/memory/heat) — a real accuracy-vs-battery tradeoff to tune empirically.; Continuous capture + on-device inference is battery/thermal heavy on a device also running Hearthstone; thermal throttling could itself cause jank if not aggressively gated.; Compose+AndroidView(Markwon) interop for chat adds an interop seam and must be certified against the freeze gate; a pure-Compose team pays a learning/verification cost.; GPU-delegate LiteRT can silently CPU-fallback and run slower on some SoCs; requires per-device benchmarking before enabling.; Opponent tracking stays open-set (no deckstring), so opponent recognition accuracy is inherently weaker and harder than own-deck tracking.; ToS/anti-cheat ambiguity for a screen-reading advisor (grayer than PC log trackers) — needs a product/ToS decision from Ignacio; kept strictly observational, no input automation.
Cost: Near-zero recurring cost. Recognition is 100% on-device (pHash, LiteRT INT8, OpenCV, ML Kit OCR) — free, offline, private, no per-frame network. Cloud is used only for (a) the AI chat brain and (b) rare hard-board disambiguation, via Gemini 2.5-flash FREE tier, event-gated to <30 calls/match with media_resolution=LOW cropped ROIs and pHash-cache dedupe — an 800x360 frame is ~64-72 tokens at LOW, so per-call cost is fractions of a cent and total stays far under the $0.10 authorization threshold and the free-tier RPD cap. No paid vision API. Two items to flag to Ignacio as explicit decisions (not blockers): free-tier Gemini uses prompts+responses for training with human review — mitigated by sending ONLY the minimal structured GAME STATE block + typed question (never raw screenshots to the chat model); true privacy would need paid tier or an on-device LLM (a >=$0.10 / product call). Bundled HearthstoneJSON assets add app size but zero runtime cost.
Complexity: high

### DeckView Hybrid-Balanced: On-device gate + cloud-identify, stability-first
Thesis: A cheap on-device change-detector decides WHEN a card region changed and crops it; free Gemini 2.5-flash identifies only those changed crops (bounded to a few calls/game), while deckstring import narrows the candidate set and every heavy stage (capture, CV, Markdown parse, LLM) runs off the UI thread with hard back-pressure and crash guards.
Stack: Language=Kotlin (100%), coroutines + Flow, UI toolkit=Android Views + RecyclerView for the CHAT; Compose allowed only for the static tracker overlay/settings, Markdown=Markwon 4.6.x with textSetter(PrecomputedTextSetterCompat.create(bgExecutor)), Capture=MediaProjection -> VirtualDisplay -> ImageReader(maxImages=2-3, RGBA_8888) on a dedicated HandlerThread inside a FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MEDIA_PROJECTION service, On-device fast-path=Downscaled luma frame-diff + 64-bit pHash change/stability detector; ROI pHash match against bundled reference DB; ML Kit Text Recognition v2 for names/digits, Cloud vision + chat=Gemini 2.5-flash (free tier) via lean OkHttp SSE, behind a swappable LlmClient/VisionClient interface, Card data=Bundled, versioned HearthstoneJSON cards.collectible.json + precomputed pHash reference DB (keyed on dbfId); python-hearthstone deckstring decode, State store=Single source of truth GameStateStore as a StateFlow<GameState> (deck, drawn/remaining, board, mana, turn, opponent-known), Persistence=Room (chat history + session) + DataStore (settings/deckstring/API key), DI=Hilt
Data flow: MediaProjection (FGS + HandlerThread) -> ImageReader.acquireLatestImage() [always copy pixels + close() immediately in finally; throttle-gate to ~2 fps, drop stale] -> copy handed to a bounded drop-oldest (capacity 1) recognition queue on Dispatchers.Default. RecognitionWorker: (1) Stage-A phase classifier via tiny ROI fingerprints (menu/mulligan/in-game/victory); (2) per relevant ROI run sub-ms luma-diff + pHash change+stability detector -> only CHANGED+STABLE regions proceed; (3) crop the changed ROI, pHash-match against the deckstring-constrained candidate DB + ML Kit OCR for name/digits; (4) if confidence >= threshold -> emit RecognitionEvent(dbfId); if low-confidence -> enqueue the single crop to VisionClient (Gemini LOW-res, async/timeout-bounded/cancellable, rate-limited) and emit event on return, else mark 'unknown' (abstain, never guess). Events reduce into GameStateStore (StateFlow<GameState>). Tracker overlay (TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY, excluded from capture) observes GameState and renders deck/drawn/remaining. AI chat: on explicit user message OR a debounced discrete game event, build a compact structured GAME STATE block (facts resolved from bundled HearthstoneJSON, not the model) + bounded rolling history -> LlmClient.streamChat() on Dispatchers.IO -> OkHttp SSE parsed off-thread -> Flow<Delta> -> UI appends plain text to ONE streaming RecyclerView bubble (append-only, block-based, tokens coalesced to <=1 UI update/frame, unclosed delimiters suppressed) -> Markwon parses each finalized block off-thread and posts back a cached PrecomputedText. Nothing on the capture, CV, SSE, or Markdown path ever touches the main thread.
Recognition: Two-tier, event-driven, deckstring-constrained. Tier 0 (every processed frame, sub-ms, on-device): tiny-ROI phase fingerprint + luma-diff/pHash change-and-stability detector — this is the load-bearing 'WHEN did something change' gate that keeps inference count and cloud calls 1-2 orders of magnitude lower. Tier 1 (only on changed+stable relevant ROIs, on-device, free): 64-bit pHash Hamming-distance match against a bundled reference DB restricted to the imported deckstring's 30 dbfIds (+ observed opponent cards), with ML Kit OCR reading the card name and mana/attack/health digits as primary/tie-breaker. Target LARGE unambiguous elements (played-card center animation, mulligan cards, board minions, mana gems) as EVENTS — not the small fanned hand. Tier 2 (fallback only, cloud, gated): when on-device confidence is below threshold, send just the cropped changed region to Gemini 2.5-flash at media_resolution=LOW; cache by pHash to dedupe; if still ambiguous, abstain and mark 'unknown' rather than guess. Deckstring import is a first-class onboarding step and the single biggest accuracy+stability+cost lever.
Stability: Five structural guarantees against the diagnosed main-thread freeze and for zero-crash: (1) OFF-THREAD BY CONSTRUCTION — capture on a HandlerThread, CV on Dispatchers.Default, SSE on Dispatchers.IO, Markdown parse via Markwon's background executor; the UI thread only ever receives an already-parsed PrecomputedText and only blocks at measure(). (2) BACK-PRESSURE — ImageReader maxImages=2-3 with acquireLatestImage()+close() in a finally on every callback; recognition and vision fed via bounded drop-oldest (capacity 1) queues so a slow pHash or a 3s Gemini round-trip drops frames instead of stalling. (3) STREAMING DISCIPLINE — virtualized RecyclerView (only visible bubbles render), append-only block-based streaming that re-parses only the trailing block, token coalescing to one UI update per frame, incomplete-delimiter suppression, per-message Spanned LruCache so re-scroll never re-parses. (4) CRASH-SAFETY — strict Android 14+ MediaProjection call order (createScreenCaptureIntent -> startForeground -> getMediaProjection -> registerCallback -> createVirtualDisplay) wrapped in explicit handlers for SecurityException/IllegalStateException/MissingForegroundServiceTypeException; every onStop() (stop chip, screen lock, another projection, process death) is a first-class state that releases resources and prompts fresh consent (never silent resume); black/low-variance frame guard; Gemini calls timeout-bounded, cancellable, with 429 backoff and offline degradation; deterministic tracker keeps working with zero network. (5) REGRESSION GATE — reuse the spike harness inter_ms as a CI guard: any inter_ms > ~700ms during a scripted long-Markdown streaming test fails the build; StrictMode in debug flags any main-thread parse/I-O; JankStats asserts no frame > ~200ms while a long message renders.
Pros: Cost- and privacy-optimal: on-device fast-path carries continuous load for free and offline; cloud is a bounded, gated fallback, so it survives Google's volatile free-tier RPD cuts and never blocks the critical path.; Directly neutralizes the diagnosed freeze: change-gating means CV rarely fires, and the Views+Markwon+PrecomputedText+virtualized-RecyclerView chat keeps all Markdown parse off the UI thread by construction.; Deckstring import collapses recognition from open-set ~4000 cards to ~30 candidates — the single biggest simultaneous win for accuracy, latency, cost, and stability.; Reuses the proven spike harness as capture backbone AND as an inter_ms regression gate, turning the prior diagnosis into an automated build guard.; Swappable LlmClient/VisionClient abstraction future-proofs against model deprecation and lets Gemini->Claude->on-device be a DI binding change, not a rewrite.; Deterministic tracker is fully independent of any network call, so deck tracking keeps working rate-limited or offline — satisfies the PDS Gold zero-crash mandate.; Grounding via bundled HearthstoneJSON resolves card facts deterministically before prompting, killing the main LLM hallucination vector.
Cons: Two UI paradigms (Views for chat, Compose for overlay/settings) adds cognitive/build overhead versus committing to one toolkit.; Cloud fallback in the recognition path introduces 0.7-3s latency and an online dependency for hard cards; must be strictly async/cancellable or it risks reintroducing the very stall it's meant to avoid — needs careful load-testing (long chat message on screen WHILE a board is being recognized).; 800x360-class capture may be too low-res to reliably pHash even large elements; ROI resolution may need selective raising, which trades CPU/battery against stability and requires on-device benchmarking before dimensions are fixed.; Bundled reference-hash DB and card JSON go stale each Hearthstone patch (~3x/year plus nerfs and new golden/diamond art), requiring a maintained data-drop pipeline.; Free-tier data policy (training + human review of screen-derived context) is a real privacy exposure requiring Ignacio's explicit paid-vs-free decision, not something the architecture can fully solve on-device unless the chat model is also moved on-device.; Requires deckstring import for best results; a fully 'blind' screen-only mode is materially harder (open-set) and degrades the accuracy/stability guarantees — needs product-owner confirmation it's an acceptable onboarding step.; More moving parts (two-tier recognizer, bounded queues, state machine for consent) than a pure on-device or pure-cloud design — higher initial build and test surface.
Cost: Effectively free under the >=$0.10 rule. On-device pHash + ML Kit OCR are $0/offline/private and carry the continuous recognition load. Cloud Gemini 2.5-flash is used only as a low-confidence fallback on cropped LOW-res regions (~64-72 input tokens ≈ ~$0.00015/call) plus the chat itself, hard-throttled to <~30 calls/game via change-gating, debounce, caching, and a client-side rate limiter with 429 backoff — staying well inside the volatile free-tier RPD and far below any authorization threshold. Two items need Ignacio's explicit decision, both flagged not assumed: free-tier data policy (prompts/responses used for training WITH human review, and DeckView context derives from screen capture) — mitigated by sending only minimal structured game-state text + typed questions and cropped regions, never raw full screenshots; true privacy would require paid tier or an on-device chat model (a >=$0.10 decision). Bundled HearthstoneJSON redistribution licensing is the other open item.
Complexity: high
