## 5. Hearthstone data

**Card DB — HearthstoneJSON.** Bundle `cards.collectible.json` (versioned per patch) as an app asset for offline, deterministic resolution. Each card carries a string `cardId` (e.g. `EX1_001`) and a numeric **`dbfId`** (e.g. Leeroy = 559) plus name/cost/type/text/mechanics. `dbfId` is the join key across everything. Reference-art render/tile API (256×/512×) is used *only* offline if a pHash reference DB is ever added in v2 — **not needed for v1** (cloud vision absorbs recognition).

**Deckstring format.** A deck code is base64 of a varint stream keyed on `dbfId` (format version, then 1×/2×/n× card blocks). Port HearthSim's `hearthstone-deckstrings` codec into `dev.lyai.deckview.deckstring`. On import: decode → list of `(dbfId, count)` → resolve each vs the bundled DB → seed `GameStateStore` with an authoritative 30-card deck.

**Recognition → card IDs.** The deck's hidden contents are never observable; DeckView tracks *events* (card drawn/played), exactly like any tracker. Pipeline: change-detector + phase classifier decide a discrete event occurred → a cropped/downscaled frame goes to ML Kit OCR (name/digits) and/or Gemini vision, **constrained to the imported deck's ~30 dbfIds + already-seen opponent cards** (the single biggest accuracy+latency+cost lever). The recognizer returns a `dbfId` (or ABSTAINS on low confidence). The reducer subtracts it from remaining counts. Priority targets are large, unambiguous elements — the played-card center animation, mulligan cards, board minions — never the small fanned hand.

---

## 6. Stability plan (PRIORITY)

Two independent freeze surfaces, both engineered out from day one, plus structural crash-safety.

### 6.1 The diagnosed Markdown main-thread freeze (up to 3.9s) — killed by four rules

1. **Off-thread parsing, always.** SSE stream handled on `Dispatchers.IO`; CommonMark→Spanned on `Dispatchers.Default` via Markwon built once with `textSetter(PrecomputedTextSetterCompat.create(backgroundExecutor))`. The UI thread receives an already-parsed Spanned/`PrecomputedText` and only blocks at `measure()`. All CommonMark parsing runs inside a coroutine — the main thread never parses.
2. **Virtualized chat list.** `LazyColumn` with `key = message.id` and `@Immutable` message models. The in-progress answer is **one** streaming item; completed answers are individual items. A monolithic view holding the whole answer is never inflated. Parsing is kept out of composition entirely.
3. **Incremental, throttled streaming.** Tokens append plain text to the single streaming bubble, coalesced to **≤1 UI update per frame** (`Flow.sample(~33ms)` / `conflate()`). Never `setText` per token. On completion the finished message is parsed off-thread, cached in an `LruCache` (key = id + content hash), and rendered via `AndroidView(Markwon)` + `PrecomputedText`. Re-scroll/rebind reuses the cached Spanned — never re-parses.
4. **Delimiter suppression while streaming.** A lightweight single-pass `MarkdownBuffer` hides trailing unclosed `**`, `*`, `` ` ``, ` ``` ` until closed (prevents flicker); on completion the full unmodified text is rendered so intentional lone markers survive.

**PrecomputedText correctness:** set `textSize/typeface/textDir/breakStrategy` on the target `TextView` *before* building `Params`, or `measure()` throws / silently falls back on-thread. Centralize one shared text-appearance style for both the precompute step and the view; unit-test that params match.

### 6.2 The capture-pipeline freeze/ANR surface — engineered out

- **Everything off the UI thread:** MediaProjection service work runs on a dedicated HandlerThread; that Handler is passed to `createVirtualDisplay(..., handler)` and `ImageReader.setOnImageAvailableListener(listener, handler)` so callbacks never land on main.
- **Back-pressure (the classic ANR):** `ImageReader.newInstance(w,h,fmt, maxImages=2-3)`; `onImageAvailable` always `acquireLatestImage()` (drops stale) → copy pixels → `close()` in a **`finally`** block. Missing/late `close()` stalls SurfaceFlinger → ANR on `acquireLatestImage`. A watchdog logs any callback exceeding a few ms.
- **Throttle to ~2 fps** by timestamp-gating; even skipped frames are acquired+closed to avoid back-pressure. Biggest battery/thermal win.
- **Decoupled recognition:** a bounded **drop-oldest queue (capacity 1)** feeds the background recognition worker, so a slow (0.7–3s) Gemini round-trip drops frames and can never back up the buffer or block anything.

### 6.3 Crash-safety / lifecycle

- **MediaProjection state machine** enforces the strict Android 14+ order: `createScreenCaptureIntent()` → user consent → `startForeground(mediaProjection)` → `getMediaProjection()` → `registerCallback()` (mandatory before `createVirtualDisplay()` or it throws) → `createVirtualDisplay()`.
- **Typed exception handling** at each step: `SecurityException`, `IllegalStateException`, `MissingForegroundServiceTypeException` → graceful degrade, never crash.
- **Every `onStop()` cause is first-class** (status-bar stop chip, screen lock, another projection, process death, single-use-token expiry): release VirtualDisplay+Surface, mark inactive, prompt for **fresh consent** on resume (consent/token are single-use on 14+; no silent restart).
- **Black/low-variance frame guard** before recognition (FLAG_SECURE, transitions, wrong single-app share) → surface "can't read the game" instead of feeding garbage.
- **All network calls** are timeout-bounded, cancellable, with 429 exponential backoff and offline fallback. The deterministic deckstring tracker runs with **zero network** — it can never be stalled by the model.
- **Persistence** (Room + DataStore) so process death / documented session-limit cutoffs lose nothing.

### 6.4 Automated guardrails (from M1)
- **StrictMode** thread policy in debug flags main-thread parsing/I-O.
- **JankStats / FrameMetrics** assert no frame > ~200ms while a long message renders.
- **Spike-harness regression gate:** any `inter_ms > ~700ms` during a scripted long-Markdown stream **fails the build.**

---

## 7. Phased milestones

| Milestone | Goal | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **M0 — Harness reuse + baseline** | Adapt the existing `dev.lyai.deckview.spike` capture harness into `capture.spike`; reproduce the diagnosed freeze on a scripted long-Markdown message; wire the `inter_ms` gate. | Harness runs on target device, writes `frames.csv`/`cpu.csv`; a scripted long-Markdown render reproduces `inter_ms > 700ms` (baseline captured); regression gate script exists and reports pass/fail. |
| **M1 — Anti-freeze chat core** | Build the chat pipeline: off-thread SSE + Markdown parse, virtualized `LazyColumn`, throttled streaming, PrecomputedText, delimiter suppression. StrictMode + JankStats on. | Streaming a 2,000-word Markdown answer with bullets/code holds **all** `inter_ms < 700ms` and no frame > 200ms; StrictMode reports zero main-thread parse/IO; scrolling old long messages triggers zero re-parse (cache hit). |
| **M2 — Deterministic tracker** | Deckstring codec + HearthstoneJSON resolution + `GameStateStore`; tracker UI. Fully offline. | Pasting a valid deckstring yields correct 30-card list + counts; simulated "played" events decrement remaining correctly; works with airplane mode on; invalid/garbage deckstring degrades gracefully. |
| **M3 — Capture pipeline (no recognition)** | MediaProjection FGS + state machine + ImageReader drain + throttle + change-detector + phase classifier + drop-oldest queue. | Full Android 14 consent order works; every `onStop()` cause handled without crash; 30-min capture session leaks no Images (no ANR), CPU stays low, ~2fps; black-frame guard fires on a FLAG_SECURE test screen. |
| **M4 — Best-effort recognition** | Wire ML Kit OCR + deck-constrained Gemini vision behind the queue; abstain-on-low-confidence; pHash result cache; rate limiter arbitrating vision+chat budget. | On recorded gameplay, played-card events resolve to correct dbfIds at acceptable rate; low-confidence reads ABSTAIN (never corrupt state); offline/429 simply skips (tracker unaffected); < a few dozen cloud calls per simulated match. |
| **M5 — Grounded chat + persistence** | GAME STATE block assembly from DB facts; bounded rolling history; Room persistence; degraded/offline/rate-limited UI states. | Chat answers reference only current-game cards (no hallucinated cards vs DB); process kill mid-session restores chat + state; offline shows "assistant offline, tracking still active" and queues. |
| **M6 — Hardening & stability certification** | End-to-end load test (long chat message rendering *while* a board is recognized); thermal/battery soak; finalize guardrails as CI gates. | Worst-case concurrent load holds the freeze/jank budget; 1-hour ladder soak with zero crashes/ANRs; regression gate green in CI; StrictMode/JankStats clean. |
| **M7 (v2 candidates)** | Overlay HUD, selective high-res ROI, opponent recognition, more modes. | Deferred — each gated on an Ignacio go and its own stability re-certification. |

---

## 8. Risk register

| Risk | Sev | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| CV/vision on or near the UI/capture thread reintroduces multi-second freezes | **High** | Strict off-thread pipeline (HandlerThread + background coroutines), drop-oldest cap-1 queue, spike `inter_ms` CI gate; load-test long-chat-render *during* recognition (M6). |
| Missing/late `image.close()` → buffer stall → ANR | **High** | `acquireLatestImage()`+`close()` in `finally`, `maxImages` 2–3, per-callback watchdog log. |
| Android 14/15 single-use consent + FGS ordering → `SecurityException`/`IllegalStateException` crash | **High** | State machine encoding the exact order; `registerCallback` before `createVirtualDisplay`; every `onStop()` = re-consent; test on 14/15/16. |
| Gemini free-tier RPD caps volatile (cut 50–80% Dec-2025; ~250–500 RPD, ~10 RPM) → 429s make assistant feel broken | **High** | Cloud never on critical path; change-detector + phase gate + event-debounce keep calls to a handful/game; client rate limiter arbitrates shared vision+chat budget; 429 backoff; deterministic tracker independent of model. |
| Recognition accuracy capped by ~800×360 low-res + online-only latency; fanned hand unreadable | **Med** | Deckstring makes tracker authoritative regardless; recognize only large elements; deck-constrained candidate set; ABSTAIN on low confidence; selective high-res ROI designed-for (v2). |
| Privacy: free-tier sends screen-derived frames/state to Google (training + human review) | **Med** | Send only cropped card ROIs to vision + minimal structured state to chat (never raw full screenshots); PII-strip; escalate paid-tier/on-device to Ignacio (§10). |
| Card DB staleness (new sets ~3×/yr, nerfs, new art) | **Med** | HearthstoneJSON bundled as a versioned, updatable data drop; deckstring ground-truth resilient to art shifts. |
| Naive Compose Markdown re-parsing a growing string reproduces the exact bug | **Med** | Mandate `AndroidView(Markwon)` + PrecomputedText for bubble bodies; ban naive Compose Markdown in review. |
| Battery/thermal from continuous capture → throttling → its own jank | **Med** | ~2fps, reduced-res VirtualDisplay, frame-diff skip, pause when Hearthstone not foreground. |
| ToS/anti-cheat ambiguity of a screen-reading advisor | **Low** | Strictly observational, no input automation; flag to Ignacio for product/ToS call (§10). |

---

## 9. Cost & compliance

- **Default free API confirmed:** Gemini 2.5-flash serves **both** vision and chat, free tier. No paid APIs (no Imagen 4, no Google Places, no paid cloud vision). No on-device model to train/ship.
- **Per-call cost is trivially under the $0.10 rule:** an 800×360 frame ≈ ~500 input tokens (~$0.00015); `media_resolution=LOW` cuts it to ~64–72 tokens. The real budget constraint is **free-tier RPD**, not dollars — controlled by change-gating and event-debouncing to a handful of calls per game.
- **Nothing in v1 crosses the ≥$0.10 authorization threshold** as designed on free tier.
- **The one cost decision to flag (§10):** true privacy (no training / human review of screen-derived content) requires the **paid Gemini tier (≥$0.10, needs Ignacio authorization)** or an on-device model. v1 mitigates by sending only cropped ROIs + minimal structured state, never raw screenshots.
- ML Kit OCR, Room/DataStore, deckstring codec, HearthstoneJSON bundle: all free/offline.

---

## 10. Open decisions for Ignacio

1. **Privacy vs cost:** accept free-tier data terms (prompts/responses used for training, human review of screen-derived context), or authorize paid tier (≥$0.10) / commit to a future on-device model? Blocks the vision+chat privacy posture.
2. **Deckstring import as required onboarding?** It is the biggest single accuracy+stability win and makes the tracker authoritative offline. Confirm it can be a required (or strongly-guided) first step, vs demanding a fully "blind" screen-only mode (much weaker).
3. **Target device(s) + screen resolution / aspect ratio.** Determines the resolution/stability tradeoff dial and whether high-res ROI capture is needed sooner. Also fixes on-device benchmarking targets.
4. **Min/target SDK pin** (plan assumes min 26 / target 34). Android 14 vs 15 vs 16 materially change consent/FGS/single-app-share behavior.
5. **Opponent tracking scope for v1.** User deck is authoritative via deckstring; opponent is open-set (harder). Confirm opponent = best-effort annotation only in v1.
6. **Game modes in scope.** v1 assumes Standard/Wild constructed. Battlegrounds/Arena/Duels need separate ROI maps and recognition logic — v2.
7. **Overlay HUD in v1 or v2?** Plan defers the `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY` bubble to v2 (v1 = normal foreground app + import flow). Confirm.
8. **ToS/anti-cheat sign-off** on a screen-reading advisory app (strictly observational, no automation).
9. **The Android repo.** No DeckView source exists yet; this is build-from-scratch. Confirm repo location/creation so M0 can begin by adapting the `spike` harness.

PROJECT: DeckView — an Android app to be BUILT FROM SCRATCH (no existing source code exists). Product owner: Ignacio (LyAi Labs). Package namespace: dev.lyai.deckview.*

PRODUCT: A Hearthstone deck tracker with an integrated AI CHAT interface (assistant answers in Markdown).

CONFIRMED CORE INPUT MECHANISM (decided by product owner): real-time SCREEN CAPTURE via Android MediaProjection. Hearthstone runs on the SAME Android device; DeckView observes the game screen, recognizes cards / board / deck state via computer vision or AI, tracks the deck, and an AI chat comments and answers questions in Markdown.
WHY screen-capture (not log parsing): on Android you CANNOT read another app's files (sandbox), unlike PC trackers (Hearthstone Deck Tracker, Firestone) that parse Power.log. Screen capture + vision is the only viable on-device path.

ALREADY BUILT (prototype to reuse/learn from): dev.lyai.deckview.spike — a MediaProjection screen-capture harness. Captures 800x360 at ~33-60fps, logs per-frame proc_ms/inter_ms and process CPU, and dumps JPEG frames on jank (2 FPS "dataset" mode). It is effectively the prototype of the capture pipeline.

PERFORMANCE DIAGNOSIS (established with high confidence from real capture logs — bake these lessons into the plan):
- Per-frame processing is trivial (proc_ms ~2ms median). Not compute-bound.
- The app suffered multi-second UI FREEZES: inter-frame gaps up to 3.9s, costing 26-55% of wall-clock time in sessions where a LONG Markdown AI chat message was on screen.
- Capture-process CPU DROPS during freezes and an independent ~2s timer NEVER stalled -> the freeze is a BLOCKED render/UI thread waiting on something, NOT heavy compute and NOT OS suspension.
- Freezes correlated with rendering LONG Markdown chat messages, NOT with the capture/JPEG-dump machinery (the session that dumped the most frames was the SMOOTHEST).
- CONCLUSION: the #1 stability risk is MAIN-THREAD BLOCKING while rendering long Markdown chat messages. The architecture MUST parse/measure Markdown OFF the UI thread, virtualize the chat list, and stream/paginate incrementally.

HARD PRIORITY (product owner): STABILITY FIRST — zero crashes, smooth end-to-end (LyAi "PDS Gold Rule": no crashes in production, 99.99% uptime). Accuracy and features are secondary to never freezing/crashing.

LyAi ORGANIZATION CONSTRAINTS (must respect in every recommendation):
- Any action costing >= $0.10 requires explicit authorization from Ignacio.
- STRONGLY prefer FREE APIs: Gemini 2.5-flash (free) is the default for vision + chat. Avoid paid APIs (Imagen 4, Google Places, paid cloud vision) unless flagged as needing authorization.
- Privacy/on-device is a plus; screen contents may be sensitive.

=== DRAFT BUILD PLAN ===
# DeckView — Definitive Build Plan

**Version:** 1.0 · 2026-07-14 · **Package namespace:** `dev.lyai.deckview.*`
**Owner:** Ignacio (LyAi Labs) · **Mandate:** STABILITY FIRST (PDS Gold Rule — zero crashes, no freezes; accuracy/features secondary)
**Status:** Planning only. Propuesta-antes-de-aplicar. No build/deploy without explicit order.

---

## 1. Product & scope

**DeckView** is an on-device Android Hearthstone deck tracker with an integrated, grounded AI chat. Because Android's sandbox forbids reading another app's `Power.log` (the mechanism every PC tracker relies on), DeckView observes the game the only way it can on-device: it captures the screen via **MediaProjection**, recognizes discrete game events (card played, mulligan, board, turn) with best-effort cloud vision, and maintains an authoritative deck state that is seeded by the user **importing their deck as a deckstring**. A streaming, Markdown-rendering AI chat (Gemini 2.5-flash) — the product star — answers questions and comments on the current game, grounded on deterministic card facts so it cannot invent cards.

**The central bet:** the tracker is *correct and fully offline from the deckstring alone*; screen recognition is pure best-effort upside layered on top, never on the critical path. This is what lets v1 be freeze-proof and free.

### MVP (v1) — IN
- Deckstring import → authoritative 30-card deck, drawn/remaining counts, fully offline.
- MediaProjection capture service (foreground, off-thread) reusing the `spike` harness.
- On-device change-detector (luma-diff / pHash) + Tier-0 phase classifier gating.
- Best-effort Gemini 2.5-flash vision on discrete, debounced events (card played / mulligan), constrained to the imported deck's ~30 dbfIds.
- Deterministic `GameStateStore` (single source of truth) = deckstring − observed played/drawn.
- Compose tracker UI (deck list, counts, current turn/mana if read).
- Grounded, streaming, Markdown AI chat with off-thread parse + virtualized list (the anti-freeze core).
- Room persistence of chat + session; graceful offline/rate-limited/degraded states.
- Guardrails: StrictMode, JankStats, spike-harness `inter_ms` regression gate.

### Later (v2+) — explicitly NOT in v1
- `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY` HUD bubble over Hearthstone (v1 is a normal foreground app + import flow).
- Opponent open-set card recognition (v1 tracks the *user's* deck authoritatively; opponent = best-effort only).
- On-device ML classifier / bundled pHash reference DB per expansion (cloud vision absorbs open-set in v1).
- Selective high-resolution ROI capture for in-hand card art (designed-for, deferred).
- Battlegrounds / Arena / Duels mode-specific ROI maps (v1 = Standard/Wild constructed only).
- Paid-tier / on-device LLM for privacy (an Ignacio cost decision, §10).
- Input automation of any kind (strictly observational — ToS posture).

Cloud-first best-effort recognition, deterministic offline tracker, two independently engineered-out freeze surfaces (capture pipeline and chat rendering).

## 3. Tech stack

| Layer | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Language | **Kotlin** | Coroutines/Flow are the backbone of the off-thread stability model. |
| Min/Target SDK | **min 26, target 34** (pin, see §10) | Android 14 FGS/consent rules are the constraint we design to. |
| App/UI shell | **Jetpack Compose** | Lean, modern for tracker/onboarding/chat list. |
| Chat bubble body | **`AndroidView(Markwon)` + PrecomputedText** | Proven anti-freeze path; avoids naive Compose Markdown that re-parses a growing string (reproduces the diagnosed bug). |
| Chat list | **`LazyColumn`, stable keys, `@Immutable` models** | Virtualized — streaming answer is one item, never a monolith. |
| Async | **Coroutines + Flow** (IO=network/SSE, Default=parsing) | Structured concurrency, cancellation, `sample()/conflate()` throttling, drop-oldest backpressure. |
| DI | **Hilt** | Wires capture service, `LlmClient`, repos, dispatchers; keeps LLM swappable. |
| Networking | **OkHttp, raw SSE** (no Retrofit/SDK) | Lean footprint; POST `streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`. |
| LLM abstraction | **`interface LlmClient { fun streamChat(...): Flow<Delta> }`** | Isolates Gemini; Claude / on-device swap later without touching UI/grounding. |
| Chat model | **Gemini 2.5-flash (free tier)** via `GeminiClient`; `OfflineClient` fallback | Free default per LyAi rules; canned degraded response offline. |
| Capture | **MediaProjection + VirtualDisplay + ImageReader** in a `mediaProjection` FGS on a HandlerThread | Raw frames for vision (not MediaCodec); off-thread from day one. |
| Change-detector | **On-device luma-diff / 64-bit pHash** | Sub-ms gate — the biggest cost/battery/RPD lever. |
| Recognition (identify) | **Gemini 2.5-flash vision**, background, best-effort, deck-constrained | No ML model to train / no per-patch pHash DB — the lean bet. |
| OCR | **Google ML Kit Text Recognition v2** (offline, free) | Card names + digits; disambiguator/tie-breaker; not Tesseract. |
| Card data | **Bundled HearthstoneJSON `cards.collectible.json`** + ported deckstring codec | Offline dbfId→facts; ground-truth deck import. |
| Persistence | **Room** (chat/session/cache) + **DataStore** (settings, API key, active deckstring) | Survives process death / session cutoffs. |
| Markdown | **Markwon 4.6.x + `PrecomputedTextSetterCompat`** on a background Executor | Parses spans off main thread; UI blocks only at `measure()`. |
| Guardrails | **StrictMode (debug) + JankStats/FrameMetrics + spike `inter_ms` gate** | Turns the zero-freeze mandate into an automated build check. |

## 5. Hearthstone data

**Card DB — HearthstoneJSON.** Bundle `cards.collectible.json` (versioned per patch) as an app asset for offline, deterministic resolution. Each card carries a string `cardId` (e.g. `EX1_001`) and a numeric **`dbfId`** (e.g. Leeroy = 559) plus name/cost/type/text/mechanics. `dbfId` is the join key across everything. Reference-art render/tile API (256×/512×) is used *only* offline if a pHash reference DB is ever added in v2 — **not needed for v1** (cloud vision absorbs recognition).

**Deckstring format.** A deck code is base64 of a varint stream keyed on `dbfId` (format version, then 1×/2×/n× card blocks). Port HearthSim's `hearthstone-deckstrings` codec into `dev.lyai.deckview.deckstring`. On import: decode → list of `(dbfId, count)` → resolve each vs the bundled DB → seed `GameStateStore` with an authoritative 30-card deck.

**Recognition → card IDs.** The deck's hidden contents are never observable; DeckView tracks *events* (card drawn/played), exactly like any tracker. Pipeline: change-detector + phase classifier decide a discrete event occurred → a cropped/downscaled frame goes to ML Kit OCR (name/digits) and/or Gemini vision, **constrained to the imported deck's ~30 dbfIds + already-seen opponent cards** (the single biggest accuracy+latency+cost lever). The recognizer returns a `dbfId` (or ABSTAINS on low confidence). The reducer subtracts it from remaining counts. Priority targets are large, unambiguous elements — the played-card center animation, mulligan cards, board minions — never the small fanned hand.

---

## 6. Stability plan (PRIORITY)

Two independent freeze surfaces, both engineered out from day one, plus structural crash-safety.

### 6.1 The diagnosed Markdown main-thread freeze (up to 3.9s) — killed by four rules

1. **Off-thread parsing, always.** SSE stream handled on `Dispatchers.IO`; CommonMark→Spanned on `Dispatchers.Default` via Markwon built once with `textSetter(PrecomputedTextSetterCompat.create(backgroundExecutor))`. The UI thread receives an already-parsed Spanned/`PrecomputedText` and only blocks at `measure()`. All CommonMark parsing runs inside a coroutine — the main thread never parses.
2. **Virtualized chat list.** `LazyColumn` with `key = message.id` and `@Immutable` message models. The in-progress answer is **one** streaming item; completed answers are individual items. A monolithic view holding the whole answer is never inflated. Parsing is kept out of composition entirely.
3. **Incremental, throttled streaming.** Tokens append plain text to the single streaming bubble, coalesced to **≤1 UI update per frame** (`Flow.sample(~33ms)` / `conflate()`). Never `setText` per token. On completion the finished message is parsed off-thread, cached in an `LruCache` (key = id + content hash), and rendered via `AndroidView(Markwon)` + `PrecomputedText`. Re-scroll/rebind reuses the cached Spanned — never re-parses.
4. **Delimiter suppression while streaming.** A lightweight single-pass `MarkdownBuffer` hides trailing unclosed `**`, `*`, `` ` ``, ` ``` ` until closed (prevents flicker); on completion the full unmodified text is rendered so intentional lone markers survive.

**PrecomputedText correctness:** set `textSize/typeface/textDir/breakStrategy` on the target `TextView` *before* building `Params`, or `measure()` throws / silently falls back on-thread. Centralize one shared text-appearance style for both the precompute step and the view; unit-test that params match.

### 6.2 The capture-pipeline freeze/ANR surface — engineered out

- **Everything off the UI thread:** MediaProjection service work runs on a dedicated HandlerThread; that Handler is passed to `createVirtualDisplay(..., handler)` and `ImageReader.setOnImageAvailableListener(listener, handler)` so callbacks never land on main.
- **Back-pressure (the classic ANR):** `ImageReader.newInstance(w,h,fmt, maxImages=2-3)`; `onImageAvailable` always `acquireLatestImage()` (drops stale) → copy pixels → `close()` in a **`finally`** block. Missing/late `close()` stalls SurfaceFlinger → ANR on `acquireLatestImage`. A watchdog logs any callback exceeding a few ms.
- **Throttle to ~2 fps** by timestamp-gating; even skipped frames are acquired+closed to avoid back-pressure. Biggest battery/thermal win.
- **Decoupled recognition:** a bounded **drop-oldest queue (capacity 1)** feeds the background recognition worker, so a slow (0.7–3s) Gemini round-trip drops frames and can never back up the buffer or block anything.

### 6.3 Crash-safety / lifecycle

- **MediaProjection state machine** enforces the strict Android 14+ order: `createScreenCaptureIntent()` → user consent → `startForeground(mediaProjection)` → `getMediaProjection()` → `registerCallback()` (mandatory before `createVirtualDisplay()` or it throws) → `createVirtualDisplay()`.
- **Typed exception handling** at each step: `SecurityException`, `IllegalStateException`, `MissingForegroundServiceTypeException` → graceful degrade, never crash.
- **Every `onStop()` cause is first-class** (status-bar stop chip, screen lock, another projection, process death, single-use-token expiry): release VirtualDisplay+Surface, mark inactive, prompt for **fresh consent** on resume (consent/token are single-use on 14+; no silent restart).
- **Black/low-variance frame guard** before recognition (FLAG_SECURE, transitions, wrong single-app share) → surface "can't read the game" instead of feeding garbage.
- **All network calls** are timeout-bounded, cancellable, with 429 exponential backoff and offline fallback. The deterministic deckstring tracker runs with **zero network** — it can never be stalled by the model.
- **Persistence** (Room + DataStore) so process death / documented session-limit cutoffs lose nothing.

### 6.4 Automated guardrails (from M1)
- **StrictMode** thread policy in debug flags main-thread parsing/I-O.
- **JankStats / FrameMetrics** assert no frame > ~200ms while a long message renders.
- **Spike-harness regression gate:** any `inter_ms > ~700ms` during a scripted long-Markdown stream **fails the build.**

---

## 7. Phased milestones

| Milestone | Goal | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **M0 — Harness reuse + baseline** | Adapt the existing `dev.lyai.deckview.spike` capture harness into `capture.spike`; reproduce the diagnosed freeze on a scripted long-Markdown message; wire the `inter_ms` gate. | Harness runs on target device, writes `frames.csv`/`cpu.csv`; a scripted long-Markdown render reproduces `inter_ms > 700ms` (baseline captured); regression gate script exists and reports pass/fail. |
| **M1 — Anti-freeze chat core** | Build the chat pipeline: off-thread SSE + Markdown parse, virtualized `LazyColumn`, throttled streaming, PrecomputedText, delimiter suppression. StrictMode + JankStats on. | Streaming a 2,000-word Markdown answer with bullets/code holds **all** `inter_ms < 700ms` and no frame > 200ms; StrictMode reports zero main-thread parse/IO; scrolling old long messages triggers zero re-parse (cache hit). |
| **M2 — Deterministic tracker** | Deckstring codec + HearthstoneJSON resolution + `GameStateStore`; tracker UI. Fully offline. | Pasting a valid deckstring yields correct 30-card list + counts; simulated "played" events decrement remaining correctly; works with airplane mode on; invalid/garbage deckstring degrades gracefully. |
| **M3 — Capture pipeline (no recognition)** | MediaProjection FGS + state machine + ImageReader drain + throttle + change-detector + phase classifier + drop-oldest queue. | Full Android 14 consent order works; every `onStop()` cause handled without crash; 30-min capture session leaks no Images (no ANR), CPU stays low, ~2fps; black-frame guard fires on a FLAG_SECURE test screen. |
| **M4 — Best-effort recognition** | Wire ML Kit OCR + deck-constrained Gemini vision behind the queue; abstain-on-low-confidence; pHash result cache; rate limiter arbitrating vision+chat budget. | On recorded gameplay, played-card events resolve to correct dbfIds at acceptable rate; low-confidence reads ABSTAIN (never corrupt state); offline/429 simply skips (tracker unaffected); < a few dozen cloud calls per simulated match. |
| **M5 — Grounded chat + persistence** | GAME STATE block assembly from DB facts; bounded rolling history; Room persistence; degraded/offline/rate-limited UI states. | Chat answers reference only current-game cards (no hallucinated cards vs DB); process kill mid-session restores chat + state; offline shows "assistant offline, tracking still active" and queues. |
| **M6 — Hardening & stability certification** | End-to-end load test (long chat message rendering *while* a board is recognized); thermal/battery soak; finalize guardrails as CI gates. | Worst-case concurrent load holds the freeze/jank budget; 1-hour ladder soak with zero crashes/ANRs; regression gate green in CI; StrictMode/JankStats clean. |
| **M7 (v2 candidates)** | Overlay HUD, selective high-res ROI, opponent recognition, more modes. | Deferred — each gated on an Ignacio go and its own stability re-certification. |

## 8. Risk register

| Risk | Sev | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| CV/vision on or near the UI/capture thread reintroduces multi-second freezes | **High** | Strict off-thread pipeline (HandlerThread + background coroutines), drop-oldest cap-1 queue, spike `inter_ms` CI gate; load-test long-chat-render *during* recognition (M6). |
| Missing/late `image.close()` → buffer stall → ANR | **High** | `acquireLatestImage()`+`close()` in `finally`, `maxImages` 2–3, per-callback watchdog log. |
| Android 14/15 single-use consent + FGS ordering → `SecurityException`/`IllegalStateException` crash | **High** | State machine encoding the exact order; `registerCallback` before `createVirtualDisplay`; every `onStop()` = re-consent; test on 14/15/16. |
| Gemini free-tier RPD caps volatile (cut 50–80% Dec-2025; ~250–500 RPD, ~10 RPM) → 429s make assistant feel broken | **High** | Cloud never on critical path; change-detector + phase gate + event-debounce keep calls to a handful/game; client rate limiter arbitrates shared vision+chat budget; 429 backoff; deterministic tracker independent of model. |
| Recognition accuracy capped by ~800×360 low-res + online-only latency; fanned hand unreadable | **Med** | Deckstring makes tracker authoritative regardless; recognize only large elements; deck-constrained candidate set; ABSTAIN on low confidence; selective high-res ROI designed-for (v2). |
| Privacy: free-tier sends screen-derived frames/state to Google (training + human review) | **Med** | Send only cropped card ROIs to vision + minimal structured state to chat (never raw full screenshots); PII-strip; escalate paid-tier/on-device to Ignacio (§10). |
| Card DB staleness (new sets ~3×/yr, nerfs, new art) | **Med** | HearthstoneJSON bundled as a versioned, updatable data drop; deckstring ground-truth resilient to art shifts. |
| Naive Compose Markdown re-parsing a growing string reproduces the exact bug | **Med** | Mandate `AndroidView(Markwon)` + PrecomputedText for bubble bodies; ban naive Compose Markdown in review. |
| Battery/thermal from continuous capture → throttling → its own jank | **Med** | ~2fps, reduced-res VirtualDisplay, frame-diff skip, pause when Hearthstone not foreground. |
| ToS/anti-cheat ambiguity of a screen-reading advisor | **Low** | Strictly observational, no input automation; flag to Ignacio for product/ToS call (§10). |

---

## 9. Cost & compliance

- **Default free API confirmed:** Gemini 2.5-flash serves **both** vision and chat, free tier. No paid APIs (no Imagen 4, no Google Places, no paid cloud vision). No on-device model to train/ship.
- **Per-call cost is trivially under the $0.10 rule:** an 800×360 frame ≈ ~500 input tokens (~$0.00015); `media_resolution=LOW` cuts it to ~64–72 tokens. The real budget constraint is **free-tier RPD**, not dollars — controlled by change-gating and event-debouncing to a handful of calls per game.
- **Nothing in v1 crosses the ≥$0.10 authorization threshold** as designed on free tier.
- **The one cost decision to flag (§10):** true privacy (no training / human review of screen-derived content) requires the **paid Gemini tier (≥$0.10, needs Ignacio authorization)** or an on-device model. v1 mitigates by sending only cropped ROIs + minimal structured state, never raw screenshots.
- ML Kit OCR, Room/DataStore, deckstring codec, HearthstoneJSON bundle: all free/offline.

- Per-frame processing is trivial (proc_ms ~2ms median). Not compute-bound.
- The app suffered multi-second UI FREEZES: inter-frame gaps up to 3.9s, costing 26-55% of wall-clock time in sessions where a LONG Markdown AI chat message was on screen.
- Capture-process CPU DROPS during freezes and an independent ~2s timer NEVER stalled -> the freeze is a BLOCKED render/UI thread waiting on something, NOT heavy compute and NOT OS suspension.
- Freezes correlated with rendering LONG Markdown chat messages, NOT with the capture/JPEG-dump machinery (the session that dumped the most frames was the SMOOTHEST).
- CONCLUSION: the #1 stability risk is MAIN-THREAD BLOCKING while rendering long Markdown chat messages. The architecture MUST parse/measure Markdown OFF the UI thread, virtualize the chat list, and stream/paginate incrementally.

=== DRAFT BUILD PLAN ===
# DeckView — Definitive Build Plan

**Version:** 1.0 · 2026-07-14 · **Package namespace:** `dev.lyai.deckview.*`
**Owner:** Ignacio (LyAi Labs) · **Mandate:** STABILITY FIRST (PDS Gold Rule — zero crashes, no freezes; accuracy/features secondary)
**Status:** Planning only. Propuesta-antes-de-aplicar. No build/deploy without explicit order.

---

## 1. Product & scope

**DeckView** is an on-device Android Hearthstone deck tracker with an integrated, grounded AI chat. Because Android's sandbox forbids reading another app's `Power.log` (the mechanism every PC tracker relies on), DeckView observes the game the only way it can on-device: it captures the screen via **MediaProjection**, recognizes discrete game events (card played, mulligan, board, turn) with best-effort cloud vision, and maintains an authoritative deck state that is seeded by the user **importing their deck as a deckstring**. A streaming, Markdown-rendering AI chat (Gemini 2.5-flash) — the product star — answers questions and comments on the current game, grounded on deterministic card facts so it cannot invent cards.

**The central bet:** the tracker is *correct and fully offline from the deckstring alone*; screen recognition is pure best-effort upside layered on top, never on the critical path. This is what lets v1 be freeze-proof and free.

### MVP (v1) — IN
- Deckstring import → authoritative 30-card deck, drawn/remaining counts, fully offline.
- MediaProjection capture service (foreground, off-thread) reusing the `spike` harness.
- On-device change-detector (luma-diff / pHash) + Tier-0 phase classifier gating.
- Best-effort Gemini 2.5-flash vision on discrete, debounced events (card played / mulligan), constrained to the imported deck's ~30 dbfIds.
- Deterministic `GameStateStore` (single source of truth) = deckstring − observed played/drawn.
- Compose tracker UI (deck list, counts, current turn/mana if read).
- Grounded, streaming, Markdown AI chat with off-thread parse + virtualized list (the anti-freeze core).
- Room persistence of chat + session; graceful offline/rate-limited/degraded states.
- Guardrails: StrictMode, JankStats, spike-harness `inter_ms` regression gate.

### Later (v2+) — explicitly NOT in v1
- `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY` HUD bubble over Hearthstone (v1 is a normal foreground app + import flow).
- Opponent open-set card recognition (v1 tracks the *user's* deck authoritatively; opponent = best-effort only).
- On-device ML classifier / bundled pHash reference DB per expansion (cloud vision absorbs open-set in v1).
- Selective high-resolution ROI capture for in-hand card art (designed-for, deferred).
- Battlegrounds / Arena / Duels mode-specific ROI maps (v1 = Standard/Wild constructed only).
- Paid-tier / on-device LLM for privacy (an Ignacio cost decision, §10).
- Input automation of any kind (strictly observational — ToS posture).

Cloud-first best-effort recognition, deterministic offline tracker, two independently engineered-out freeze surfaces (capture pipeline and chat rendering).

## 3. Tech stack

| Layer | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Language | **Kotlin** | Coroutines/Flow are the backbone of the off-thread stability model. |
| Min/Target SDK | **min 26, target 34** (pin, see §10) | Android 14 FGS/consent rules are the constraint we design to. |
| App/UI shell | **Jetpack Compose** | Lean, modern for tracker/onboarding/chat list. |
| Chat bubble body | **`AndroidView(Markwon)` + PrecomputedText** | Proven anti-freeze path; avoids naive Compose Markdown that re-parses a growing string (reproduces the diagnosed bug). |
| Chat list | **`LazyColumn`, stable keys, `@Immutable` models** | Virtualized — streaming answer is one item, never a monolith. |
| Async | **Coroutines + Flow** (IO=network/SSE, Default=parsing) | Structured concurrency, cancellation, `sample()/conflate()` throttling, drop-oldest backpressure. |
| DI | **Hilt** | Wires capture service, `LlmClient`, repos, dispatchers; keeps LLM swappable. |
| Networking | **OkHttp, raw SSE** (no Retrofit/SDK) | Lean footprint; POST `streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`. |
| LLM abstraction | **`interface LlmClient { fun streamChat(...): Flow<Delta> }`** | Isolates Gemini; Claude / on-device swap later without touching UI/grounding. |
| Chat model | **Gemini 2.5-flash (free tier)** via `GeminiClient`; `OfflineClient` fallback | Free default per LyAi rules; canned degraded response offline. |
| Capture | **MediaProjection + VirtualDisplay + ImageReader** in a `mediaProjection` FGS on a HandlerThread | Raw frames for vision (not MediaCodec); off-thread from day one. |
| Change-detector | **On-device luma-diff / 64-bit pHash** | Sub-ms gate — the biggest cost/battery/RPD lever. |
| Recognition (identify) | **Gemini 2.5-flash vision**, background, best-effort, deck-constrained | No ML model to train / no per-patch pHash DB — the lean bet. |
| OCR | **Google ML Kit Text Recognition v2** (offline, free) | Card names + digits; disambiguator/tie-breaker; not Tesseract. |
| Card data | **Bundled HearthstoneJSON `cards.collectible.json`** + ported deckstring codec | Offline dbfId→facts; ground-truth deck import. |
| Persistence | **Room** (chat/session/cache) + **DataStore** (settings, API key, active deckstring) | Survives process death / session cutoffs. |
| Markdown | **Markwon 4.6.x + `PrecomputedTextSetterCompat`** on a background Executor | Parses spans off main thread; UI blocks only at `measure()`. |
| Guardrails | **StrictMode (debug) + JankStats/FrameMetrics + spike `inter_ms` gate** | Turns the zero-freeze mandate into an automated build check. |

## 5. Hearthstone data

**Card DB — HearthstoneJSON.** Bundle `cards.collectible.json` (versioned per patch) as an app asset for offline, deterministic resolution. Each card carries a string `cardId` (e.g. `EX1_001`) and a numeric **`dbfId`** (e.g. Leeroy = 559) plus name/cost/type/text/mechanics. `dbfId` is the join key across everything. Reference-art render/tile API (256×/512×) is used *only* offline if a pHash reference DB is ever added in v2 — **not needed for v1** (cloud vision absorbs recognition).

**Deckstring format.** A deck code is base64 of a varint stream keyed on `dbfId` (format version, then 1×/2×/n× card blocks). Port HearthSim's `hearthstone-deckstrings` codec into `dev.lyai.deckview.deckstring`. On import: decode → list of `(dbfId, count)` → resolve each vs the bundled DB → seed `GameStateStore` with an authoritative 30-card deck.

**Recognition → card IDs.** The deck's hidden contents are never observable; DeckView tracks *events* (card drawn/played), exactly like any tracker. Pipeline: change-detector + phase classifier decide a discrete event occurred → a cropped/downscaled frame goes to ML Kit OCR (name/digits) and/or Gemini vision, **constrained to the imported deck's ~30 dbfIds + already-seen opponent cards** (the single biggest accuracy+latency+cost lever). The recognizer returns a `dbfId` (or ABSTAINS on low confidence). The reducer subtracts it from remaining counts. Priority targets are large, unambiguous elements — the played-card center animation, mulligan cards, board minions — never the small fanned hand.

---

## 6. Stability plan (PRIORITY)

Two independent freeze surfaces, both engineered out from day one, plus structural crash-safety.

### 6.1 The diagnosed Markdown main-thread freeze (up to 3.9s) — killed by four rules

1. **Off-thread parsing, always.** SSE stream handled on `Dispatchers.IO`; CommonMark→Spanned on `Dispatchers.Default` via Markwon built once with `textSetter(PrecomputedTextSetterCompat.create(backgroundExecutor))`. The UI thread receives an already-parsed Spanned/`PrecomputedText` and only blocks at `measure()`. All CommonMark parsing runs inside a coroutine — the main thread never parses.
2. **Virtualized chat list.** `LazyColumn` with `key = message.id` and `@Immutable` message models. The in-progress answer is **one** streaming item; completed answers are individual items. A monolithic view holding the whole answer is never inflated. Parsing is kept out of composition entirely.
3. **Incremental, throttled streaming.** Tokens append plain text to the single streaming bubble, coalesced to **≤1 UI update per frame** (`Flow.sample(~33ms)` / `conflate()`). Never `setText` per token. On completion the finished message is parsed off-thread, cached in an `LruCache` (key = id + content hash), and rendered via `AndroidView(Markwon)` + `PrecomputedText`. Re-scroll/rebind reuses the cached Spanned — never re-parses.
4. **Delimiter suppression while streaming.** A lightweight single-pass `MarkdownBuffer` hides trailing unclosed `**`, `*`, `` ` ``, ` ``` ` until closed (prevents flicker); on completion the full unmodified text is rendered so intentional lone markers survive.

**PrecomputedText correctness:** set `textSize/typeface/textDir/breakStrategy` on the target `TextView` *before* building `Params`, or `measure()` throws / silently falls back on-thread. Centralize one shared text-appearance style for both the precompute step and the view; unit-test that params match.

### 6.2 The capture-pipeline freeze/ANR surface — engineered out

- **Everything off the UI thread:** MediaProjection service work runs on a dedicated HandlerThread; that Handler is passed to `createVirtualDisplay(..., handler)` and `ImageReader.setOnImageAvailableListener(listener, handler)` so callbacks never land on main.
- **Back-pressure (the classic ANR):** `ImageReader.newInstance(w,h,fmt, maxImages=2-3)`; `onImageAvailable` always `acquireLatestImage()` (drops stale) → copy pixels → `close()` in a **`finally`** block. Missing/late `close()` stalls SurfaceFlinger → ANR on `acquireLatestImage`. A watchdog logs any callback exceeding a few ms.
- **Throttle to ~2 fps** by timestamp-gating; even skipped frames are acquired+closed to avoid back-pressure. Biggest battery/thermal win.
- **Decoupled recognition:** a bounded **drop-oldest queue (capacity 1)** feeds the background recognition worker, so a slow (0.7–3s) Gemini round-trip drops frames and can never back up the buffer or block anything.

### 6.3 Crash-safety / lifecycle

- **MediaProjection state machine** enforces the strict Android 14+ order: `createScreenCaptureIntent()` → user consent → `startForeground(mediaProjection)` → `getMediaProjection()` → `registerCallback()` (mandatory before `createVirtualDisplay()` or it throws) → `createVirtualDisplay()`.
- **Typed exception handling** at each step: `SecurityException`, `IllegalStateException`, `MissingForegroundServiceTypeException` → graceful degrade, never crash.
- **Every `onStop()` cause is first-class** (status-bar stop chip, screen lock, another projection, process death, single-use-token expiry): release VirtualDisplay+Surface, mark inactive, prompt for **fresh consent** on resume (consent/token are single-use on 14+; no silent restart).
- **Black/low-variance frame guard** before recognition (FLAG_SECURE, transitions, wrong single-app share) → surface "can't read the game" instead of feeding garbage.
- **All network calls** are timeout-bounded, cancellable, with 429 exponential backoff and offline fallback. The deterministic deckstring tracker runs with **zero network** — it can never be stalled by the model.
- **Persistence** (Room + DataStore) so process death / documented session-limit cutoffs lose nothing.

### 6.4 Automated guardrails (from M1)
- **StrictMode** thread policy in debug flags main-thread parsing/I-O.
- **JankStats / FrameMetrics** assert no frame > ~200ms while a long message renders.
- **Spike-harness regression gate:** any `inter_ms > ~700ms` during a scripted long-Markdown stream **fails the build.**

---

## 7. Phased milestones

| Milestone | Goal | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **M0 — Harness reuse + baseline** | Adapt the existing `dev.lyai.deckview.spike` capture harness into `capture.spike`; reproduce the diagnosed freeze on a scripted long-Markdown message; wire the `inter_ms` gate. | Harness runs on target device, writes `frames.csv`/`cpu.csv`; a scripted long-Markdown render reproduces `inter_ms > 700ms` (baseline captured); regression gate script exists and reports pass/fail. |
| **M1 — Anti-freeze chat core** | Build the chat pipeline: off-thread SSE + Markdown parse, virtualized `LazyColumn`, throttled streaming, PrecomputedText, delimiter suppression. StrictMode + JankStats on. | Streaming a 2,000-word Markdown answer with bullets/code holds **all** `inter_ms < 700ms` and no frame > 200ms; StrictMode reports zero main-thread parse/IO; scrolling old long messages triggers zero re-parse (cache hit). |
| **M2 — Deterministic tracker** | Deckstring codec + HearthstoneJSON resolution + `GameStateStore`; tracker UI. Fully offline. | Pasting a valid deckstring yields correct 30-card list + counts; simulated "played" events decrement remaining correctly; works with airplane mode on; invalid/garbage deckstring degrades gracefully. |
| **M3 — Capture pipeline (no recognition)** | MediaProjection FGS + state machine + ImageReader drain + throttle + change-detector + phase classifier + drop-oldest queue. | Full Android 14 consent order works; every `onStop()` cause handled without crash; 30-min capture session leaks no Images (no ANR), CPU stays low, ~2fps; black-frame guard fires on a FLAG_SECURE test screen. |
| **M4 — Best-effort recognition** | Wire ML Kit OCR + deck-constrained Gemini vision behind the queue; abstain-on-low-confidence; pHash result cache; rate limiter arbitrating vision+chat budget. | On recorded gameplay, played-card events resolve to correct dbfIds at acceptable rate; low-confidence reads ABSTAIN (never corrupt state); offline/429 simply skips (tracker unaffected); < a few dozen cloud calls per simulated match. |
| **M5 — Grounded chat + persistence** | GAME STATE block assembly from DB facts; bounded rolling history; Room persistence; degraded/offline/rate-limited UI states. | Chat answers reference only current-game cards (no hallucinated cards vs DB); process kill mid-session restores chat + state; offline shows "assistant offline, tracking still active" and queues. |
| **M6 — Hardening & stability certification** | End-to-end load test (long chat message rendering *while* a board is recognized); thermal/battery soak; finalize guardrails as CI gates. | Worst-case concurrent load holds the freeze/jank budget; 1-hour ladder soak with zero crashes/ANRs; regression gate green in CI; StrictMode/JankStats clean. |
| **M7 (v2 candidates)** | Overlay HUD, selective high-res ROI, opponent recognition, more modes. | Deferred — each gated on an Ignacio go and its own stability re-certification. |

---

## 8. Risk register

| Risk | Sev | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| CV/vision on or near the UI/capture thread reintroduces multi-second freezes | **High** | Strict off-thread pipeline (HandlerThread + background coroutines), drop-oldest cap-1 queue, spike `inter_ms` CI gate; load-test long-chat-render *during* recognition (M6). |
| Missing/late `image.close()` → buffer stall → ANR | **High** | `acquireLatestImage()`+`close()` in `finally`, `maxImages` 2–3, per-callback watchdog log. |
| Android 14/15 single-use consent + FGS ordering → `SecurityException`/`IllegalStateException` crash | **High** | State machine encoding the exact order; `registerCallback` before `createVirtualDisplay`; every `onStop()` = re-consent; test on 14/15/16. |
| Gemini free-tier RPD caps volatile (cut 50–80% Dec-2025; ~250–500 RPD, ~10 RPM) → 429s make assistant feel broken | **High** | Cloud never on critical path; change-detector + phase gate + event-debounce keep calls to a handful/game; client rate limiter arbitrates shared vision+chat budget; 429 backoff; deterministic tracker independent of model. |
| Recognition accuracy capped by ~800×360 low-res + online-only latency; fanned hand unreadable | **Med** | Deckstring makes tracker authoritative regardless; recognize only large elements; deck-constrained candidate set; ABSTAIN on low confidence; selective high-res ROI designed-for (v2). |
| Privacy: free-tier sends screen-derived frames/state to Google (training + human review) | **Med** | Send only cropped card ROIs to vision + minimal structured state to chat (never raw full screenshots); PII-strip; escalate paid-tier/on-device to Ignacio (§10). |
| Card DB staleness (new sets ~3×/yr, nerfs, new art) | **Med** | HearthstoneJSON bundled as a versioned, updatable data drop; deckstring ground-truth resilient to art shifts. |
| Naive Compose Markdown re-parsing a growing string reproduces the exact bug | **Med** | Mandate `AndroidView(Markwon)` + PrecomputedText for bubble bodies; ban naive Compose Markdown in review. |
| Battery/thermal from continuous capture → throttling → its own jank | **Med** | ~2fps, reduced-res VirtualDisplay, frame-diff skip, pause when Hearthstone not foreground. |
| ToS/anti-cheat ambiguity of a screen-reading advisor | **Low** | Strictly observational, no input automation; flag to Ignacio for product/ToS call (§10). |

---

## 9. Cost & compliance

- **Default free API confirmed:** Gemini 2.5-flash serves **both** vision and chat, free tier. No paid APIs (no Imagen 4, no Google Places, no paid cloud vision). No on-device model to train/ship.
- **Per-call cost is trivially under the $0.10 rule:** an 800×360 frame ≈ ~500 input tokens (~$0.00015); `media_resolution=LOW` cuts it to ~64–72 tokens. The real budget constraint is **free-tier RPD**, not dollars — controlled by change-gating and event-debouncing to a handful of calls per game.
- **Nothing in v1 crosses the ≥$0.10 authorization threshold** as designed on free tier.
- **The one cost decision to flag (§10):** true privacy (no training / human review of screen-derived content) requires the **paid Gemini tier (≥$0.10, needs Ignacio authorization)** or an on-device model. v1 mitigates by sending only cropped ROIs + minimal structured state, never raw screenshots.
- ML Kit OCR, Room/DataStore, deckstring codec, HearthstoneJSON bundle: all free/offline.

---

## 10. Open decisions for Ignacio

1. **Privacy vs cost:** accept free-tier data terms (prompts/responses used for training, human review of screen-derived context), or authorize paid tier (≥$0.10) / commit to a future on-device model? Blocks the vision+chat privacy posture.
2. **Deckstring import as required onboarding?** It is the biggest single accuracy+stability win and makes the tracker authoritative offline. Confirm it can be a required (or strongly-guided) first step, vs demanding a fully "blind" screen-only mode (much weaker).
3. **Target device(s) + screen resolution / aspect ratio.** Determines the resolution/stability tradeoff dial and whether high-res ROI capture is needed sooner. Also fixes on-device benchmarking targets.
4. **Min/target SDK pin** (plan assumes min 26 / target 34). Android 14 vs 15 vs 16 materially change consent/FGS/single-app-share behavior.
5. **Opponent tracking scope for v1.** User deck is authoritative via deckstring; opponent is open-set (harder). Confirm opponent = best-effort annotation only in v1.
6. **Game modes in scope.** v1 assumes Standard/Wild constructed. Battlegrounds/Arena/Duels need separate ROI maps and recognition logic — v2.
7. **Overlay HUD in v1 or v2?** Plan defers the `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY` bubble to v2 (v1 = normal foreground app + import flow). Confirm.
8. **ToS/anti-cheat sign-off** on a screen-reading advisory app (strictly observational, no automation).
9. **The Android repo.** No DeckView source exists yet; this is build-from-scratch. Confirm repo location/creation so M0 can begin by adapting the `spike` harness.

*Prepared as planning only. No build or deploy will occur without an explicit order from Ignacio.*

=== CRITIC GAPS TO CLOSE ===
Gaps: OVERLAY IS NOT A v2 NICE-TO-HAVE — IT IS REQUIRED FOR THE CORE USE CASE. MediaProjection keeps capturing Hearthstone while it is fullscreen foreground, but v1 has no TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY, so the tracker and chat only render when DeckView ITSELF is foreground. The user cannot see counts or ask the AI while actually playing without app-switching (which hides the game). v1 as scoped observes the game but has nowhere to surface the output during play — the product is effectively unusable in its primary moment. Deferring the overlay is a scoping error, not a v2 deferral. | THE 'AUTHORITATIVE OFFLINE TRACKER' CLAIM IS OVERSTATED AND PARTLY FALSE. The deckstring yields the starting 30-card LIST offline, but drawn/remaining COUNTS require recognizing every draw and play — which is cloud, best-effort, and designed to ABSTAIN on low confidence. Every abstain = a missed decrement = permanent drift in remaining counts over a match. The plan repeatedly conflates 'authoritative deck list' with 'authoritative live counts'; the latter is entirely dependent on the recognition it calls 'pure best-effort upside.' The central bet ('correct and fully offline from the deckstring alone') does not hold beyond turn 0. | GENERATED / DISCOVERED / SHUFFLED / COPIED CARDS ARE UNMODELED. Real Hearthstone tracking must handle cards that enter deck/hand outside the deckstring (Discover, card generation, shuffle-ins, copies, transformed cards). The reducer is defined as deckstring − observed-played, which cannot represent any of this. A tracker that ignores generation will visibly diverge from the real game state in most modern decks — this is table stakes for a 'deck tracker' and is entirely absent. | API-KEY PROVISIONING MODEL IS ABSENT — THE #1 UNADDRESSED OPERATIONAL BLOCKER. Gemini free-tier RPD is PER KEY. Three options, none chosen or even surfaced: (a) shared key embedded in the APK = instantly rate-limited across the whole userbase + trivially extractable secret + violates Google's client-key terms; (b) per-user key = severe onboarding friction, most users have no Google AI Studio key; (c) LyAi backend proxy = server infra + aggregated cost that can exceed free tier and cross the $0.10 rule at scale — none of which is planned. This is not in §10 Open Decisions and it gates the entire cloud pipeline. | 800x360 CAPTURE RESOLUTION IS LIKELY BELOW LEGIBILITY FOR CARD IDENTITY. At 800x360 the played-card name text and mana/atk/hp digits are only a handful of pixels; the plan optimistically assumes 'large elements' are recognizable but provides zero evidence OCR/vision can read identity at that scale. The one asset that could settle this (thousands of existing spike JPGs) is never used to validate legibility. Recognition may be near-useless at the chosen resolution. | ROI-TO-DEVICE MAPPING IS UNSOLVED. Hearthstone's UI element positions vary by device resolution and aspect ratio, and the VirtualDisplay aspect ratio must match the native screen or you get letterboxing/distortion that shifts every ROI. The plan references 'Tier-0 ROI phase classifier' and 'ROI maps' but never explains how ROI coordinates are normalized across arbitrary devices — a recognition-blocking gap given open-decision #3 leaves target device unfixed. | 2 FPS SAMPLING VS SUB-SECOND PLAY ANIMATIONS. A card-play center animation is fast (often <1s) and transient; a 2fps timestamp gate can miss it entirely or catch a motion-blurred mid-animation frame. The plan's biggest cost/battery lever (throttle to 2fps) directly undercuts its own event-detection reliability, with no timing analysis reconciling the two. | NO QUANTITATIVE RECOGNITION-ACCURACY BENCHMARK OR ACCEPTANCE TARGET. M4's acceptance criterion is 'resolve to correct dbfIds at acceptable rate' — unmeasurable. There is no labeled ground-truth dataset, no precision/recall/abstain target, no eval harness, despite thousands of spike JPGs available to label. You cannot certify recognition works, or detect regressions, against a prose adjective. | NO PRODUCTION CRASH/ANR/UPTIME TELEMETRY — THE PDS GOLD RULE CANNOT BE CERTIFIED. 'Zero crashes, 99.99% uptime' is unmeasurable in the field without Crashlytics/ANR reporting/field JankStats. The plan's guardrails (StrictMode, JankStats, spike gate) are all pre-release/CI; there is no observability plan to actually PROVE the stability mandate in production. | AndroidView-IN-LazyColumn IS ITSELF A JANK/RECYCLING RISK. AndroidView does not recycle cleanly inside LazyColumn and its inflation cost on fast scroll can stutter; PrecomputedText only fixes the measure() step, not view creation/binding churn. Separately, Markdown images (card art, assistant-returned images) have no async-load plan — a Markwon image request or card thumbnail on the main thread reintroduces exactly the freeze class being engineered out. | BITMAP MEMORY MANAGEMENT / OOM UNADDRESSED. Continuous per-frame pixel copies over a 20+ minute match with no bitmap pooling/reuse strategy risks OutOfMemory, especially if v2's high-res ROI is added. M6 soak has no RSS-growth or leak acceptance bound. OOM is a crash class the 'zero crashes' mandate must explicitly design against. | LOCALIZATION MISMATCH. Ignacio and the likely userbase are Spanish-speaking, but HearthstoneJSON card names are English and the grounding GAME STATE block feeds English facts. A user asking in Spanish with localized card names breaks both OCR name-matching and chat grounding. No locale strategy for card data, OCR, or the chat prompt. | DISTRIBUTION + IP/LEGAL BEYOND ToS. Only 'ToS/anti-cheat sign-off' is flagged. Missing: the Play Store distribution decision, Play policy on MediaProjection disclosure and AI content, and Blizzard IP exposure (reading their game surface + bundling their card data). A screen-reading Hearthstone tool is a plausible store-rejection/IP-strike target; the distribution channel is silently assumed. | DECKSTRING CODEC COMPLETENESS. Modern deck codes carry a sideboard block (E.T.C. Band Manager) plus hero/format headers. A naive port of the classic base64/varint format that ignores the sideboard block will mis-parse current, widely-used codes. Not called out; codec must be tested against official code vectors including sideboards. | DATA EGRESS / CELLULAR / CONTINUOUS-TRANSMISSION CONSENT. Repeatedly uploading screen-derived frames has real mobile-data cost and continuously transmits potentially sensitive screen content. There is no wifi-only gate, no user-visible 'transmitting now' control, and no data-usage budget — beyond the single §10 privacy note about cropping ROIs. | ROTATION / CONFIG-CHANGE HANDLING. Hearthstone is landscape; onboarding is portrait. VirtualDisplay must be recreated/reconfigured on rotation, rotation invalidates all ROIs, and mishandling the capture surface across config changes is a known crash source. Not addressed. | RATE-LIMITER ARBITRATION IS UNDERSPECIFIED. Vision and chat share one RPD/RPM budget. If a match burns the budget on vision recognition, the chat 429s exactly when the user wants in-game advice. The plan asserts a shared limiter exists but defines no priority policy (e.g., reserve budget for user-initiated chat over passive recognition). | NO REAL-DEVICE / OS-VERSION TEST INFRASTRUCTURE. MediaProjection and the 14/15/16 consent+FGS variations cannot be validated on emulator reliably, and 'test on 14/15/16' has no device-farm/Firebase Test Lab plan behind it. There is also no acknowledgment that end-to-end game testing requires manual playtesting against a live Hearthstone install (unautomatable).
Missing decisions: API-key provisioning model (per-user key vs. embedded shared key vs. LyAi backend proxy) — gates the entire cloud pipeline, has security/cost/ToS implications, and is not in §10. | Whether the overlay HUD is actually required for v1 usability — the plan defers it, but without it v1 cannot display tracker/chat during play. This deferral should be an explicit Ignacio decision, framed honestly as 'v1 is unusable mid-game without it.' | Language/localization: English-only card data + English grounding vs. Spanish UI/chat and localized card names — affects OCR, grounding, and product fit for a Spanish-speaking owner/userbase. | Distribution channel (Play Store vs. sideload) and acceptance of Blizzard IP / Play-policy risk for a screen-reading tool that bundles their card data — beyond the ToS/anti-cheat item already listed. | A concrete, numeric recognition-accuracy acceptance target (precision/recall/abstain rate) and whether the existing spike JPGs will be labeled to build the eval set — otherwise M4 cannot be signed off. | Crash/telemetry vendor decision (e.g., Crashlytics) and its privacy tradeoff — required to certify the PDS Gold Rule in production, but it ships screen-app crash context to a third party. | Explicit product decision on whether live remaining-counts must be reliable (which mandates recognition on the critical path) or whether v1 ships as a static deck-list + best-effort annotations — because the plan currently claims both.
Unverified assumptions: That Gemini 2.5-flash free tier serves BOTH streaming chat (streamGenerateContent?alt=sse) AND vision under a single key at the quoted ~250-500 RPD / ~10 RPM, and that these terms are stable — the plan itself notes the caps were cut 50-80% in Dec-2025, i.e., volatile. | That 800x360 frames are legible enough for OCR/vision to identify specific cards — asserted, never tested against the available JPG corpus. | The 'media_resolution=LOW -> ~64-72 tokens' and '~500 input tokens per 800x360 frame' cost figures — quoted precisely but unverified. | That the free-tier data terms (prompts/responses used for training + human review) are acceptable for a product that transmits screen-derived content — flagged as a decision but the underlying terms are stated as fact without verification. | That HearthstoneJSON's card data and HearthSim's deckstring codec licensing permit bundling/porting into a distributed app. | That Markwon 4.6.x + PrecomputedTextSetterCompat on a background executor behaves as claimed under incremental streaming + LazyColumn recycling — asserted as a 'proven anti-freeze path' but not demonstrated for this specific streaming+virtualized configuration. | That min-SDK 26 / target-34 is compatible with the Android 14+ single-use-consent and mediaProjection FGS behavior the plan designs to — the SDK pin is itself listed as an open decision, so the whole capture-ordering design rests on an unpinned assumption.

### **Claude** `01:12`

# DeckView — Definitive Build Plan

**Version:** 2.0 · 2026-07-14 · **Package namespace:** `dev.lyai.deckview.*`
**Owner:** Ignacio (LyAi Labs) · **Mandate:** STABILITY FIRST (PDS Gold Rule — zero crashes, no freezes; accuracy/features secondary)
**Status:** Planning only. Propuesta-antes-de-aplicar. No build/deploy without explicit order.

---

## 1. Product & scope

**DeckView** is an on-device Android Hearthstone deck tracker with an integrated, grounded, streaming AI chat. Because Android's sandbox forbids reading another app's `Power.log` (the mechanism every PC tracker relies on), DeckView observes the game the only way it can on-device: it captures the screen via **MediaProjection**, recognizes discrete game events (card played, mulligan, draw, board, turn) with best-effort vision, and maintains a live game-state model that is *seeded* by the user importing their deck as a deckstring. A streaming, Markdown-rendering AI chat (Gemini 2.5-flash) — the product star — answers questions and comments on the current game, grounded on deterministic card facts so it cannot invent cards. Because the user is looking at Hearthstone (fullscreen, foreground) during play, DeckView surfaces its output through a **draw-over-other-apps overlay HUD** — this is core, not optional.

**Honest framing of the central bet (corrected).** The deckstring gives us the **authoritative starting 30-card *list*, fully offline** — the one thing we can guarantee without recognition. **Live drawn/remaining *counts* are NOT offline-authoritative:** they depend on recognizing every draw/play, which is best-effort and abstains on low confidence. Each abstain is a missed decrement, i.e. drift. We therefore treat counts as a **confidence-annotated estimate**, expose an "uncertain" state honestly in the UI, and never claim a count is authoritative when it is inferred. This distinction is load-bearing and is reflected everywhere below.

### MVP (v1) — IN
- **Deckstring import** → authoritative 30-card *list*, offline; seeds the state model.
- **Overlay HUD** (`TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY`) — compact, movable, collapsible tracker + chat launcher that renders *over Hearthstone during play*. This is what makes v1 usable in its primary moment.
- **MediaProjection capture service** (foreground, off-thread) reusing the `spike` harness.
- **Adaptive capture** — low idle rate with **event-triggered burst capture** so fast (<1s) play animations are not missed (§6.2).
- On-device **change-detector** (luma-diff / pHash) + **Tier-0 phase classifier** gating; **anchor-based ROI normalization** across device resolutions (§5).
- **Best-effort recognition** on discrete, debounced events, constrained to the imported deck's dbfIds + seen opponent cards, with **explicit legibility validation** against the existing spike JPG corpus as a gating pre-task (§5, §7 M-neg1).
- **Extended `GameStateStore`** that models not just deckstring − played, but also **generated / discovered / shuffled / copied / transformed** cards via a zone-and-provenance model (§5), with per-fact confidence.
- **Overlay + in-app Compose tracker UI** (deck list, remaining counts with confidence, turn/mana if read).
- **Grounded, streaming, Markdown AI chat** with off-thread parse + virtualized list + async image loading (the anti-freeze core).
- **Room persistence** of chat + session + state; graceful offline / rate-limited / degraded states.
- **Localization (Spanish-first):** localized card names (HearthstoneJSON locale packs), Spanish chat, locale-aware OCR/grounding (§5, §11).
- **API-key provisioning via LyAi backend proxy** (decision resolved, §9/§10).
- **Guardrails + production telemetry:** StrictMode, JankStats, spike-harness `inter_ms` regression gate, plus **field crash/ANR/jank telemetry** to certify the PDS Gold Rule (§6.4, §6.5).

### Later (v2+) — explicitly NOT in v1
- Opponent **open-set** card recognition (v1 tracks the *user's* deck list authoritatively; opponent + generated cards = best-effort annotation only).
- On-device ML classifier / bundled pHash reference DB per expansion.
- Selective high-resolution ROI capture beyond the minimum needed for v1 legibility (§5 sets the v1 floor).
- Battlegrounds / Arena / Duels mode-specific ROI maps (v1 = Standard/Wild constructed only).
- Paid-tier / on-device LLM for full privacy (an Ignacio cost decision, §10).
- Any input automation (strictly observational — ToS posture).

---

## 2. Architecture

Best-effort recognition feeding a deterministic-where-possible, confidence-annotated tracker; two independently engineered-out freeze surfaces (capture pipeline and chat rendering); an overlay HUD as the primary in-play surface.

```
 ONBOARDING (one-time)
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ user pastes DECKSTRING ─► decode (base64/varint,│
 │   incl. sideboard + hero/format headers)        │
 │   ─► (dbfId,count)[] + sideboard ─► resolve vs   │
 │       bundled HearthstoneJSON (locale) ─►        │
 │       GameStateStore: authoritative 30-card LIST │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘

 CAPTURE / RECOGNITION  (dedicated HandlerThread — NEVER the UI thread)
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ MediaProjection ─► VirtualDisplay(aspect-matched) ─► ImageReader    │
 │        │ onImageAvailable (HandlerThread), maxImages=2-3           │
 │        ▼                                                           │
 │  acquireLatestImage() ─► copy into POOLED bitmap ─► close()[finally]│
 │        │  ADAPTIVE gate: ~1-2 fps idle, BURST ~6-10 fps when the    │
 │        │  change-detector sees motion (catch <1s play animations)  │
 │        ▼                                                           │
 │  on-device change-detector (luma-diff / 64-bit pHash, sub-ms)      │
 │        │  anchor-detect (fixed UI landmarks) ─► normalize ROIs      │
 │        ▼                                                           │
 │  Tier-0 ROI phase classifier (menu/mulligan/in-game/victory)      │
 │        │  meaningful discrete event ? debounce/settle             │
 │        ▼                                                           │
 │  bounded DROP-OLDEST queue (capacity 1)                            │
 │        ▼                                                           │
 │  background recognition worker (coroutine, timeout, cancellable)   │
 │    ├─ ML Kit OCR (offline): card name + mana/atk/hp digits         │
 │    └─ Gemini 2.5-flash VISION via LyAi PROXY (best-effort, gated,  │
 │         429-backoff, candidate set = deck dbfIds + seen oppo)      │
 │        │  low confidence ► ABSTAIN (mark unknown, never guess)     │
 │        ▼                                                           │
 │  resolve dbfId vs HearthstoneJSON ─► RecognitionEvent{conf}        │
 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐  confidence-annotated
 │ GameStateStore  (StateFlow<GameState>) │  zones: DECK · HAND · PLAYED · GENERATED
 │  reducer merges: deckstring LIST truth │  · SHUFFLED-UNKNOWN · TRANSFORMED · OPPONENT
 │  + provenance-aware recognition events │  each card: source + confidence + certain?
 └────────────────────────────────────────┘
   │ collect (Main)                              ▲ recompute per turn
   ▼                                             │
 ┌──────────────┐  ┌───────────────┐   ┌─────────┴──────────────────┐
 │ OVERLAY HUD  │  │ IN-APP TRACKER│   │ CHAT layer                 │
 │ (over HS,    │  │ (Compose)     │   │ on user msg OR debounced    │
 │  movable,    │  │ deck/counts/  │   │ game event                  │
 │  collapsible)│  │ turn — store  │   │ build compact GAME STATE    │
 │ counts+conf, │  │ only          │   │  block (canonical DB facts, │
 │ chat launcher│  └───────────────┘   │  localized) + bounded hist  │
 └──────────────┘                      │        ▼                    │
        ▲ driven ONLY by the store,    │ LlmClient.streamChat()      │
        │ never a pending API call     │  proxy → Gemini SSE (IO)    │
        │                              │        ▼ Flow<Delta>        │
        │                              │ append plain text to ONE    │
        │                              │  streaming bubble ≤1/frame   │
        │                              │  (sample ~33ms)             │
        │                              │        ▼ on complete        │
        │                              │ parse Markdown OFF-thread   │
        │                              │  (Default) ─► LruCache ─►   │
        │                              │  AndroidView(Markwon)+      │
        │                              │  PrecomputedText+async imgs │
        │                              └────────────────────────────┘

        └────────────── Room (chat, session, state snapshot, cache) ◄┘
```

---

## 3. Tech stack

| Layer | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Language | **Kotlin** | Coroutines/Flow are the backbone of the off-thread stability model. |
| Min/Target SDK | **min 26, target 34** (to re-pin per §10.4) | Android 14 FGS/consent rules are the constraint we design to; pin confirmed before M3. |
| App/UI shell | **Jetpack Compose** | Lean, modern for tracker/onboarding/chat list. |
| **Overlay HUD** | **`WindowManager` + `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY`** hosting a `ComposeView` (with a `LifecycleOwner`/`SavedStateRegistryOwner`/`ViewModelStoreOwner` shim) | The only way to show tracker+chat over fullscreen Hearthstone. Core v1 surface. |
| Chat bubble body | **`AndroidView(Markwon)` + PrecomputedText**, pooled | Proven anti-freeze parse path; view-creation churn mitigated by an off-screen inflation pool + stable keys (§6.1). |
| Chat list | **`LazyColumn`, stable keys, `@Immutable` models** | Virtualized — streaming answer is one item, never a monolith. |
| Async | **Coroutines + Flow** (IO=network/SSE, Default=parsing/CV) | Structured concurrency, cancellation, `sample()/conflate()`, drop-oldest backpressure. |
| DI | **Hilt** | Wires capture service, overlay, `LlmClient`, repos, dispatchers; keeps LLM swappable. |
| Networking | **OkHttp, raw SSE** to LyAi proxy | Lean footprint; POST proxied `streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`. |
| LLM abstraction | **`interface LlmClient { fun streamChat(...): Flow<Delta> }`** | Isolates provider; Claude / on-device swap later without touching UI/grounding. |
| Chat model | **Gemini 2.5-flash** via LyAi proxy; `OfflineClient` fallback | Free default per LyAi rules; canned degraded response offline. |
| Capture | **MediaProjection + VirtualDisplay + ImageReader** in a `mediaProjection` FGS on a HandlerThread | Raw frames for vision; off-thread from day one; aspect-matched VirtualDisplay. |
| Bitmap mgmt | **Bitmap pool / reuse (`inBitmap`), bounded** | Prevents OOM over 20+ min matches (§6.6). |
| Change-detector | **On-device luma-diff / 64-bit pHash** | Sub-ms gate; also the burst-capture trigger. |
| Recognition | **Gemini 2.5-flash vision** (proxied) + **ML Kit OCR** (offline) | Deck-constrained; OCR disambiguates/ties-break; both feed confidence. |
| Card data | **Bundled HearthstoneJSON** `cards.collectible.json` + **locale packs** + ported deckstring codec (with sideboard) | Offline dbfId→facts; localized names; ground-truth import. |
| Persistence | **Room** (chat/session/state/cache) + **DataStore** (settings, active deckstring, prefs) | Survives process death / session cutoffs. |
| Markdown | **Markwon 4.6.x** + `PrecomputedTextSetterCompat` + **async image plugin (Coil/OkHttp)** | Off-thread parse; images loaded async, never on main. |
| Telemetry | **Firebase Crashlytics + ANR reporting + field JankStats** (privacy-reviewed, §6.5/§10.6) | Certifies the PDS Gold Rule in production, not just CI. |
| Guardrails | **StrictMode (debug) + JankStats/FrameMetrics + spike `inter_ms` CI gate** | Turns the zero-freeze mandate into an automated build check. |
| Test infra | **Firebase Test Lab (14/15/16 physical) + manual playtest protocol** | MediaProjection consent/FGS variants can't be validated on emulator (§6.7). |

Single Gradle app module for v1 (fastest ship); package boundaries drawn so modules can split later.

| Package | Responsibility |

| `…capture` | `CaptureService` (FGS type=mediaProjection), `MediaProjectionStateMachine`, HandlerThread, ImageReader drain, **adaptive/burst throttle**, bitmap pool, black-frame guard, rotation/config handling, typed exceptions. |
| `…capture.spike` | The existing `spike` harness, adapted as capture backbone + `inter_ms`/`proc_ms`/`cpu` instrumentation and regression-gate hooks. |
| `…recognition` | `ChangeDetector`, `AnchorLocator` + `RoiNormalizer`, `PhaseClassifier`, drop-oldest queue, `RecognitionWorker`, `RecognitionEvent` (with confidence), abstain logic. |
| `…recognition.vision` | `GeminiVisionClient` (via proxy, deck-constrained prompt, timeout, 429 backoff, pHash-keyed cache). |

| `…recognition.eval` | **Labeled-corpus eval harness**: precision/recall/abstain over spike JPGs; regression report. |
