## 5. Hearthstone data, recognition & state model

**Card DB — HearthstoneJSON.** Bundle `cards.collectible.json` (versioned per patch) plus **locale name packs** (at minimum `esES`/`esMX` + `enUS`) as app assets for offline, deterministic resolution. Each card carries string `cardId` (`EX1_001`), numeric **`dbfId`** (Leeroy = 559), name (per-locale), cost/type/text/mechanics. `dbfId` is the join key across everything and is **locale-invariant** — so recognition, grounding, and display can each pick their own locale off the same id.

**Deckstring format (completeness fixed).** A deck code is base64 of a varint stream keyed on `dbfId`, but modern codes include a **format/hero header and a sideboard block (E.T.C. Band Manager)**. The `…deckstring` codec ports HearthSim's `hearthstone-deckstrings` **including sideboard and header handling**, and is unit-tested against official code vectors that include sideboarded and Wild/Standard codes. On import: decode → `(dbfId,count)[]` + sideboard → resolve vs bundled DB → seed the authoritative 30-card list.

**Live state model (generated/discovered/copied/shuffled fixed).** The reducer is **not** merely `deckstring − played`. `GameState` models explicit **zones with provenance**:
- **DECK (from deckstring):** the only cards we can enumerate; remaining count is deckstring-list minus *confidently* observed leaves; unobserved/abstained events leave the count flagged **uncertain** rather than silently wrong.
- **GENERATED / DISCOVERED:** cards that enter hand/deck outside the deckstring; added as best-effort, clearly labeled "generated," never mixed into the authoritative list.
- **SHUFFLED-UNKNOWN:** shuffle-ins (e.g. tokens) tracked as opaque count adjustments where recognized.
- **COPIED / TRANSFORMED:** modeled as new provenance-tagged entries; the original is not double-counted.
- **OPPONENT:** open-set, best-effort annotation only (v1).

Every card fact carries `{source, confidence, certain:boolean}`. The UI and the chat grounding both **surface uncertainty honestly** ("~2 copies remaining, unconfirmed") instead of asserting precision we do not have. This is the corrected, defensible version of the "tracker" claim: **authoritative list, confidence-annotated live state.**

**Recognition → card IDs.** Change-detector + phase classifier decide a discrete event occurred → a **normalized, cropped, upscaled ROI** goes to ML Kit OCR (name/digits) and/or Gemini vision, **constrained to the imported deck's dbfIds + already-seen opponent/generated cards**. The recognizer returns a `dbfId` with a confidence or **ABSTAINS**. Priority targets are large, unambiguous elements — the played-card center animation, mulligan cards, board minions — never the small fanned hand.

**ROI-to-device normalization (fixed).** ROIs are **not** hard-coded pixel rectangles. The `VirtualDisplay` is created **aspect-ratio-matched to the source display** (no letterbox/distortion). `AnchorLocator` finds a few fixed Hearthstone UI landmarks (mana crystal cluster, end-turn button, rope, board rune frame) per frame; `RoiNormalizer` expresses every ROI in **anchor-relative normalized coordinates**, so the same map works across resolutions/aspect ratios and survives rotation. This removes the dependency on a fixed target device for recognition to function.

**Legibility validation (fixed — gating pre-task).** Before committing to any capture resolution, **M-neg1** labels a sample of the **existing spike JPGs** and measures whether OCR/vision can actually read card identity and digits at 800×360. If they cannot (likely for the fanned hand and small digits), the capture resolution / selective-high-res-ROI floor for v1 is **raised to the minimum that passes** the accuracy target (§7 M4). We do not assume "large elements are legible" — we prove it against real frames first.

**Sampling vs animation timing (fixed).** Idle capture runs ~1–2 fps for battery; the change-detector triggers a **burst window (~6–10 fps for a bounded interval)** the instant motion is detected, so sub-second play animations are caught and the debounce settles on a clean, non-motion-blurred frame. This reconciles the battery lever with event-detection reliability.

## 6. Stability plan (PRIORITY)

Two independent freeze surfaces, both engineered out from day one, plus structural crash-safety, memory-safety, overlay lifecycle safety, and a verification strategy that certifies the mandate in production.

### 6.1 The diagnosed Markdown main-thread freeze (up to 3.9s) — killed by five rules

1. **Off-thread parsing, always.** SSE on `Dispatchers.IO`; CommonMark→Spanned on `Dispatchers.Default` via one Markwon built with `textSetter(PrecomputedTextSetterCompat.create(backgroundExecutor))`. The UI thread receives an already-parsed Spanned/`PrecomputedText` and only blocks at `measure()`. The main thread never parses.
2. **Virtualized chat list.** `LazyColumn`, `key = message.id`, `@Immutable` models. The in-progress answer is **one** streaming item; completed answers are individual items. No monolithic view is ever inflated. Parsing is out of composition entirely.
3. **Incremental, throttled streaming.** Tokens append plain text to the single streaming bubble, coalesced to **≤1 UI update/frame** (`Flow.sample(~33ms)` / `conflate()`). Never `setText` per token. On completion the finished message is parsed off-thread, cached in an `LruCache` (key = id + content hash), rendered via `AndroidView(Markwon)` + `PrecomputedText`. Rebind reuses the cached Spanned — never re-parses.
4. **Delimiter suppression while streaming.** A single-pass `MarkdownBuffer` hides trailing unclosed `**`, `*`, `` ` ``, ` ``` ` until closed; on completion the full unmodified text renders so intentional lone markers survive.
5. **`AndroidView`-in-`LazyColumn` churn + images (fixed).** `AndroidView` does not recycle cleanly on fast scroll and `PrecomputedText` only fixes `measure()`, not inflation. Mitigations: **stable keys** so bubbles aren't re-created; an **off-screen `TextView` inflation pool** reused across bind; capping visible completed bubbles and paginating history; and an **async Markwon image plugin** (Coil/OkHttp on IO) so card art or assistant images **never** load on the main thread. A synchronous image fetch is banned in review — it would reintroduce exactly this freeze class.

**PrecomputedText correctness:** set `textSize/typeface/textDir/breakStrategy` on the target `TextView` *before* building `Params`, or `measure()` throws / silently falls back on-thread. One shared text-appearance style for both the precompute step and the view; unit-test that params match.

### 6.2 The capture-pipeline freeze/ANR surface — engineered out

- **Everything off the UI thread:** service work on a dedicated HandlerThread; that Handler is passed to `createVirtualDisplay(..., handler)` and `ImageReader.setOnImageAvailableListener(listener, handler)` so callbacks never land on main.
- **Back-pressure (the classic ANR):** `ImageReader.newInstance(w,h,fmt, maxImages=2-3)`; `onImageAvailable` always `acquireLatestImage()` (drops stale) → copy into a **pooled** bitmap → `close()` in a **`finally`**. Missing/late `close()` stalls SurfaceFlinger → ANR; a watchdog logs any callback over a few ms.
- **Adaptive throttle:** ~1–2 fps idle, burst on motion (§5); even skipped frames are acquired+closed to avoid back-pressure.
- **Decoupled recognition:** a bounded **drop-oldest queue (capacity 1)** feeds the background worker, so a slow (0.7–3s) round-trip drops frames and can never back up the buffer or block anything.

### 6.3 Crash-safety / lifecycle / rotation

- **MediaProjection state machine** enforces the Android 14+ order: `createScreenCaptureIntent()` → consent → `startForeground(mediaProjection)` → `getMediaProjection()` → `registerCallback()` (mandatory before `createVirtualDisplay()`) → `createVirtualDisplay()`.
- **Typed exception handling** per step: `SecurityException`, `IllegalStateException`, `MissingForegroundServiceTypeException` → graceful degrade, never crash.
- **Every `onStop()` cause is first-class** (stop chip, screen lock, another projection, process death, single-use-token expiry): release VirtualDisplay+Surface, mark inactive, re-prompt for **fresh consent** on resume (14+ tokens are single-use; no silent restart).
- **Rotation / config change (fixed):** landscape game vs portrait onboarding. On rotation/display change the VirtualDisplay+ImageReader are **recreated at the new dimensions**, ROIs are re-derived from anchors (so they stay valid), and the overlay re-lays-out. Config-change handling is explicit — a known crash source, closed.
- **Black/low-variance frame guard** (FLAG_SECURE, transitions, wrong single-app share) → surface "can't read the game" instead of feeding garbage.
- **All network calls** timeout-bounded, cancellable, 429 exponential backoff, offline fallback. The deterministic list-tracker runs with **zero network** — it can never be stalled by the model.
- **Persistence** (Room + DataStore) so process death / documented session cutoffs lose nothing.

### 6.4 Overlay lifecycle safety

- Overlay permission requested via `ACTION_MANAGE_OVERLAY_PERMISSION` in onboarding; app fully functional (in-app view) if declined, with a clear explanation of what's lost in-game.
- Overlay `ComposeView` hosted with proper `Lifecycle`/`SavedStateRegistry`/`ViewModelStore` owners; window added/removed in lock-step with the capture service; never leaked on stop/rotation/process death.
- Overlay renders **only** from `GameStateStore` — never blocks on a pending API call — so an in-play HUD can never freeze the thing the user is playing on.

### 6.5 Memory-safety / OOM

- **Bitmap pool** with `inBitmap` reuse; bounded working-set; explicit recycle of copied frames. No unbounded per-frame allocation over a 20+ min match.
- Recognition-cache and Spanned `LruCache` are size-bounded.
- **M6 soak adds an RSS-growth acceptance bound** and a leak check (LeakCanary in debug) — OOM is a crash class the zero-crash mandate designs against explicitly.

### 6.6 Production telemetry (PDS Gold Rule certification — fixed)

CI guardrails prove stability pre-release; they cannot prove 99.99% in the field. v1 ships **Firebase Crashlytics + ANR reporting + field JankStats** (frame-time histograms tagged to "long-Markdown render" and "in-game capture" scenarios), privacy-reviewed (§10.6). This is what makes the mandate *measurable in production* rather than aspirational. Crash-free-session and ANR-rate SLOs become the release gate.

### 6.7 Verification & test strategy

- **Unit / instrumentation:** deckstring codec vs official vectors (incl. sideboards); reducer provenance logic (generated/copied/shuffled/transform cases); PrecomputedText param-match; MarkdownBuffer delimiter cases.
- **Recognition eval harness (`recognition.eval`):** the labeled spike-JPG corpus (§5) yields **precision / recall / abstain-rate** numbers per event type; run in CI as a **regression gate** against a numeric target (§7 M4). Replaces "acceptable rate" prose with a signed-off number.
- **Freeze/jank gates:** StrictMode (zero main-thread parse/IO), JankStats (no frame > ~200ms during long render), spike `inter_ms > ~700ms` **fails the build**, including a scenario that renders a long chat message **while** recognition runs (worst-case concurrency, M6).
- **Real-device / OS matrix (fixed):** MediaProjection consent + FGS variants validated on **physical Android 14/15/16** via **Firebase Test Lab** — not emulator. A documented **manual playtest protocol** against a live Hearthstone install covers what cannot be automated (real games, real animations, real rotation).
- **Soak:** 1-hour ladder session — zero crashes/ANRs, bounded RSS, stable CPU/thermal, no Image leaks.

## 8. Risk register

| Risk | Sev | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| CV/vision on/near the UI/capture thread reintroduces multi-second freezes | **High** | Strict off-thread pipeline (HandlerThread + background coroutines), drop-oldest cap-1 queue, spike `inter_ms` CI gate; load-test long-chat-render *during* recognition (M6). |
| Missing/late `image.close()` → buffer stall → ANR | **High** | `acquireLatestImage()`+`close()` in `finally`, `maxImages` 2–3, per-callback watchdog. |
| **Live counts drift because recognition abstains/misses draws** | **High** | Counts are confidence-annotated, never claimed authoritative; "uncertain" surfaced honestly; deckstring *list* stays authoritative regardless; user can manually confirm. |
| **No mid-game surface** (overlay was deferred) → product unusable while playing | **High** | Overlay HUD promoted into **v1 core** (M3); in-app fallback if permission declined. |
| **Generated/discovered/copied/shuffled cards diverge from real state** | **High** | Provenance/zone reducer models them explicitly, labeled "generated," never mixed into the authoritative list. |
| Android 14/15/16 single-use consent + FGS ordering + rotation → crash | **High** | State machine encoding the exact order; `registerCallback` before `createVirtualDisplay`; rotation recreates display/ROIs; every `onStop()`=re-consent; Test Lab 14/15/16. |
| **API-key provisioning / free-tier RPD is per-key** | **High** | **LyAi backend proxy** (decision, §9): rotates keys, meters, caches, hides secret; cloud never on critical path; change-gating keeps calls to a handful/game. |
| Gemini free-tier RPD volatile (cut 50–80% Dec-2025) → 429s | **High** | Proxy-side pooling + backoff; priority rate limiter reserves chat budget; deterministic list-tracker independent of model. |
| **800×360 illegible for card identity** | **High** | **M-neg1 validates legibility on real spike JPGs first** and sets the v1 resolution/ROI floor from data, not assumption. |
| **ROI positions vary by device/aspect/rotation** | **Med** | Aspect-matched VirtualDisplay + anchor-relative normalized ROIs; no fixed target device required. |
| **2fps misses sub-second animations** | **Med** | Adaptive idle rate + motion-triggered burst window catches fast plays. |
| **Recognition unmeasurable ("acceptable rate")** | **Med** | Labeled corpus + eval harness → numeric precision/recall/abstain gate in CI. |
| `AndroidView`-in-`LazyColumn` churn + Markdown images on main thread | **Med** | Stable keys, off-screen inflation pool, capped/paginated bubbles, async image plugin; sync image fetch banned in review. |
| **OOM over long match** | **Med** | Bitmap pool/reuse, bounded caches, RSS soak bound, LeakCanary. |
| **Localization mismatch (Spanish user, English card data)** | **Med** | dbfId-keyed locale packs; Spanish OCR name-match + grounding + chat; English kept as fallback. |
| Privacy: free-tier sends screen-derived content (training + human review) | **Med** | Send only cropped ROIs + minimal structured state (never raw screenshots); PII-strip; wifi-only + egress control; paid/on-device escalation to Ignacio (§10). |
| **Data egress / cellular cost / continuous transmission** | **Med** | Wifi-only gate (default), user-visible "transmitting" indicator, data-usage budget, change-gating minimizes uploads. |
| Card DB staleness (new sets ~3×/yr, nerfs, art) | **Med** | HearthstoneJSON bundled as versioned, updatable data drop; deckstring ground-truth resilient to art shifts. |
| **PDS Gold Rule uncertifiable in field** | **Med** | Crashlytics + ANR + field JankStats; crash-free-session/ANR SLO as release gate. |
| **Deckstring codec mis-parses sideboarded codes** | **Med** | Codec handles sideboard + headers; tested vs official vectors incl. sideboards. |
| **Distribution / Blizzard IP / Play policy** | **Med** | §10 decision: sideload vs Play; MediaProjection + AI-content disclosure; IP posture on reading game surface + bundling card data. |
| ToS/anti-cheat ambiguity of a screen-reading advisor | **Low** | Strictly observational, no input automation; Ignacio product/ToS call (§10). |

## 9. Cost & compliance

- **Default free API confirmed:** Gemini 2.5-flash serves **both** vision and chat, free tier. No paid APIs (no Imagen 4, Places, paid cloud vision). No on-device model to train/ship in v1.
- **API-key provisioning (decision resolved): LyAi backend proxy.** All Gemini traffic routes through a thin LyAi-hosted proxy that holds server-side keys, meters/rate-limits per user, caches identical vision requests, strips PII, and never ships a secret in the APK. This is the only option that (a) doesn't embed an extractable, instantly-rate-limited shared key, (b) doesn't impose per-user Google-AI-Studio-key onboarding friction, and (c) keeps client terms clean. **Cost caveat flagged:** aggregated proxy usage at scale can exceed free tier and cross the **$0.10 rule** — so the proxy enforces a **global budget cap** and the design keeps per-game calls to a handful. Any move past free tier is an explicit Ignacio authorization (§10).
- **Per-call cost is trivially under $0.10** *if* free-tier terms hold: an 800×360 frame ≈ ~500 input tokens; `media_resolution=LOW` cuts it materially. **These token/cost figures and the ~250–500 RPD / ~10 RPM caps are quoted from volatile, recently-cut terms and are treated as UNVERIFIED — re-confirmed against live Google docs before M4** (§10). The real constraint is RPD, controlled by change-gating + event-debouncing.
- **Nothing in v1 crosses ≥$0.10** as designed on free tier through the proxy budget cap.
- **The one cost decision to flag (§10):** true privacy (no training / human review of screen-derived content) requires the **paid Gemini tier (≥$0.10, Ignacio auth)** or an on-device model. v1 mitigates by sending only cropped ROIs + minimal structured state, never raw screenshots.
- **Telemetry cost/privacy:** Crashlytics is free but ships crash context of a screen-reading app to a third party — an explicit privacy tradeoff (§10.6).
- ML Kit OCR, Room/DataStore, deckstring codec, HearthstoneJSON bundle: all free/offline. **Licensing to verify (§10):** HearthstoneJSON data + HearthSim deckstring codec permit bundling/porting into a distributed app.

## 10. Open decisions for Ignacio

1. **Privacy vs cost.** Accept free-tier data terms (prompts/responses used for training + human review of screen-derived context), or authorize paid tier (≥$0.10) / commit to a future on-device model? Blocks the vision+chat privacy posture. *(Terms are volatile — to be re-verified before commit.)*
2. **API-key provisioning — confirm the LyAi backend proxy** (recommended, §9) vs per-user key vs embedded key. Proxy adds server infra + an aggregated cost that can cross the $0.10 rule at scale (budget-capped in the design). Gates the entire cloud pipeline.
3. **Overlay HUD is required for v1, not deferred.** Framed honestly: **without it, v1 cannot show tracker/chat during play and is unusable in its primary moment.** Confirm overlay-in-v1 (plan now assumes yes).
4. **Live-counts posture.** Confirm the honest framing: **authoritative deck *list* offline; live remaining *counts* are confidence-annotated best-effort.** If reliable live counts are mandatory, recognition moves onto the critical path — a much larger, riskier scope. Which does v1 ship?
5. **Localization.** Confirm Spanish-first (localized card names, Spanish chat/grounding/OCR) with English fallback.
6. **Telemetry vendor** (Crashlytics + ANR) — accept shipping screen-app crash context to a third party to certify the PDS Gold Rule? Alternative: self-hosted/minimal telemetry.
7. **Recognition acceptance target.** Approve labeling the existing spike JPGs to build the eval set and set a **numeric precision/recall/abstain target** for M4 sign-off.
8. **Target device(s) + resolution / aspect ratio,** and confirm the **v1 capture-resolution floor** will be set by M-neg1's legibility test (may exceed 800×360).
9. **Min/target SDK pin** (assume min 26 / target 34). 14 vs 15 vs 16 change consent/FGS/single-app-share behavior; pin before M3.
10. **Distribution + IP/legal.** Play Store vs sideload; Play policy on MediaProjection disclosure + AI content; Blizzard IP exposure (reading their surface + bundling card data). A screen-reading Hearthstone tool is a plausible store-rejection/IP-strike target.
11. **Opponent + generated-card scope for v1.** Confirm opponent = best-effort annotation only, generated/discovered cards = labeled best-effort (user deck list authoritative).
12. **Game modes.** v1 assumes Standard/Wild constructed; BG/Arena/Duels need separate ROI maps → v2.
13. **ToS/anti-cheat sign-off** on a strictly observational, no-automation advisory app.
14. **Licensing confirmation** to bundle HearthstoneJSON data and port the HearthSim deckstring codec into a distributed app.
15. **Data egress defaults.** Confirm **wifi-only by default** with a user-visible "transmitting" control and a data-usage budget.
16. **The Android repo.** No DeckView source exists — build-from-scratch. Confirm repo location/creation so M-neg1/M0 can begin by adapting the `spike` harness.

## MODE LANE: constructed (status: active)
Full feature parity spec for CONSTRUCTED (Standard + Wild ladder, plus Tavern Brawl) matching Firestone and Hearthstone Deck Tracker (HDT). The load-bearing reality check: HDT and Firestone read Hearthstone's local Power.log / game-state file, giving them PERFECT ground truth (exact entity IDs, provenance, hidden triggers, mulligan/return events). DeckView has ONLY MediaProjection screen capture — no log access. This is the single most important constraint: everything that depends on invisible or entity-level state (card provenance/created-by, stolen/returned/mulliganed tracking, exact secret elimination via hidden triggers, precise fatigue counting) is either much harder or must abstain. Deterministic/visible features (own cards-left, mana/turn, draw probability) are reliable; stats-DB features (opponent archetype prediction, mulligan/matchup win-rates) are reliable because they only need class + visibly-played cards + an external meta feed (HSReplay-style). Per STABILITY-FIRST mandate, every recognizer must abstain on low confidence rather than show wrong state.
FEATURES:
  - [must/medium] Own deck / cards-left tracker: Live overlay of the player's 30-card decklist with each card greyed out / decremented as it is drawn or milled, showing exact copies remaining. Core, table-stakes feature of both HDT and Firestone. Requires a known starting decklist: from a pasted/imported deck code (reliable) OR reconstructed from observed draws (partial). On our screen-capture stack the decklist itself isn't in any log, so import/deck-code entry is the anchor; draws are inferred by detecting a new card entering hand and matching it to a deck card via OCR/vision. (recog: Starting decklist (user-imported deck code, or built from observed cards). Detect draw events: a card sliding into the player's hand; identify the drawn card by OCR/ML Kit + Gemini vision against the deck's candidate set. Detect mill/discard. Needs reliable 'card entered hand' motion trigger.; compute: deterministic state-tracking (lookup vs known decklist))
  - [must/low] Turn / mana crystal tracker: Reads current turn number and available/total mana crystals; drives 'what could the opponent play at this mana' and lethal math. Trivial for log-based trackers. For DeckView it's a fixed-ROI read of the mana-crystal gem row and the turn/rope indicator. (recog: Anchor-normalized ROI over the mana crystal tray (count filled vs empty gems) and the end-turn/rope state. High-contrast, stable location — well suited to change-detector + template read, no OCR needed.; compute: deterministic (ROI read))
  - [must/medium] Opponent played-card log + hand/deck counts: Chronological list of every card the opponent has revealed (played, or shown), plus a live hand-count and deck-count. Foundation for archetype prediction. HDT/Firestone also tag provenance (created/stolen/returned/mulliganed) and 'how long held' — those tags come from Power.log entity tracking we do NOT have. DeckView can reliably log visibly-played cards and count hand size by counting card-backs in the opponent hand fan; it should NOT claim provenance it can't see. (recog: Identify each card the opponent plays (OCR/vision on the play animation / board). Count opponent hand cards (card-back fan count). Track deck-count by decrementing on draw animation. Provenance/created-by tags: NOT reliably recognizable from pixels — mark as unsupported or best-effort.; compute: deterministic state-tracking)
  - [should/medium] Opponent deck / archetype prediction: Guess the opponent's archetype and surface 'cards they could still have' by matching the set of cards they've played (plus hero/class) against current meta decklists, filtering out decks that lack an observed card and ranking remaining candidates by popularity. This is exactly the HDT MetaDetector / deck-predictor plugin and Firestone's related-cards behaviour. Needs an external meta-deck corpus (HSReplay-style). Very achievable for us because inputs are only class + visibly-played cards. (recog: Opponent hero class (hero portrait / hero power ROI). The running list of opponent's played cards (from the play-log feature). No hidden state required — screen-capture friendly. Compute is offline once meta corpus is bundled/synced.; compute: stats DB match + probability ranking)
  - [should/medium] Mulligan advisor + mulligan win-rates: During the opening mulligan, overlay a keep/toss recommendation and the mulligan win-rate for each offered card, conditioned on your deck and (if known) opponent class. (recog: The 3 (coin) or 4 mulligan cards shown — read via OCR/vision in the fixed mulligan layout. Player deck identity (from import). Opponent class if revealed. Time-boxed recognition window; abstain if a card can't be confidently identified.; compute: stats DB lookup (external mulligan win-rate table))
  - [should/high] Secrets helper (possible secrets, cross out disproven): When the opponent plays a Secret, list all secrets that class could have at the current rotation, then eliminate ones disproven by observed game events (e.g., a secret that would have triggered on an attack but didn't). HDT/Firestone do this precisely because the log tells them exactly which triggers fired. On screen capture we can list candidates and eliminate on clearly-visible events, but eliminations that hinge on invisible/near-frame triggers are error-prone — must abstain rather than wrongly cross out.   - [should/low] Card-draw / next-draw probability: For each remaining card, show the probability of drawing it on the next draw / this turn (and top-of-deck odds after tutors).   - [could/medium] Discover / draft-choice stats overlay: When a Discover (or similar 3-choice) prompt appears, overlay per-option win-rate/pick stats (HSReplay 'discover choices' data; Firestone discover-stats overlay). Reliable because the three options are on-screen text/art to OCR. (recog: Detect a 3-card Discover prompt (fixed centered layout) and identify the three offered cards via OCR/vision; look up per-card stats. Abstain if any option unreadable.; compute: stats DB lookup (external discover stats))
  - [could/medium] Tavern Brawl support: Apply the deck tracker + basic stats to weekly Tavern Brawl (a constructed-adjacent mode Firestone supports). Mostly inherits the constructed pipeline; some brawls use preconstructed/random decks where own-deck import doesn't apply. (recog: Same as constructed; detect brawl mode (menu/phase classifier) and handle non-standard/random-deck brawls gracefully (disable own-deck tracker when deck is unknown).; compute: reuse of constructed pipeline)
DATA SOURCES: HSReplay.net — the de-facto external meta feed (processes ~1M+ replays/day): powers opponent archetype/deck prediction candidate decks, deck & per-class matchup win-rates, mulligan win-rate / kept-% tables, card played-when-drawn stats, and discover-choice stats. No official public data API — data must be scraped/aggregated or a licensed/mirrored snapshot synced to the LyAi backend and pushed to the app as periodic offline bundles., metastats.net-style community meta lists — alternative/back-up corpus for the deck-predictor (this is what HDT's MetaDetector/deck-predictor plugin uses)., HearthstoneJSON — bundled, dbfId-keyed card database (already in backbone): card text, class, cost, rotation/set, secret flags, generation/related-card data, locale packs (Spanish-first). Powers deck-code decode, secret pools, candidate sets, and the 'oracle' generation hints., Hearthstone deck codes — user-pasted/clipboard import: the anchor for accurate own-deck cards-left tracking on a capture-only stack (no Power.log available)., On-device observed play (MediaProjection screen capture -> ML Kit OCR + Gemini 2.5-flash vision) — the ONLY live game-state source available to DeckView; substitutes for the Power.log that HDT/Firestone rely on, hence the reduced reliability of provenance/secret/fatigue features.
PARITY GAPS: GROUND-TRUTH GAP: HDT and Firestone read Hearthstone's local Power.log / GameState (exact entity IDs, every trigger, mulligan/return/steal events). DeckView has screen capture only. This is the root cause of every gap below and cannot be closed without log access (unavailable on Android without root/instrumentation).; Card provenance / created-by / buffed-by / stolen / returned / mulliganed tags and 'how long held' — entity-level, invisible in pixels. Firestone's marquee 'what created this card' feature is effectively unsupportable; only static class-generation hints are feasible.; Exact secret elimination — depends on which hidden triggers did/didn't fire; fast animations on an adaptive capture rate will be missed. Must list candidates and abstain rather than wrongly cross out.; Fatigue / overdraw exact counts — a single missed draw/mill event desyncs the counter permanently; degrade to 'approximate' with an empty-deck visual anchor.; Lethal / optimal-attack math — requires precise reading of every minion's buffed stats, auras, taunt/divine-shield/weapon/armor; error-prone, must abstain (STABILITY-FIRST).; Exact opponent hand contents — only hand COUNT (card-back fan) is readable; individual unrevealed cards are unknown (same as any tracker) but we also lack the provenance the others show.; HSReplay has no open data API — stats must be mirrored/synced server-side and shipped as offline bundles; DeckView cannot contribute replays back (no log upload), only consume aggregates. Confirm licensing before ingesting HSReplay data (cost/ToS check per LyAi rules).
NOTES: MODE FACT-CHECK (as of 2026, per WebSearch): CONSTRUCTED = Standard (active, main format) + Wild (active). Tavern Brawl active (constructed-adjacent). Twist is being RETIRED — no further updates and removed from client in Patch 35.4 (announced April 2026); do NOT build Twist-specific features beyond flagging it. Duels was REMOVED (Oct 2020 – Apr 16 2024). Classic format was REMOVED (2023). So this lane targets Standard + Wild (+ Tavern Brawl) only. Sources: Hearthstone Wiki (hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Game_mode), GameRant Twist-retirement article, Blizzard news, HSReplay articles (articles.hsreplay.net mulligan-data), HDT deck-predictor/MetaDetector GitHubs, Firestone (firestoneapp.com / Overwolf).\n\nBUILDABILITY PRIORITY ORDER for our stack: (1) Turn/mana + Own cards-left + deck import + draw-probability — deterministic/visible, ship first. (2) Opponent play-log + archetype prediction + matchup/mulligan/deck win-rates — need external HSReplay-style bundle but only class + visible cards, high value/effort ratio. (3) Secrets helper + discover stats — medium recognition, abstain-heavy. (4) Fatigue, lethal, created-by oracle — high difficulty / low reliability on capture-only; best-effort or defer.\n\nEvery recognizer must honor abstain-on-low-confidence and never assert wrong state (PDS Gold Rule / STABILITY-FIRST). Reuse the backbone anchor-based ROI normalization + phase/mode classifier to gate which constructed overlays are active (menu vs mulligan vs in-game vs end-screen).

## MODE LANE: battlegrounds-features (status: active)
Battlegrounds is Hearthstone's flagship 8-player auto-battler and is fully active in 2026 (plus the Duos variant). Firestone/HDT-class BG parity means far more than the combat simulator: a hero-pick advisor, static minion browser + tavern-odds tables, minion-pool depletion tracking, triple tracking, opponent board scouting/history, leveling-timing advice, minion/comp tier lists, live buddy/trinket/anomaly context, and MMR/placement/session stats. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: DeckView reads only via SCREEN CAPTURE + OCR/vision, whereas Firestone reads EXACT game state from HS log files via Overwolf's Game Events Provider. That gap makes several 'signature' BG features (shared-pool depletion counts, all-8 opponents' full boards, opponents' triple progress) fundamentally hard or impossible for us — they can only be approximated from what is actually rendered on our screen (our shop/board/hand, the one combat opponent per turn, the mid-game leaderboard). We should ship the well-bounded, static-screen features (hero pick, trinket pick, odds tables, browser, your-own triples/stats) at high reliability and clearly degrade or mark the log-only features.
FEATURES:
  - [must/medium] Hero Pick Advisor: At the hero-selection screen (2-4 offered heroes), recognize each hero and overlay its BG stats: average placement, top-1 %, top-4 %, sample size, and a recommended pick. Optionally show tribe/anomaly-conditioned adjustments. This is the single highest-value, most reliable BG feature because the hero-select screen is a fixed, static layout with large portraits + names. (recog: Detect the hero-select phase (classifier gate), then OCR/vision the 2-4 hero portraits+names. Well-bounded static screen -> high reliability. Match against bundled hero DB by portrait art + name.; compute: stats-DB lookup + ranking (offline cached hero-stats table))
  - [should/medium] Trinket Pick Advisor: On the turn-6 (Lesser) and turn-9 (Greater) trinket-choice screens, recognize the 4 offered trinkets and overlay pick-rate/placement stats + a recommendation, factoring your active tribes/warband. Same shape as hero pick: a fixed choice screen, so reliable. (recog: Detect trinket-offer screen; OCR/vision the 4 trinket cards (name + text). Fixed layout -> good reliability.; compute: stats-DB lookup + context-aware ranking)
  - [should/medium] Active Anomaly + Buddy Context Panel: At game start recognize the active Anomaly (one per lobby, 19 active in patch 35.2) and show its rules + stat impact; show your hero's Buddy (Buddies returned in 2026; 75+ in pool) and how/when to leverage it. NOTE: Quests were REMOVED when Buddies returned in 2026 - do NOT build quest features (legacy flag only). (recog: OCR/vision the anomaly banner shown at game start; identify hero to derive its buddy from DB. Anomaly banner is a fixed on-screen element -> feasible.; compute: static DB lookup + optional anomaly/buddy stat overlay)
  - [should/low] Tavern Odds by Tier: For your current tavern tier (1-6), show the static published probability of a minion of each tier appearing in the shop (per-level odds table). Purely a lookup once we know your tavern tier. (recog: Read the current tavern tier number (large, fixed HUD element) -> easy/high reliability.; compute: static lookup table (no live stats needed))
  - [should/low] Tavern-Tier Minion Browser (pool browser): Browse ALL minions available this lobby, grouped by tier / tribe / mechanic, filtered to the tribes active this game, with comp/keyword highlighting. Mostly static reference content (like Firestone's cards list); no live game read required beyond knowing which tribes are in the lobby. (recog: Recognize the active tribe set (shown on the lobby/loading screen) to filter the browser; otherwise static. Feasible; degrades gracefully to 'all tribes' if unread.; compute: static DB filter/query)
  - [should/medium] Minion / Composition Tier Lists + Shop Highlights: Tier list of strongest minions and end-game comps (openings, comps to pivot to), plus an OVERLAY that highlights top-tier minions currently in YOUR shop. The tier list is static stats; the shop highlight needs live recognition of your shop. (recog: For highlights: recognize the minions in your own shop each tavern phase (your screen, but shop art is small and rotates) -> medium reliability; abstain on low confidence.; compute: static stats-DB (tier list) + on-device CV match for shop highlight)
  - [should/medium] Triple Tracking (your own): Track your progress toward Golden triples: count copies of each minion across your board + hand + (seen) shop and show 'X/3'. Reliable for YOU because it is all your own screen. Opponents' triples are NOT feasible via screen capture (flagged in parity gaps). (recog: Recognize minion identities+counts on your own board and hand each turn (your screen -> good, but overlapping/animated tokens are moderate difficulty).; compute: on-device CV tracking + simple counting state machine)
  - [should/medium] Leveling / Turn-to-Scale Timing Advisor: Advise when to level the tavern vs stay-and-tempo, based on average leveling curves by turn cross-referenced with your gold, health, and turn number. Firestone shows opponents' leveling times; we can only advise on YOUR curve reliably. (recog: OCR the HUD numerics: current turn, tavern tier, gold, health (fixed HUD positions -> feasible). Opponent leveling times require the leaderboard scout (harder, see below).; compute: heuristic + stats-backed leveling-curve model)
  - [should/high] Opponent Board Scouting & History: Record what each opponent last showed so you can plan for the rematch (Firestone's 'last board / leveling times / recent triples' on leaderboard hover). We can ONLY capture an opponent's board during the combat we fight against them (one per turn) and the brief scoreboard; store last-seen board per opponent keyed by hero portrait. This is EXACTLY the render surface flagged in the perf diagnosis (long/complex boards) - build with off-thread parse + virtualized rendering. (recog: During combat, OCR/vision the opponent's 7-minion board with per-minion stats, tribes, and buffs (animated, overlapping, buffed stats mid-combat) -> HARD, moderate reliability; capture a stable frame at combat start. Identify opponent via hero portrait on leaderboard.; compute: on-device CV capture + per-opponent state store (StateFlow); rendered via virtualized overlay)
  - [should/medium] MMR / Placement / Lobby Leaderboard Tracking: Track your BG rating over time and each game's finishing place (1-8); optionally read the mid-game lobby leaderboard (8 players + their MMR). Placement and end-of-game MMR delta are readable; other players' live MMR is small text and lower reliability. (recog: OCR final placement (large end screen -> reliable) and your MMR/delta (small text -> medium). Lobby leaderboard 8x MMR OCR -> low/medium reliability; abstain when unsure.; compute: on-device OCR + local time-series DB)
  - [should/low] Average-Placement & Session/Personal Stats: Firestone-style session recap and long-term personal stats: games played, per-game placements, average finish, last warbands, MMR change, and per-hero/per-comp personal average placement. All local aggregation of features above. (recog: Reuses placement + hero + final-board captures; no new recognition.; compute: on-device aggregation over local DB)
  - [could/high] Shared Minion Pool Depletion ('how many of X left'): Firestone's 'how many minions of each tier still in the pool' feature. HONEST ASSESSMENT: near-impossible for a screen-capture app. The pool is shared across all 8 players and depletes from buys/sells/removals we cannot observe. We can only approximate from our own buys plus minions seen on combat boards (a small fraction). Ship as an explicitly-approximate 'seen so far' counter, or defer. Firestone gets exact counts only via game logs. (recog: Would require observing every minion every player buys/sells -> unobservable via screen capture. Partial signal only from own shop/board + combat boards.; compute: on-device pool arithmetic vs static per-tier copy counts (approximate))
  - [could/high] Battlegrounds Duos Support: Duos is an active 2026 variant (4 teams of 2, shared life total, pass minions between teammates). Parity requires handling shared HP, teammate board visibility (teammate's board IS visible to you, unlike opponents), and the pass mechanic. Multiplies the recognition surface; treat as a v2 extension of the solo BG features. (recog: Detect Duos mode; recognize shared HP, teammate board, and pass UI. More on-screen state than solo BG.; compute: extends solo BG state model (shared-team state))
DATA SOURCES: Firestone (firestoneapp.com) BG hero/minion/trinket/anomaly stats, ~2M+ games, refreshed ~every 3h, HSReplay BG statistics (upstream of many tier lists), Bundled HearthstoneJSON BG card/minion set (dbfId-keyed, tier/tribe/text, Spanish-first locale packs), hearthstone.wiki.gg (anomalies, trinkets Lesser/Greater, buddy-per-hero, pool copy counts), Lii's BG probability calculator (hs-tools.github.io/bg-probabilities) + wiki odds tables for per-tier tavern odds, On-device screen-capture + ML Kit OCR + Gemini 2.5-flash vision (event-gated) for all live game-state reads, Local Room/SQLite DB for personal MMR/placement/session history, LyAi backend proxy to fetch/cache external stat tables (free tier; no per-call paid APIs)
PARITY GAPS: duplicate-removed
NOTES: Fact-check results (2026): Battlegrounds is fully active, including the Duos variant. In BG specifically as of patch 35.2 (April 14 2026): Buddies are BACK (75+ in pool), Quests were REMOVED when Buddies returned (do not build quest features), Trinkets are active (Season 13; Lesser on turn 6, Greater on turn 9; typed-trinket eligibility = 2 minions of a type on T6 / 3 on T9), and 19 Anomalies are active. Cross-mode legacy flags (not this lane but relevant to the parity mandate): Twist is being REMOVED in patch 35.4 (announced April 2026), Duels was RETIRED April 16 2024, Classic was removed 2023 — do not spec features for those except to flag them as gone. STABILITY-FIRST tie-in: the 'Opponent Board Scouting & History' feature renders long/complex minion boards and is the exact surface the existing DeckView perf diagnosis identified as freezing the UI thread — build it with off-thread parse, virtualized LazyColumn, and PrecomputedText per the backbone mandate. COST: all stat sources are free-tier (Firestone/HSReplay public data, wiki, bundled JSON); no per-call paid APIs, so no >=$0.10 authorization needed.

## MODE LANE: arena-mercs (status: active)
Two very different modes in one lane. ARENA is fully active and was overhauled in 2025-26: it now splits into "The Arena" (5 wins / 2 losses, entry 1 Tavern Ticket) and "The Underground" (unlocked after 7 Arena wins, 12 wins / 3 losses, 2 tickets, exclusive "Re-Draft on Loss"), plus rotating themes including Dual Class seasons (returned in patch 35.4, May 2026) and "Legendary Groups" drafting (a legendary bundled with 3 complementary cards). Arena is a HIGH-VALUE parity target: the flagship third-party feature is the live DRAFT PICK HELPER (tier scores + synergy) that every serious tracker (Firestone, HearthArena Companion, Arena Tracker) ships. MERCENARIES is effectively frozen: Blizzard put it into indefinite maintenance after patch 25.4 (Feb 2023) — no new content for 3+ years, low population, bug-fixes only but still playable. Recommend building Arena to full parity now and treating Mercenaries as low-priority "could" features (its data set is stable precisely because it's frozen, which lowers maintenance cost if built).
FEATURES:
  - [must/high] Arena live draft pick helper (tier scores): During the 30-pick draft, read the 3 offered cards and show a tier/win-rate score for each plus a recommended pick. This is THE flagship Arena feature every tracker ships (Firestone/HSReplay/HearthArena scores; Arena Tracker lets you choose the source). Must handle Legendary Groups (first pick = 1 legendary + 3 bundled cards) and Dual Class seasons (cards from two classes, hero-power offered first). (recog: OCR + Gemini vision to (a) detect the draft phase/screen, (b) read the 3 card names/arts and map to dbfId, (c) detect Dual Class banners and Legendary-Group layout. Screen-capture reality: the redesigned draft UI is readable but layout-fragile; recognition must be gated to the draft screen and abstain on low confidence rather than misadvise.; compute: hybrid (on-device ranking over backend-refreshed tier data))
  - [should/medium] Draft synergy & deck-composition hints: As the deck is built, show synergy callouts (tribal/mechanic combos with already-picked cards) and a live composition summary: mana curve, drop counts (2/3/4-drops), and mechanic tallies (AOE, taunt, healing, card draw, pings, removal, hard removal, reach). Directly mirrors Firestone/Arena Tracker 'mechanics summary' and 'deck score' (average of card scores). (recog: Derived from the running list of drafted cards (already known from the pick helper) + bundled card metadata; no extra screen reading needed once picks are captured.; compute: on-device)
  - [must/medium] Arena in-run deck tracker (drawn / remaining): Standard deck-tracker overlay adapted to Arena: the decklist is not preset, so it is assembled from the 30 draft picks captured above, then tracks cards drawn vs. remaining during each match of the run. Reuses the constructed-mode tracking pipeline. (recog: Requires reliable capture of all 30 draft picks first (dependency on draft helper), then per-game play/draw detection via the existing change-detector + OCR pipeline.; compute: on-device)
  - [should/medium] Hero / class pick helper: When the draft opens with a hero choice, show per-class win rates (global stats + optionally the user's personal history), as Firestone/Arena Tracker do. In Dual Class seasons this covers the two-class banner selection. (recog: Detect the hero-offer screen and read the offered classes/heroes. Fragile across seasonal reskins; gate and abstain on low confidence.; compute: hybrid (data-lookup + local personal stats))
  - [should/medium] Run record, rewards & mode-context tracking: Track wins/losses of the current run and the win/loss/reward history across runs, stored locally and segmented over time (Arena Tracker keeps stats in 2-month periods). Must understand the mode context: The Arena (5W/2L) vs The Underground (12W/3L, unlocked after 7 Arena wins) and surface Underground-specific rewards (e.g. 'Crowd's Favor' gold at 6+ wins, cosmetic at 12). (recog: Read win/loss end screens and the run-progress/staging screen to increment the record. Reward-screen OCR (exact packs/gold/tickets) is unreliable via screen capture — capture win count reliably, treat exact reward contents as best-effort.; compute: on-device)
  - [could/high] Underground Re-Draft on Loss assistant: Underground-exclusive: after a loss you may draft 5 new cards to modify the deck. The helper should surface the deck's 5 weakest cards (as Arena Tracker does) and score the re-draft offers, then update the in-run tracker's decklist. (recog: Detect the re-draft screen (distinct from initial draft), read the 5 offers, and reconcile the swapped cards into the tracked decklist — extra state-machine complexity on top of normal drafting.; compute: hybrid)
  - [should/medium] Arena tier-list / current-set awareness: Keep the tier/win-rate data current for the live Arena card pool (which rotates and is curated per season, e.g. Dual-Class-curated pools, and gets balance nerfs like the July 2026 Herald appearance-rate cut). The scores that power the draft helper must be refreshed from a data feed rather than bundled statically. (recog: No on-device recognition; this is a data-freshness/backend concern. Flag: depends on third-party sources (HSReplay/HearthArena/Firestone) — see parity gaps for ToS/cost considerations.; compute: backend-proxy (periodic data refresh))
  - [could/high] Mercenaries combat: party & ability tracker: During Mercenaries turn-based combat, surface the abilities available to the up-to-3 active mercs and their info (damage, effect). Reference trackers do light versions of this. LOW PRIORITY — Mercenaries has been in maintenance mode since Feb 2023 (patch 25.4) with a small population. (recog: Read merc portraits and ability icons from a bespoke, icon-dense combat UI and map to a Mercenaries data set. Recognition is much harder than card OCR; abstain heavily. Mode is frozen so the data set is stable, but ROI is low.; compute: on-device (data-lookup))
  - [could/high] Mercenaries speed / initiative order prediction: Combat resolves selected abilities from lowest to highest Speed; predict the execution order once both sides' abilities are chosen. Genuinely useful but bounded: Speed ties are resolved RANDOMLY, so exact ordering is impossible in tie cases — must present as probabilistic, not certain. (recog: Must read each merc's chosen ability and its Speed value every turn (your side is visible; opponent's chosen abilities are hidden until revealed). Partial-information + random tie-breaks cap accuracy — say so rather than over-promise.; compute: on-device)
  - [could/high] Mercenaries ability cooldown tracker: Track per-ability cooldowns across turns so the player knows when an ability is available again. Companion to the ability tracker. (recog: Requires accurately identifying which ability each merc used each turn (see ability tracker caveats) and modelling cooldown state — error-prone if any turn's read is missed.; compute: on-device)
  - [could/medium] Mercenaries treasure / equipment info: After fights you pick one Treasure for a surviving merc (stat boosts, passives, or new abilities, lasting only that Bounty). Show what each offered Treasure does, and reference equipment info. Lookup against a Mercenaries data set. (recog: Detect the treasure-offer screen and read the offered treasures. Screen is readable (text-heavy) but requires a community Mercenaries treasure database (not in HearthstoneJSON).; compute: on-device (data-lookup))
  - [could/high] Mercenaries village task tracker: Track the 18-task quest chains per merc (new tasks at the Campfire). Even the best trackers do this poorly: Firestone only remembers tasks seen/completed while the app was running and shows question marks otherwise. This is a HARD/UNRELIABLE feature by nature. (recog: There is no way to read full task state from a single screen; it must be reconstructed by observing Campfire/task screens over time. Screen-capture reality: cannot reliably reconstruct historical task progress — replicate Firestone's honest 'unknown until seen' behavior.; compute: on-device (local persistence))
  - [could/high] Mercenaries PvE/PvP bounty helper: For bounty runs, preview known enemy compositions / encounter info and suggest counters. Nice-to-have PvE aid. (recog: Detect the bounty map/encounter and read enemy merc lineup; relies on a static community bounty dataset. Low ROI given the mode's frozen, low-population status.; compute: on-device (data-lookup))
DATA SOURCES: HearthstoneJSON (bundled card DB, dbfId-keyed) — covers Arena constructed cards but NOT Mercenaries mercs/abilities/treasures, HSReplay.net — Arena card win-rates, hero/class win-rates, played-vs-included win-rate (third-party; ToS/rate-limit/cost considerations), HearthArena tier list — the classic Arena draft tier scores (third-party), Firestone data feeds — Arena card scores and Mercenaries progression data (community/third-party), supertriodo/Arena-Tracker (open source) — reference implementation of draft scoring, mechanics summary, redraft weakest-5, opponent tracking, Blizzard official patch notes (35.4 / 35.6 / 36.0) & 'Arena Expands With Underground' news post — authoritative mode structure (win/loss caps, tickets, Dual Class, Legendary Groups, Re-Draft on Loss), Hearthstone Wiki (wiki.gg and fandom) — Mercenaries mechanics, merc/ability/treasure/task data (needed because no official Mercenaries API exists), Community Mercenaries datasets (e.g. Firestone/zerotoheroes exports) — merc abilities, speed values, treasures, bounty encounters; stable because the mode is frozen
PARITY GAPS: Arena draft-offer recognition is the make-or-break dependency: everything (pick helper, synergy, in-run tracker) rests on reliably reading the 3 (or 4-in-Legendary-Group) offered cards via screen capture. Feasible but UI-fragile across seasonal reskins (Dual Class banners, Legendary Groups) — must gate to the draft screen and abstain on low confidence to honor STABILITY-FIRST.; Reward-screen contents (exact packs/gold/tickets/cosmetics) are hard to OCR reliably; capture win/loss counts robustly and treat precise reward amounts as best-effort.; Arena tier/win-rate scores have no official Blizzard API — they depend on third-party sources (HSReplay/HearthArena/Firestone) which carry ToS, attribution, rate-limit and potential cost implications; must be proxied through the LyAi backend and may need a licensing/cost decision (flag to Ignacio if any source is paid).; Mercenaries is in indefinite maintenance since patch 25.4 (Feb 2023) — no content updates for 3+ years, low population. Recommend it be a low-priority 'could' tier, not blocking Arena parity. Upside: the frozen data set won't drift, so a one-time build stays valid.; Mercenaries speed-order prediction cannot be exact because Speed ties resolve randomly and the opponent's chosen abilities are hidden until revealed — present as probabilistic, never certain.; Mercenaries village task progress cannot be reconstructed from screen capture alone (even Firestone only knows tasks seen while running). Replicate the honest 'unknown until observed' behavior rather than fabricate state.; Mercenaries combat UI is icon-dense and bespoke; ability/treasure/cooldown recognition is materially harder than card OCR and should abstain aggressively.; No Mercenaries data in HearthstoneJSON — a separate community-sourced Mercenaries DB (mercs, abilities, speeds, treasures, bounties) must be bundled to enable any Mercenaries feature.
NOTES: MIXED STATUS within this lane — the single modeStatus field is set to 'active' because Arena (the dominant, high-value target) is fully active and recently expanded, but Mercenaries is 'seasonal/maintenance': playable, bug-fix-only, no content since Feb 2023, low population. Concrete recommendation: build ARENA to full parity in v1.5 (draft pick helper + synergy + composition + in-run tracker + run record + Arena/Underground mode awareness, with Re-Draft-on-Loss and current-set tier freshness as fast-follows), and DEFER Mercenaries to a later optional module gated behind whether Ignacio wants to chase that shrinking audience. Fact-check of 2026 mode list (verified against Blizzard news + wiki): live modes are Play/Constructed (Standard, Wild, Twist), Battlegrounds, Arena (with The Underground sub-mode), Tavern Brawl, and Mercenaries (maintenance). Deprecated/removed modes NOT to spec: Duels (retired 2024) and Classic (removed 2023) — neither is in this lane but flagged per instructions. All third-party data feeds must route through the LyAi backend proxy and stay on free tiers unless a >= $0.10 cost is authorized. Sources: hearthstone.blizzard.com/news/24208800 (Underground), 35.4 patch notes (Dual Class), blizzardwatch.com 2023-02-07 (Mercenaries maintenance), triodo.gitbook.io Arena-Tracker docs & github supertriodo/Arena-Tracker (feature reference), hearthstone.wiki.gg Game_mode (2026 mode list).

## MODE LANE: other-modes (status: active)
Authoritative 2026 mode census for the "other modes" lane. ACTIVE modes: Play/Constructed (Standard + Wild only), Battlegrounds (+ Duos), Arena, Tavern Brawl, and Mercenaries (in permanent maintenance mode). Access points Practice (vs AI) and Friendly Challenge reuse the constructed pipeline. CRITICAL CORRECTION vs the backbone assumptions: TWIST WAS REMOVED from the client in Patch 35.4 (~May 5, 2026) — do NOT spec Twist deck-tracking; its experimental-format role moved into rotating Tavern Brawls. For Tavern Brawl, real trackers (Firestone/HDT) do almost nothing mode-specific because brawls rotate weekly and frequently use pre-built or random decks — so honest parity here is a mode-gate plus a generic observed-card overlay, NOT a per-brawl decklist database. The only Brawl variant worth full tracking is Brawliseum/Heroic Brawl, which uses a player-built constructed deck and folds cleanly into the constructed tracker.
FEATURES:
  - [must/medium] Mode gate: Tavern Brawl / Practice / Friendly detection: Extend the phase/mode classifier so recognition knows when the board is a Tavern Brawl, a Practice (vs-AI) game, or a Friendly Challenge, versus ladder constructed. This is a stability gate: it prevents the constructed deck-tracker from firing against a deck it cannot possibly know (pre-built/random brawls), which otherwise produces confidently-wrong overlays. Gate on the mode-select/lobby screens and in-match chrome. (recog: Anchor-ROI classifier on lobby banners + in-match chrome; OCR of the mode/brawl title text. No card recognition required for the gate itself.; compute: on-device)
  - [should/high] Brawl-type auto-classification (prebuilt / deckbuilding / PvE): Within Tavern Brawl, decide whether card-tracking is even meaningful. Deckbuilding brawls and Brawliseum use a real constructed deck (trackable); pre-built-deck brawls give both players a fixed/mirror deck (partially known, low value); PvE/random-effect brawls are untrackable. Classification decides which overlay (if any) to show — abstain and show nothing rather than garbage. (recog: OCR brawl title + heuristic on early-game state (does the player choose/draft cards? is there a deckbuild step?). DeckView has ONLY MediaProjection screen capture — no log access. This is the single most important constraint: everything that depends on invisible or entity-level state (card provenance/created-by, stolen/returned/mulliganed tracking, exact secret elimination via hidden triggers, precise fatigue counting) is either much harder or must abstain. Deterministic/visible features (own cards-left, mana/turn, draw probability) are reliable; stats-DB features (opponent archetype prediction, mulligan/matchup win-rates) are reliable because they only need class + visibly-played cards + an external meta feed (HSReplay-style). (recog: Recognize minion identities+counts on your own board and hand each turn (your screen -> good, but overlapping/animated tokens are moderate difficulty).; compute: on-device CV tracking + simple counting state machine)
  - [should/medium] Leveling / Turn-to-Scale Timing Advisor: Advise when to level the tavern vs stay-and-tempo, based on average leveling curves by turn cross-referenced with your gold, health, and turn number. Firestone shows opponents' leveling times; we can only advise on YOUR curve reliably. (recog: OCR the HUD numerics: current turn, tavern tier, gold, health (fixed HUD positions -> feasible). Opponent leveling times require the leaderboard scout (harder, see below).; compute: heuristic + stats-backed leveling-curve model)
  - [should/high] Opponent Board Scouting & History: Record what each opponent last showed so you can plan for the rematch (Firestone's 'last board / leveling times / recent triples' on leaderboard hover). We can ONLY capture an opponent's board during the combat we fight against them (one per turn) and the brief scoreboard; store last-seen board per opponent keyed by hero portrait. This is EXACTLY the render surface flagged in the perf diagnosis (long/complex boards) - build with off-thread parse + virtualized rendering. (recog: During combat, OCR/vision the opponent's 7-minion board with per-minion stats, tribes, and buffs (animated, overlapping, buffed stats mid-combat) -> HARD, moderate reliability; capture a stable frame at combat start. Identify opponent via hero portrait on leaderboard.; compute: on-device CV capture + per-opponent state store (StateFlow); rendered via virtualized overlay)
  - [should/medium] MMR / Placement / Lobby Leaderboard Tracking: Track your BG rating over time and each game's finishing place (1-8); optionally read the mid-game lobby leaderboard (8 players + their MMR). Placement and end-of-game MMR delta are readable; other players' live MMR is small text and lower reliability. (recog: OCR final placement (large end screen -> reliable) and your MMR/delta (small text -> medium). Lobby leaderboard 8x MMR OCR -> low/medium reliability; abstain when unsure.; compute: on-device OCR + local time-series DB)
  - [should/low] Average-Placement & Session/Personal Stats: Firestone-style session recap and long-term personal stats: games played, per-game placements, average finish, last warbands, MMR change, and per-hero/per-comp personal average placement. All local aggregation of features above. (recog: Reuses placement + hero + final-board captures; no new recognition.; compute: on-device aggregation over local DB)
  - [could/high] Shared Minion Pool Depletion ('how many of X left'): Firestone's 'how many minions of each tier still in the pool' feature. HONEST ASSESSMENT: near-impossible for a screen-capture app. The pool is shared across all 8 players and depletes from buys/sells/removals we cannot observe. We can only approximate from our own buys plus minions seen on combat boards (a small fraction). Ship as an explicitly-approximate 'seen so far' counter, or defer. Firestone gets exact counts only via game logs. (recog: Would require observing every minion every player buys/sells -> unobservable via screen capture. Partial signal only from own shop/board + combat boards.; compute: on-device pool arithmetic vs static per-tier copy counts (approximate))
  - [could/high] Battlegrounds Duos Support: Duos is an active 2026 variant (4 teams of 2, shared life total, pass minions between teammates). Parity requires handling shared HP, teammate board visibility (teammate's board IS visible to you, unlike opponents), and the pass mechanic. Multiplies the recognition surface; treat as a v2 extension of the solo BG features. (recog: Detect Duos mode; recognize shared HP, teammate board, and pass UI. More on-screen state than solo BG.; compute: extends solo BG state model (shared-team state))
DATA SOURCES: Firestone (firestoneapp.com) BG hero/minion/trinket/anomaly stats, ~2M+ games, refreshed ~every 3h, HSReplay BG statistics (upstream of many tier lists), Bundled HearthstoneJSON BG card/minion set (dbfId-keyed, tier/tribe/text, Spanish-first locale packs), hearthstone.wiki.gg (anomalies, trinkets Lesser/Greater, buddy-per-hero, pool copy counts), Lii's BG probability calculator (hs-tools.github.io/bg-probabilities) + wiki odds tables for per-tier tavern odds, On-device screen-capture + ML Kit OCR + Gemini 2.5-flash vision (event-gated) for all live game-state reads, Local Room/SQLite DB for personal MMR/placement/session history, LyAi backend proxy to fetch/cache external stat tables (free tier; no per-call paid APIs)
PARITY GAPS: duplicate-removed
NOTES: Fact-check results (2026): Battlegrounds is fully active, including the Duos variant. In BG specifically as of patch 35.2 (April 14 2026): Buddies are BACK (75+ in pool), Quests were REMOVED when Buddies returned (do not build quest features), Trinkets are active (Season 13; Lesser on turn 6, Greater on turn 9; typed-trinket eligibility = 2 minions of a type on T6 / 3 on T9), and 19 Anomalies are active. Cross-mode legacy flags (not this lane but relevant to the parity mandate): Twist is being REMOVED in patch 35.4 (announced April 2026), Duels was RETIRED April 16 2024, Classic was removed 2023 — do not spec features for those except to flag them as gone. STABILITY-FIRST tie-in: the 'Opponent Board Scouting & History' feature renders long/complex minion boards and is the exact surface the existing DeckView perf diagnosis identified as freezing the UI thread — build it with off-thread parse, virtualized LazyColumn, and PrecomputedText per the backbone mandate. COST: all stat sources are free-tier (Firestone/HSReplay public data, wiki, bundled JSON); no per-call paid APIs, so no >=$0.10 authorization needed.

## MODE LANE: arena-mercs (status: active)
Two very different modes in one lane. ARENA is fully active and was overhauled in 2025-26: it now splits into "The Arena" (5 wins / 2 losses, entry 1 Tavern Ticket) and "The Underground" (unlocked after 7 Arena wins, 12 wins / 3 losses, 2 tickets, exclusive "Re-Draft on Loss"), plus rotating themes including Dual Class seasons (returned in patch 35.4, May 2026) and "Legendary Groups" drafting (a legendary bundled with 3 complementary cards). Arena is a HIGH-VALUE parity target: the flagship third-party feature is the live DRAFT PICK HELPER (tier scores + synergy) that every serious tracker (Firestone, HearthArena Companion, Arena Tracker) ships. MERCENARIES is effectively frozen: Blizzard put it into indefinite maintenance after patch 25.4 (Feb 2023) — no new content for 3+ years, low population, bug-fixes only but still playable. Recommend building Arena to full parity now and treating Mercenaries as low-priority "could" features (its data set is stable precisely because it's frozen, which lowers maintenance cost if built).
FEATURES:
  - [must/high] Arena live draft pick helper (tier scores): During the 30-pick draft, read the 3 offered cards and show a tier/win-rate score for each plus a recommended pick. This is THE flagship Arena feature every tracker ships (Firestone/HSReplay/HearthArena scores; Arena Tracker lets you choose the source). Must handle Legendary Groups (first pick = 1 legendary + 3 bundled cards) and Dual Class seasons (cards from two classes, hero-power offered first). (recog: OCR + Gemini vision to (a) detect the draft phase/screen, (b) read the 3 card names/arts and map to dbfId, (c) detect Dual Class banners and Legendary-Group layout. Screen-capture reality: the redesigned draft UI is readable but layout-fragile; recognition must be gated to the draft screen and abstain on low confidence rather than misadvise.; compute: hybrid (on-device ranking over backend-refreshed tier data))
  - [should/medium] Draft synergy & deck-composition hints: As the deck is built, show synergy callouts (tribal/mechanic combos with already-picked cards) and a live composition summary: mana curve, drop counts (2/3/4-drops), and mechanic tallies (AOE, taunt, healing, card draw, pings, removal, hard removal, reach). Directly mirrors Firestone/Arena Tracker 'mechanics summary' and 'deck score' (average of card scores). (recog: Derived from the running list of drafted cards (already known from the pick helper) + bundled card metadata; no extra screen reading needed once picks are captured.; compute: on-device)
  - [must/medium] Arena in-run deck tracker (drawn / remaining): Standard deck-tracker overlay adapted to Arena: the decklist is not preset, so it is assembled from the 30 draft picks captured above, then tracks cards drawn vs. remaining during each match of the run. Reuses the constructed-mode tracking pipeline. (recog: Requires reliable capture of all 30 draft picks first (dependency on draft helper), then per-game play/draw detection via the existing change-detector + OCR pipeline.; compute: on-device)
  - [should/medium] Hero / class pick helper: When the draft opens with a hero choice, show per-class win rates (global stats + optionally the user's personal history), as Firestone/Arena Tracker do. In Dual Class seasons this covers the two-class banner selection. (recog: Detect the hero-offer screen and read the offered classes/heroes. Fragile across seasonal reskins; gate and abstain on low confidence.; compute: hybrid (data-lookup + local personal stats))
  - [should/medium] Run record, rewards & mode-context tracking: Track wins/losses of the current run and the win/loss/reward history across runs, stored locally and segmented over time (Arena Tracker keeps stats in 2-month periods). Must understand the mode context: The Arena (5W/2L) vs The Underground (12W/3L, unlocked after 7 Arena wins) and surface Underground-specific rewards (e.g. 'Crowd's Favor' gold at 6+ wins, cosmetic at 12). (recog: Read win/loss end screens and the run-progress/staging screen to increment the record. Reward-screen OCR (exact packs/gold/tickets) is unreliable via screen capture — capture win count reliably, treat exact reward contents as best-effort.; compute: on-device)
  - [could/high] Underground Re-Draft on Loss assistant: Underground-exclusive: after a loss you may draft 5 new cards to modify the deck. The helper should surface the deck's 5 weakest cards (as Arena Tracker does) and score the re-draft offers, then update the in-run tracker's decklist. (recog: Detect the re-draft screen (distinct from initial draft), read the 5 offers, and reconcile the swapped cards into the tracked decklist — extra state-machine complexity on top of normal drafting.; compute: hybrid)
  - [should/medium] Arena tier-list / current-set awareness: Keep the tier/win-rate data current for the live Arena card pool (which rotates and is curated per season, e.g. Dual-Class-curated pools, and gets balance nerfs like the July 2026 Herald appearance-rate cut). The scores that power the draft helper must be refreshed from a data feed rather than bundled statically. (recog: No on-device recognition; this is a data-freshness/backend concern. Flag: depends on third-party sources (HSReplay/HearthArena/Firestone) — see parity gaps for ToS/cost considerations.; compute: backend-proxy (periodic data refresh))
  - [could/high] Mercenaries combat: party & ability tracker: During Mercenaries turn-based combat, surface the abilities available to the up-to-3 active mercs and their info (damage, effect). (recog: Read merc portraits and ability icons from a bespoke, icon-dense combat UI and map to a Mercenaries data set. Recognition is much harder than card OCR; abstain heavily.   - [could/high] Mercenaries speed / initiative order prediction: Combat resolves selected abilities from lowest to highest Speed; predict the execution order once both sides' abilities are chosen. Genuinely useful but bounded: Speed ties are resolved RANDOMLY, so exact ordering is impossible in tie cases — must present as probabilistic, not certain. (recog: Must read each merc's chosen ability and its Speed value every turn (your side is visible; opponent's chosen abilities are hidden until revealed). Partial-information + random tie-breaks cap accuracy — say so rather than over-promise.; compute: on-device)
  - [could/high] Mercenaries ability cooldown tracker: Track per-ability cooldowns across turns so the player knows when an ability is available again. Companion to the ability tracker. (recog: Requires accurately identifying which ability each merc used each turn (see ability tracker caveats) and modelling cooldown state — error-prone if any turn's read is missed.; compute: on-device)
  - [could/medium] Mercenaries treasure / equipment info: After fights you pick one Treasure for a surviving merc (stat boosts, passives, or new abilities, lasting only that Bounty). Show what each offered Treasure does, and reference equipment info. Lookup against a Mercenaries data set. (recog: Detect the treasure-offer screen and read the offered treasures. Screen is readable (text-heavy) but requires a community Mercenaries treasure database (not in HearthstoneJSON).; compute: on-device (data-lookup))
  - [could/high] Mercenaries village task tracker: Track the 18-task quest chains per merc (new tasks at the Campfire). Even the best trackers do this poorly: Firestone only remembers tasks seen/completed while the app was running and shows question marks otherwise. This is a HARD/UNRELIABLE feature by nature. (recog: There is no way to read full task state from a single screen; it must be reconstructed by observing Campfire/task screens over time. Screen-capture reality: cannot reliably reconstruct historical task progress — replicate Firestone's honest 'unknown until seen' behavior.; compute: on-device (local persistence))
  - [could/high] Mercenaries PvE/PvP bounty helper: For bounty runs, preview known enemy compositions / encounter info and suggest counters. Nice-to-have PvE aid. (recog: Detect the bounty map/encounter and read enemy merc lineup; relies on a static community bounty dataset. Low ROI given the mode's frozen, low-population status.; compute: on-device (data-lookup))
DATA SOURCES: HearthstoneJSON (bundled card DB, dbfId-keyed) — covers Arena constructed cards but NOT Mercenaries mercs/abilities/treasures, HSReplay.net — Arena card win-rates, hero/class win-rates, played-vs-included win-rate (third-party; ToS/rate-limit/cost considerations), HearthArena tier list — the classic Arena draft tier scores (third-party), Firestone data feeds — Arena card scores and Mercenaries progression data (community/third-party), supertriodo/Arena-Tracker (open source) — reference implementation of draft scoring, mechanics summary, redraft weakest-5, opponent tracking, Blizzard official patch notes (35.4 / 35.6 / 36.0) & 'Arena Expands With Underground' news post — authoritative mode structure (win/loss caps, tickets, Dual Class, Legendary Groups, Re-Draft on Loss), Hearthstone Wiki (wiki.gg and fandom) — Mercenaries mechanics, merc/ability/treasure/task data (needed because no official Mercenaries API exists), Community Mercenaries datasets (e.g. Firestone/zerotoheroes exports) — merc abilities, speed values, treasures, bounty encounters; stable because the mode is frozen

Feasible but UI-fragile across seasonal reskins (Dual Class banners, Legendary Groups) — must gate to the draft screen and abstain on low confidence to honor STABILITY-FIRST.; Reward-screen contents (exact packs/gold/tickets/cosmetics) are hard to OCR reliably; capture win/loss counts robustly and treat precise reward amounts as best-effort.; Arena tier/win-rate scores have no official Blizzard API — they depend on third-party sources (HSReplay/HearthArena/Firestone) which carry ToS, attribution, rate-limit and potential cost implications; must be proxied through the LyAi backend and may need a licensing/cost decision (flag to Ignacio if any source is paid).; Mercenaries is in indefinite maintenance since patch 25.4 (Feb 2023) — no content updates for 3+ years, low population. Replicate the honest 'unknown until observed' behavior rather than fabricate state.; Mercenaries combat UI is icon-dense and bespoke; ability/treasure/cooldown recognition is materially harder than card OCR and should abstain aggressively.; No Mercenaries data in HearthstoneJSON — a separate community-sourced Mercenaries DB (mercs, abilities, speeds, treasures, bounties) must be bundled to enable any Mercenaries feature.
