## MODE LANE: other-modes (status: active)
Authoritative 2026 mode census for the "other modes" lane. ACTIVE modes: Play/Constructed (Standard + Wild only), Battlegrounds (+ Duos), Arena, Tavern Brawl, and Mercenaries (in permanent maintenance mode). Access points Practice (vs AI) and Friendly Challenge reuse the constructed pipeline. CRITICAL CORRECTION vs the backbone assumptions: TWIST WAS REMOVED from the client in Patch 35.4 (~May 5, 2026) — do NOT spec Twist deck-tracking; its experimental-format role moved into rotating Tavern Brawls. For Tavern Brawl, real trackers (Firestone/HDT) do almost nothing mode-specific because brawls rotate weekly and frequently use pre-built or random decks — so honest parity here is a mode-gate plus a generic observed-card overlay, NOT a per-brawl decklist database. The only Brawl variant worth full tracking is Brawliseum/Heroic Brawl, which uses a player-built constructed deck and folds cleanly into the constructed tracker.
FEATURES:
  - [must/medium] Mode gate: Tavern Brawl / Practice / Friendly detection: Extend the phase/mode classifier so recognition knows when the board is a Tavern Brawl, a Practice (vs-AI) game, or a Friendly Challenge, versus ladder constructed. This is a stability gate: it prevents the constructed deck-tracker from firing against a deck it cannot possibly know (pre-built/random brawls), which otherwise produces confidently-wrong overlays. Gate on the mode-select/lobby screens and in-match chrome. (recog: Anchor-ROI classifier on lobby banners + in-match chrome; OCR of the mode/brawl title text. No card recognition required for the gate itself.; compute: on-device)
  - [should/high] Brawl-type auto-classification (prebuilt / deckbuilding / PvE): Within Tavern Brawl, decide whether card-tracking is even meaningful. Deckbuilding brawls and Brawliseum use a real constructed deck (trackable); pre-built-deck brawls give both players a fixed/mirror deck (partially known, low value); PvE/random-effect brawls are untrackable. Classification decides which overlay (if any) to show — abstain and show nothing rather than garbage. (recog: OCR brawl title + heuristic on early-game state (does the player choose/draft cards? is there a deckbuild step?). Optionally a small bundled lookup of known brawl IDs to their type, refreshed from community data.; compute: on-device)
  - [should/low] Brawliseum / Heroic Brawl run tracking (constructed reuse): Brawliseum and Heroic Brawl are paid-entry, Arena-style runs where the player brings a self-built CONSTRUCTED deck and plays until 12 wins or 3 losses. Reuse the full constructed deck-tracker (drawn/remaining, mulligan) since the deck IS known/importable, and add an Arena-style run scoreboard (current wins/losses tally read from the run screen). Highest-value Tavern Brawl feature and cheap because it rides the constructed pipeline. (recog: Existing constructed recognition + OCR of the run wins/losses counter on the Brawliseum result/key screen.; compute: on-device)
  - [could/high] Generic mode-agnostic observed-card overlay (Brawl fallback): For deckbuilding/other brawls where no imported decklist exists, provide the honest fallback that also matters for parity everywhere: log cards the PLAYER has played/drawn and cards the OPPONENT has revealed, as an observed set — not a diff against a known list. This is the only card-tracking realistically possible in most brawls and doubles as the generic opponent-tracker used in every mode. (recog: Per-card recognition (ML Kit OCR + Gemini vision, event-gated, abstain-on-low-confidence) of cards as they enter play/hand; no candidate-set constraint available, so accuracy is lower — surface as 'seen', never as 'remaining'.; compute: hybrid)
  - [could/medium] Weekly brawl identification + info card in chat: Read the current brawl's name and surface a grounded chat/HUD note: what the rules are, whether it's PvP/PvE, whether it rewards a pack, and rotation history. Low mechanical value but cheap product polish; leverages the Gemini chat backbone. Data is community-sourced (no official current-brawl API). (recog: OCR the brawl title, fuzzy-match to a bundled/periodically-refreshed brawl catalog (hearthstone.wiki.gg Tavern Brawl list).; compute: hybrid)
  - [should/low] Practice mode (vs AI) full support + internal QA harness: Practice games (Normal/Expert vs the computer) use ordinary constructed decks, so the constructed tracker works fully and OFFLINE. Beyond being a real user feature, Practice is the safest environment to develop and regression-test the entire constructed recognition pipeline with zero ladder/ranked risk — recommend wiring the spike capture harness here first. (recog: Identical to constructed; no new recognition. Detect the vs-AI context via the Practice lobby/gate.; compute: on-device)
  - [should/low] Friendly Challenge support: Friend games use player-chosen constructed decks (Standard or Wild). Reuse the constructed tracker for the player's own (importable) deck; opponent handled by the generic observed-card overlay. No new pipeline; just ensure the mode gate whitelists Friendly so tracking activates. (recog: Constructed recognition; gate on the Friendly Challenge lobby.; compute: on-device)
  - [could/medium] Ranked-vs-Casual awareness + rank medal read: Ranked and Casual within Play mode are recognition-identical (same decks/cards); the only difference is matchmaking and rank. Optionally OCR the rank medal / Legend number so session stats and the AI chat can be rank-aware ('you're 4-1 at Diamond 5 this session'). Purely additive context, not required for card tracking. Zero parity work — do not spec Twist deck-tracking. If Blizzard revives Twist-style formats it will arrive as rotating Tavern Brawl content and fold into the Brawl handling above.; Mercenaries: still playable but in permanent MAINTENANCE MODE (no content since Patch 25.4). Not a deck game (RPG/party combat) — reference trackers offer little/nothing; recommend explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for v-parity beyond a mode-gate that suppresses the constructed overlay.; No official API exposes the current weekly brawl or its ruleset — brawl identification must rely on bundled community data + OCR, so it can lag on a brand-new brawl.

=== BG SIM RESEARCH ===
## BG COMBAT SIMULATOR RESEARCH
Summary: DeckView's Battlegrounds combat simulator is the flagship "win %" feature: given both warbands at the moment combat starts, it estimates win/tie/loss probability, expected damage, and lethal chance. It is a Monte Carlo engine that fully plays out the auto-battle N times (randomness = attack-target selection, random summons/buffs, start-of-combat ordering, first-attacker tie-break) and aggregates outcomes. It runs entirely off the UI thread in pure Kotlin and is CPU-cheap (1-2k sims in well under 100 ms). Its real limit is RECOGNITION ACCURACY, not compute: your own board is known perfectly from the tracked game state, but the enemy board is only visible for a brief pre-combat window and hidden enchantments/subtle keywords are frequently unreadable, so a Firestone-style manual board editor plus confidence-gated abstention is mandatory. Mode fact-check (2026): Battlegrounds is a live first-class mode with a Duos variant (4 teams of 2, shared life, teammate-support minions); Duels was retired 2024, Classic removed 2023, and Twist was discontinued in Patch 35.4 (Apr 2026) — do NOT spec simulator features for retired modes.
Algorithm: MONTE CARLO full-combat rollout, the same family as twanvl's simulator, Firestone, and HDT's BG simulator. (1) Build an immutable CombatSnapshot from the GameStateStore (your board = perfect info) + the recognized/edited enemy board, plus both hero powers and start-of-combat effects. (2) For each of N iterations: deep-copy the snapshot into a pooled mutable working state seeded from a fast PRNG (SplitMix64/Xoshiro, NOT java.util.Random); resolve START-OF-COMBAT (hero powers + minions like Red Whelp / Prized Promoter / Deflect-o-Bot, ordered by tavern tier then random within a tier), then run the attack loop until one or both boards are empty, or a hard attack cap (~500) forces a declared TIE (guards windfury/Macaw/Scallywag infinite chains). (3) Attack loop: first attacker = side with more minions (tie = coin flip); sides alternate, each keeping a next-attacker pointer that advances left-to-right, skips 0-attack/dead minions, and wraps. Attacker picks a target at random among enemy Taunts if any exist, else any enemy (special cases: Zapp = lowest attack). Both minions deal Attack to the other's Health simultaneously; Divine Shield absorbs one hit, Poisonous/Venomous kills on any damage dealt, Cleave also hits the target's neighbors, Overkill/on-damage triggers fire. Resolve deaths in board order, firing Deathrattles (x2 under Baron Rivendare), Reborn, Avenge counters, and after-a-friendly-dies/attacks chains (Macaw re-triggers a friendly deathrattle; Scallywag summons a pirate that attacks immediately). (4) Aggregate: win/tie/loss counts -> percentages, a damage histogram (damage = winner's remaining minion star-tier sum + winner hero's tavern tier), expected damage taken/dealt, and P(you die)/P(opponent dies). Report a 95% CI so the UI can show '~62% (±2%)'. Optimization: a determinism detector short-circuits to ONE rollout when the combat has no RNG nodes (e.g. a single forced taunt line, no random summons), common late-game.
Rules to model: Attack order: first attacker = more minions (tie random); alternate sides; per-side next-attacker pointer advancing left-to-right, wrapping, skipping 0-attack/dead minions.; Target selection: random among enemy Taunts if any, else random enemy; Zapp Slywick = lowest attack; other forced-target effects.; Divine Shield (absorbs one damage instance), Taunt, Poisonous/Venomous (lethal on any damage), Windfury/Mega-Windfury (extra attacks), Reborn (resummon at 1 HP), Stealth.; Cleave (hits target + neighbors), adjacency buffs, and combat-active auras.; Deathrattles resolved in board order; Baron Rivendare doubles them; Reborn interplay; summon placement (tokens appear adjacent to the source).; Triggered chains: on-attack / after-friendly-attacks (Monstrous Macaw re-triggers a friendly deathrattle), after-a-minion-dies, Avenge counters, Scallywag pirate that attacks immediately, summon-triggered effects (Khadgar doubles summons).; Start-of-combat phase: hero powers and minions (Red Whelp damage, Prized Promoter, Deflect-o-Bot, Illidan) fire before attacks, ordered by tavern tier then random within a tier — a major pre-combat randomness source.; Blood gems: already merged into displayed stats, so treat as static; only model pending/aura gem effects if known.; Acceptable approximations: uncommon/unmodeled cards fall back to vanilla stats+keywords and are FLAGGED; exact simultaneous-death trigger ordering can differ slightly from live (twanvl notes the same caveat) — acceptable if disclosed.; Duos-specific: shared team life and cross-board teammate-support minions (Grave Narrator Avenge, Support System Divine Shield) — model as its own combat variant, not a bolt-on.
Existing art: twanvl/hearthstone-battlegrounds-simulator — canonical open-source C++ Monte Carlo battle simulator (web build at twanvl.nl/hsbg via emscripten); README explicitly notes 'there might be subtle differences in the order of triggers' — the honest baseline for approximation., Firestone — full tracker whose BG simulator runs locally with a user-adjustable accuracy/iteration slider and a drag-and-drop board editor to correct/experiment (the manual-correct fallback pattern DeckView should copy); Firestone's simulator is open-sourced., HearthSim / Hearthstone Deck Tracker — BG simulator showing win/tie/loss %; GitHub issue #4068 discusses how its simulation works and its accuracy caveats., Academic MCTS work (Central Michigan thesis 'Hearthstone Battleground: An AI Assistant with Monte Carlo Tree Search', 2021) and peter1591/hearthstone-ai (MCTS + NN in C++) — relevant to a fuller decision AI, overkill for the pure win% combat rollout., yossielimelech/BGSimulator — a deep-learning BG simulator; illustrates an ML alternative, but a rules-based rollout is more accurate, explainable, and cheaper on-device.
Perf budget: Target N = 1000-2000 sims completing in <100 ms on a mid-range 2023 phone, hard-capped so it NEVER touches the UI thread or the PDS zero-freeze mandate. Stats: stderr of a proportion = sqrt(p(1-p)/N); N=1000 gives ±1.5% at p=0.5, N=2000 gives ±1.1% — plenty for a HUD number. Each rollout is tens of microseconds if allocation-free. Engineering: run on Dispatchers.Default in a cancellable coroutine; debounce so a new recognition frame or board edit cancels the in-flight job (structured concurrency) instead of queueing; chunk the loop with periodic yield() for cancellation; optionally fan out across cores (split N, merge counts), though single-thread already suffices. Zero garbage in the hot loop: pooled struct-of-arrays / reused MinionState, primitive int arrays for slots, reuse one working buffer across all N sims (reset, don't reallocate). Cap attacks per rollout (~500) and wall-clock (~250 ms) so it always returns; if a cap trips, return the partial aggregate flagged 'approximate'.
Inputs from recognition: YOUR board = near-perfect, from the GameStateStore not the screen: minion dbfId, current Atk/HP (buffs already baked in), keywords, tribe, golden/triple, blood-gem count, deathrattle/enchant provenance, your hero power, any start-of-combat quest reward., ENEMY board = the hard part: only fully visible in the short combat-preview window as combat begins (exactly when you want the sim). Recognition must read, per minion: card identity (ML Kit OCR of name + Gemini vision fallback), displayed Atk/HP (tiny text, error-prone), tribe, and visible keyword glyphs (Divine Shield gold border, Taunt frame, Poison/Venom drip, Reborn, Windfury, Stealth)., REALISTICALLY UNREADABLE and therefore bounding usefulness: hidden enchantments applied during the opponent's turn (secret +X/+X only shown in tooltips), deathrattle/magnetic payloads not surfaced on the card face, pending auras vs already-merged blood gems, the opponent's hero power and start-of-combat effects, and golden-vs-normal when art is ambiguous. Minion position/order IS readable and matters., Confidence: recognition emits a per-minion confidence and an overall enemy-board confidence. Displayed Atk/HP is ground truth for on-board buffs, but any effect that fires only at combat start is invisible pre-combat., Fallback input: user corrections from the manual board editor override recognition and are treated as perfect info.
Outputs: Win % / Tie % / Loss % for the upcoming combat, with a 95% confidence interval, plus a low-confidence 'approximate' or 'abstain' badge when recognition confidence is below threshold., Expected damage taken and expected damage dealt (mean of the damage distribution), and the full damage histogram for a mini bar chart., Lethal info: P(this combat kills you) and P(this combat kills the opponent), given both players' current life totals — the single most decision-relevant number., Averaged result summary (e.g. 'you usually win by 4') and, in Duos, the shared-life-aware team outcome., A confidence/abstain signal plus a 'this combat modeled approximately (uncommon card X treated as vanilla)' note when the effect registry hit an unmodeled card, so the HUD never presents a wrong number as authoritative.
Accuracy realism: Two independent accuracy ceilings. (A) SIMULATION fidelity: even a perfect rules engine outputs a DISTRIBUTION, not a certainty — combat is genuinely random (targets, summons, start-of-combat order), so 62% means 62%, and trigger-ordering edge cases plus unmodeled new cards add a few % drift (twanvl/Firestone/HDT all carry this caveat and are still trusted). Mitigate with a data-driven, patch-updatable effect registry, a replay regression harness, and an explicit 'approximate — card X unmodeled' flag rather than silent error. (B) RECOGNITION fidelity — the DOMINANT limit and the honest headline: your board is exact, but the enemy board is only glimpsed for ~a second at combat start, tiny Atk/HP text and subtle keyword glyphs are error-prone, and hidden enchantments / the opponent's hero power & start-of-combat effects are effectively invisible. A single misread keyword (Divine Shield, Poison, Taunt, Reborn) or a wrong HP can swing win% by tens of points. Therefore: (1) show a confidence badge and ABSTAIN rather than display a confident-but-wrong number when recognition is low-confidence; (2) ship a Firestone-style manual board editor (drag minions, set atk/hp/keywords) so the user corrects in seconds and the sim re-runs live; (3) never let the HUD imply false precision — round, show the CI, label approximations. Brutally honest bottom line: the simulator is only as good as the enemy-board read, and the manual-correct fallback is what makes it trustworthy in practice.
Module design: New Kotlin module bg/sim, pure logic, no Android deps (JVM-unit-testable). Core types: (1) immutable CombatSnapshot { BoardSnapshot self, BoardSnapshot enemy, HeroPower each, List<StartOfCombatEffect>, tribe context, mode = SOLO|DUOS }. (2) MinionState — pooled mutable: dbfId, atk, hp, maxHp, keyword bitmask, tribe, deathrattleIds, enchant refs, flags (golden, attackedThisCombat). Prefer struct-of-arrays / object pool to stay allocation-free. (3) CombatEngine.simulateOnce(snapshot, rng): Outcome — the deterministic-given-RNG core. (4) CombatSimulator.run(snapshot, iterations, budgetMs): Result — coroutine on Dispatchers.Default, cancellable, chunked, aggregates counts + histogram + CI. (5) EffectRegistry — DATA-DRIVEN map cardId/keyword -> handler for hooks: startOfCombat, deathrattle, onAttack, afterFriendlyAttack, afterDeath(Avenge), onSummon. New cards/patches ship as an updatable effect table, NOT engine edits (respects offline card DB + patch cadence). Unknown card -> vanilla + coverage flag. (6) DeterminismDetector to short-circuit to 1 rollout. Integration: fed by GameStateStore (your board) + a RecognitionResult (enemy board) + a ManualEditOverride; emits a WinProbability model consumed by the Overlay HUD widget and the grounded AI chat ('should I hero-power / sell / reposition?'). Testing: a replay harness loading known real combats (authored fixtures) that asserts the aggregate matches the known outcome distribution; regression suite run per patch.
Risks: Enemy-board misrecognition (wrong HP, missed Divine Shield/Poison/Taunt/Reborn) flips win% dramatically and erodes trust. -> Per-minion confidence + overall abstain threshold; confidence badge; manual board editor so users correct in seconds and the sim re-runs live; never present low-confidence output as authoritative.; Rule-coverage gaps: a new/uncommon card's effect isn't modeled, so the sim silently diverges from the live game. -> Data-driven EffectRegistry updatable per patch (not engine edits); unknown cards fall back to vanilla and are FLAGGED 'approximate'; replay regression harness of known combats run each patch.; Pathological combats (windfury mirrors, Macaw/Scallywag chains) loop or blow the time budget, risking a UI stall. -> Hard per-rollout attack cap (~500) declaring a TIE, plus a wall-clock budget (~250 ms) returning a partial aggregate flagged approximate; strictly off-thread and cancellable.; Running the sim on the UI thread or leaking concurrent jobs breaks the PDS zero-freeze/99.99% mandate. -> Dispatchers.Default only, structured-concurrency cancellation, one debounced in-flight job that cancels on new frame/edit, chunked yield().; Statistical noise makes the % jitter frame-to-frame and look unreliable. -> N>=1000 (±1.5%), report a CI, round for display, and short-circuit deterministic combats to a single stable rollout.; Balance patches change card behavior, silently invalidating the engine. -> Externalize card effects + stats into the bundled, updatable offline card data, version it, and gate the regression harness on each patch bump.

# DeckView — Consolidated Per-Mode Feature Matrix

Priorities: **must / should / could**. Recognition difficulty: **Low / Med / High** (how hard for our MediaProjection screen-capture + OCR/Gemini-vision stack). Compute type: **Deterministic** (ROI/state math), **Stats-DB** (external meta lookup), **Sim** (Monte Carlo), **Hybrid**, **CV** (on-device vision matching). Every recognizer honors **abstain-on-low-confidence** (PDS Gold Rule / STABILITY-FIRST).

The single load-bearing constraint everywhere: **Firestone/HDT read Hearthstone's local Power.log (perfect entity-level ground truth); DeckView sees only rendered pixels.** Anything depending on invisible/entity state (provenance, hidden triggers, shared pools, other players' full boards) is degraded or must abstain.

## Cross-cutting honesty summary (what screen-capture cannot deliver)

- **Card provenance / created-by / buffed-by / stolen / returned / mulliganed / "how long held"** — entity-level, invisible in pixels. Firestone's marquee "what created this card" is effectively **unsupportable**; only static class-generation hints.
- **Exact secret elimination** — hinges on which hidden triggers fired; fast animations missed on adaptive frame rates → **list candidates, abstain, never wrongly cross out**.
- **Fatigue / overdraw exact counts** — one missed draw/mill desyncs permanently → **approximate + empty-deck anchor**.
- **Lethal / optimal-attack** — needs every buffed stat/aura/keyword read → **abstain**.
- **BG enemy board** — glimpsed ~1s; tiny stats + subtle glyphs + hidden enchants/hero-power → **manual editor + confidence badge is what makes the sim trustworthy**.
- **BG shared minion pool** and **all-8 opponents' full boards / triples / leveling times** — unobservable; approximate or defer.
- **Reward-screen contents** (Arena/Brawliseum packs/gold/tickets) — unreliable OCR → best-effort.
- **HSReplay has no open data API** — stats must be mirrored server-side and shipped as offline bundles; DeckView cannot upload replays (no log). **Confirm licensing/ToS + any cost before ingesting** (LyAi rules).
- **All named stat sources (Firestone/HSReplay/HearthArena/wiki/HearthstoneJSON) are free-tier** — no ≥$0.10 authorization needed as specced.

MANDATE: STABILITY FIRST — zero crashes/freezes (LyAi "PDS Gold Rule", 99.99%). COST: free APIs only (Gemini 2.5-flash) unless Ignacio authorizes >= $0.10.
v1 backbone scope covers ONLY Standard/Wild CONSTRUCTED. Everything about OTHER MODES and richer per-mode features is what THIS plan must add.

=== BG SIM RESEARCH ===
## BG COMBAT SIMULATOR RESEARCH
Summary: DeckView's Battlegrounds combat simulator is the flagship "win %" feature: given both warbands at the moment combat starts, it estimates win/tie/loss probability, expected damage, and lethal chance. It is a Monte Carlo engine that fully plays out the auto-battle N times (randomness = attack-target selection, random summons/buffs, start-of-combat ordering, first-attacker tie-break) and aggregates outcomes. It runs entirely off the UI thread in pure Kotlin and is CPU-cheap (1-2k sims in well under 100 ms). Its real limit is RECOGNITION ACCURACY, not compute: your own board is known perfectly from the tracked game state, but the enemy board is only visible for a brief pre-combat window and hidden enchantments/subtle keywords are frequently unreadable, so a Firestone-style manual board editor plus confidence-gated abstention is mandatory. Mode fact-check (2026): Battlegrounds is a live first-class mode with a Duos variant (4 teams of 2, shared life, teammate-support minions); Duels was retired 2024, Classic removed 2023, and Twist was discontinued in Patch 35.4 (Apr 2026) — do NOT spec simulator features for retired modes.
Algorithm: MONTE CARLO full-combat rollout, the same family as twanvl's simulator, Firestone, and HDT's BG simulator. (1) Build an immutable CombatSnapshot from the GameStateStore (your board = perfect info) + the recognized/edited enemy board, plus both hero powers and start-of-combat effects. (2) For each of N iterations: deep-copy the snapshot into a pooled mutable working state seeded from a fast PRNG (SplitMix64/Xoshiro, NOT java.util.Random); resolve START-OF-COMBAT (hero powers + minions like Red Whelp / Prized Promoter / Deflect-o-Bot, ordered by tavern tier then random within a tier), then run the attack loop until one or both boards are empty, or a hard attack cap (~500) forces a declared TIE (guards windfury/Macaw/Scallywag infinite chains). (3) Attack loop: first attacker = side with more minions (tie = coin flip); sides alternate, each keeping a next-attacker pointer that advances left-to-right, skips 0-attack/dead minions, and wraps. Attacker picks a target at random among enemy Taunts if any exist, else any enemy (special cases: Zapp = lowest attack). Both minions deal Attack to the other's Health simultaneously; Divine Shield absorbs one hit, Poisonous/Venomous kills on any damage dealt, Cleave also hits the target's neighbors, Overkill/on-damage triggers fire. Resolve deaths in board order, firing Deathrattles (x2 under Baron Rivendare), Reborn, Avenge counters, and after-a-friendly-dies/attacks chains (Macaw re-triggers a friendly deathrattle; Scallywag summons a pirate that attacks immediately). (4) Aggregate: win/tie/loss counts -> percentages, a damage histogram (damage = winner's remaining minion star-tier sum + winner hero's tavern tier), expected damage taken/dealt, and P(you die)/P(opponent dies). Report a 95% CI so the UI can show '~62% (±2%)'. Optimization: a determinism detector short-circuits to ONE rollout when the combat has no RNG nodes (e.g. a single forced taunt line, no random summons), common late-game.
Rules to model: Attack order: first attacker = more minions (tie random); alternate sides; per-side next-attacker pointer advancing left-to-right, wrapping, skipping 0-attack/dead minions.; Target selection: random among enemy Taunts if any, else random enemy; Zapp Slywick = lowest attack; other forced-target effects.; Divine Shield (absorbs one damage instance), Taunt, Poisonous/Venomous (lethal on any damage), Windfury/Mega-Windfury (extra attacks), Reborn (resummon at 1 HP), Stealth.; Cleave (hits target + neighbors), adjacency buffs, and combat-active auras.; Deathrattles resolved in board order; Baron Rivendare doubles them; Reborn interplay; summon placement (tokens appear adjacent to the source).; Triggered chains: on-attack / after-friendly-attacks (Monstrous Macaw re-triggers a friendly deathrattle), after-a-minion-dies, Avenge counters, Scallywag pirate that attacks immediately, summon-triggered effects (Khadgar doubles summons).; Start-of-combat phase: hero powers and minions (Red Whelp damage, Prized Promoter, Deflect-o-Bot, Illidan) fire before attacks, ordered by tavern tier then random within a tier — a major pre-combat randomness source.; Blood gems: already merged into displayed stats, so treat as static; only model pending/aura gem effects if known.; Acceptable approximations: uncommon/unmodeled cards fall back to vanilla stats+keywords and are FLAGGED; exact simultaneous-death trigger ordering can differ slightly from live (twanvl notes the same caveat) — acceptable if disclosed.; Duos-specific: shared team life and cross-board teammate-support minions (Grave Narrator Avenge, Support System Divine Shield) — model as its own combat variant, not a bolt-on.
Existing art: twanvl/hearthstone-battlegrounds-simulator — canonical open-source C++ Monte Carlo battle simulator (web build at twanvl.nl/hsbg via emscripten); README explicitly notes 'there might be subtle differences in the order of triggers' — the honest baseline for approximation., Firestone — full tracker whose BG simulator runs locally with a user-adjustable accuracy/iteration slider and a drag-and-drop board editor to correct/experiment (the manual-correct fallback pattern DeckView should copy); Firestone's simulator is open-sourced., HearthSim / Hearthstone Deck Tracker — BG simulator showing win/tie/loss %; GitHub issue #4068 discusses how its simulation works and its accuracy caveats., Academic MCTS work (Central Michigan thesis 'Hearthstone Battleground: An AI Assistant with Monte Carlo Tree Search', 2021) and peter1591/hearthstone-ai (MCTS + NN in C++) — relevant to a fuller decision AI, overkill for the pure win% combat rollout., yossielimelech/BGSimulator — a deep-learning BG simulator; illustrates an ML alternative, but a rules-based rollout is more accurate, explainable, and cheaper on-device.
Perf budget: Target N = 1000-2000 sims completing in <100 ms on a mid-range 2023 phone, hard-capped so it NEVER touches the UI thread or the PDS zero-freeze mandate. Stats: stderr of a proportion = sqrt(p(1-p)/N); N=1000 gives ±1.5% at p=0.5, N=2000 gives ±1.1% — plenty for a HUD number. Each rollout is tens of microseconds if allocation-free. Engineering: run on Dispatchers.Default in a cancellable coroutine; debounce so a new recognition frame or board edit cancels the in-flight job (structured concurrency) instead of queueing; chunk the loop with periodic yield() for cancellation; optionally fan out across cores (split N, merge counts), though single-thread already suffices. Zero garbage in the hot loop: pooled struct-of-arrays / reused MinionState, primitive int arrays for slots, reuse one working buffer across all N sims (reset, don't reallocate). Cap attacks per rollout (~500) and wall-clock (~250 ms) so it always returns; if a cap trips, return the partial aggregate flagged 'approximate'.
Inputs from recognition: YOUR board = near-perfect, from the GameStateStore not the screen: minion dbfId, current Atk/HP (buffs already baked in), keywords, tribe, golden/triple, blood-gem count, deathrattle/enchant provenance, your hero power, any start-of-combat quest reward., ENEMY board = the hard part: only fully visible in the short combat-preview window as combat begins (exactly when you want the sim). Recognition must read, per minion: card identity (ML Kit OCR of name + Gemini vision fallback), displayed Atk/HP (tiny text, error-prone), tribe, and visible keyword glyphs (Divine Shield gold border, Taunt frame, Poison/Venom drip, Reborn, Windfury, Stealth)., REALISTICALLY UNREADABLE and therefore bounding usefulness: hidden enchantments applied during the opponent's turn (secret +X/+X only shown in tooltips), deathrattle/magnetic payloads not surfaced on the card face, pending auras vs already-merged blood gems, the opponent's hero power and start-of-combat effects, and golden-vs-normal when art is ambiguous. Minion position/order IS readable and matters., Confidence: recognition emits a per-minion confidence and an overall enemy-board confidence. Displayed Atk/HP is ground truth for on-board buffs, but any effect that fires only at combat start is invisible pre-combat., Fallback input: user corrections from the manual board editor override recognition and are treated as perfect info.
Outputs: Win % / Tie % / Loss % for the upcoming combat, with a 95% confidence interval, plus a low-confidence 'approximate' or 'abstain' badge when recognition confidence is below threshold., Expected damage taken and expected damage dealt (mean of the damage distribution), and the full damage histogram for a mini bar chart., Lethal info: P(this combat kills you) and P(this combat kills the opponent), given both players' current life totals — the single most decision-relevant number., Averaged result summary (e.g. 'you usually win by 4') and, in Duos, the shared-life-aware team outcome., A confidence/abstain signal plus a 'this combat modeled approximately (uncommon card X treated as vanilla)' note when the effect registry hit an unmodeled card, so the HUD never presents a wrong number as authoritative.
Accuracy realism: Two independent accuracy ceilings. (A) SIMULATION fidelity: even a perfect rules engine outputs a DISTRIBUTION, not a certainty — combat is genuinely random (targets, summons, start-of-combat order), so 62% means 62%, and trigger-ordering edge cases plus unmodeled new cards add a few % drift (twanvl/Firestone/HDT all carry this caveat and are still trusted). Mitigate with a data-driven, patch-updatable effect registry, a replay regression harness, and an explicit 'approximate — card X unmodeled' flag rather than silent error. (B) RECOGNITION fidelity — the DOMINANT limit and the honest headline: your board is exact, but the enemy board is only glimpsed for ~a second at combat start, tiny Atk/HP text and subtle keyword glyphs are error-prone, and hidden enchantments / the opponent's hero power & start-of-combat effects are effectively invisible. A single misread keyword (Divine Shield, Poison, Taunt, Reborn) or a wrong HP can swing win% by tens of points. Therefore: (1) show a confidence badge and ABSTAIN rather than display a confident-but-wrong number when recognition is low-confidence; (2) ship a Firestone-style manual board editor (drag minions, set atk/hp/keywords) so the user corrects in seconds and the sim re-runs live; (3) never let the HUD imply false precision — round, show the CI, label approximations. Brutally honest bottom line: the simulator is only as good as the enemy-board read, and the manual-correct fallback is what makes it trustworthy in practice.
Module design: New Kotlin module bg/sim, pure logic, no Android deps (JVM-unit-testable). Core types: (1) immutable CombatSnapshot { BoardSnapshot self, BoardSnapshot enemy, HeroPower each, List<StartOfCombatEffect>, tribe context, mode = SOLO|DUOS }. (2) MinionState — pooled mutable: dbfId, atk, hp, maxHp, keyword bitmask, tribe, deathrattleIds, enchant refs, flags (golden, attackedThisCombat). Prefer struct-of-arrays / object pool to stay allocation-free. (3) CombatEngine.simulateOnce(snapshot, rng): Outcome — the deterministic-given-RNG core. (4) CombatSimulator.run(snapshot, iterations, budgetMs): Result — coroutine on Dispatchers.Default, cancellable, chunked, aggregates counts + histogram + CI. (5) EffectRegistry — DATA-DRIVEN map cardId/keyword -> handler for hooks: startOfCombat, deathrattle, onAttack, afterFriendlyAttack, afterDeath(Avenge), onSummon. New cards/patches ship as an updatable effect table, NOT engine edits (respects offline card DB + patch cadence). Unknown card -> vanilla + coverage flag. (6) DeterminismDetector to short-circuit to 1 rollout. Integration: fed by GameStateStore (your board) + a RecognitionResult (enemy board) + a ManualEditOverride; emits a WinProbability model consumed by the Overlay HUD widget and the grounded AI chat ('should I hero-power / sell / reposition?'). Testing: a replay harness loading known real combats (authored fixtures) that asserts the aggregate matches the known outcome distribution; regression suite run per patch.
Risks: Enemy-board misrecognition (wrong HP, missed Divine Shield/Poison/Taunt/Reborn) flips win% dramatically and erodes trust. -> Per-minion confidence + overall abstain threshold; confidence badge; manual board editor so users correct in seconds and the sim re-runs live; never present low-confidence output as authoritative.; Rule-coverage gaps: a new/uncommon card's effect isn't modeled, so the sim silently diverges from the live game. -> Data-driven EffectRegistry updatable per patch (not engine edits); unknown cards fall back to vanilla and are FLAGGED 'approximate'; replay regression harness of known combats run each patch.; Pathological combats (windfury mirrors, Macaw/Scallywag chains) loop or blow the time budget, risking a UI stall. -> Hard per-rollout attack cap (~500) declaring a TIE, plus a wall-clock budget (~250 ms) returning a partial aggregate flagged approximate; strictly off-thread and cancellable.; Running the sim on the UI thread or leaking concurrent jobs breaks the PDS zero-freeze/99.99% mandate. -> Dispatchers.Default only, structured-concurrency cancellation, one debounced in-flight job that cancels on new frame/edit, chunked yield().; Statistical noise makes the % jitter frame-to-frame and look unreliable. -> N>=1000 (±1.5%), report a CI, round for display, and short-circuit deterministic combats to a single stable rollout.; Balance patches change card behavior, silently invalidating the engine. -> Externalize card effects + stats into the bundled, updatable offline card data, version it, and gate the regression harness on each patch bump.

# DeckView — Battlegrounds Combat Simulator Module

**Module:** `dev.lyai.deckview.modes.bg.sim.*` · Pure Kotlin/JVM (no Android deps) · JVM-unit-testable · Off-thread only

---

## 0. Module layout

```
modes/bg/sim/
  model/          CombatSnapshot, BoardSnapshot, MinionSpec (immutable inputs)
  runtime/        MinionState (SoA pool), WorkBoard, WorkState (mutable, per-rollout)
  rng/            SplitMix64, RngSource
  engine/         CombatEngine (simulateOnce), AttackLoop, StartOfCombat, DeathResolver
  effects/        EffectRegistry, EffectHooks, handlers/ (data-driven card table)
  aggregate/      Outcome, ResultAccumulator, WinProbability, DamageHistogram, CI
  api/            CombatSimulator (coroutine orchestrator, cancellable, budgeted)
  detect/         DeterminismDetector
  test-fixtures/  replay combats (authored), regression harness
```

Boundary rule: `model` and `engine` never import Android or coroutines. Only `api/CombatSimulator` touches `kotlinx.coroutines`. Recognition, GameStateStore, and the overlay live outside this module and communicate only via the immutable `CombatSnapshot` in and `WinProbability` out.

---

## 1. Domain model

### 1.1 Immutable input types (built once per combat, shared read-only across all N rollouts)

```kotlin
// Identity + static description of one minion as it enters combat.
data class MinionSpec(
    val dbfId: Int,
    val name: String,
    val atk: Int,            // displayed atk (blood gems / on-board buffs already baked in)
    val hp: Int,             // displayed hp
    val tavernTier: Int,     // 1..6 ; used for damage calc + start-of-combat ordering
    val tribe: TribeMask,    // bitmask; a minion may be multi-tribe (e.g. All)
    val keywords: KeywordMask,
    val golden: Boolean,
    val bloodGems: Int,      // informational; already in atk/hp
    val deathrattleIds: IntArray,  // ordered effect ids (registry keys)
    val enchantIds: IntArray,      // known combat-relevant enchants (Avenge counters, auras)
    val provenance: Provenance,    // SELF_TRACKED | ENEMY_RECOGNIZED | MANUAL_EDIT
    val confidence: Float          // 0..1 per-minion recognition confidence
)

@JvmInline value class KeywordMask(val bits: Int) {
    companion object {
        const val TAUNT=1; const val DIVINE_SHIELD=2; const val POISONOUS=4
        const val VENOMOUS=8; const val WINDFURY=16; const val MEGA_WINDFURY=32
        const val REBORN=64; const val STEALTH=128; const val CLEAVE=256
    }
}

@JvmInline value class TribeMask(val bits: Int)  // MURLOC, DEMON, MECH, BEAST, DRAGON, PIRATE, ELEMENTAL, QUILBOAR, NAGA, UNDEAD, ALL

data class BoardSnapshot(val minions: List<MinionSpec>)   // left-to-right order preserved

data class HeroPowerSpec(val id: Int, val startOfCombat: Boolean, val payload: IntArray)

data class CombatSnapshot(
    val self: BoardSnapshot,
    val enemy: BoardSnapshot,
    val selfHero: HeroPowerSpec,
    val enemyHero: HeroPowerSpec,
    val startEffects: List<StartOfCombatEffect>,   // hero + minion SoC, tier-ordered lazily at runtime
    val selfLife: Int,
    val enemyLife: Int,
    val selfTavernTier: Int,     // for damage-taken calc
    val enemyTavernTier: Int,
    val mode: BgMode,            // SOLO | DUOS
    val duosContext: DuosContext? = null,
    val enemyConfidence: Float   // aggregate; drives abstain badge
)
```

### 1.2 Mutable runtime state (allocation-free, pooled, reset — never reallocated per rollout)

To hit the perf budget the hot loop must not allocate. Represent the working board as **struct-of-arrays** indexed by slot, one buffer reused across all N sims:

```kotlin
class WorkBoard(maxSlots: Int = 7) {           // 7 board slots per side, +overflow for summons (cap 7 real)
    val dbfId = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val atk   = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val hp    = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val maxHp = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val kw    = IntArray(maxSlots)              // live keyword bits (DS can be stripped mid-combat)
    val tribe = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val tier  = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val flags = IntArray(maxSlots)              // GOLDEN, ATTACKED_THIS_TURN, PENDING_DEATH, WINDFURY_USED
    val drIdx = Array(maxSlots){ EMPTY_INT }    // pointer into a shared deathrattle-id arena
    var count = 0
    var nextAttacker = 0                        // left-to-right pointer
    fun reset(src: BoardSnapshot) { … }         // fill from immutable spec, count set, pointers zeroed
}

class WorkState {
    val a = WorkBoard(); val b = WorkBoard()
    var attackNo = 0
    // per-side counters that persist across the combat:
    var aAvenge = IntArray(...); var bAvenge = ...   // Avenge trigger countdowns
    fun reset(snap: CombatSnapshot) { a.reset(snap.self); b.reset(snap.enemy); attackNo=0 … }
}
```

`MinionState` as an object exists only for the EffectRegistry handler API (a thin cursor `(board, slot)` view) so card handlers read like game text without the hot loop paying object-allocation cost.

---

## 2. Monte-Carlo simulation loop

### 2.1 RNG

`SplitMix64` seeded per rollout from a master seed + iteration index. **Never** `java.util.Random` (synchronized, slow, allocates). One `RngSource` instance reused; `nextInt(bound)` via Lemire's bounded-multiply. Seeding per-iteration deterministically (`masterSeed xor mix(i)`) makes any single rollout reproducible for debugging ("replay rollout #843").

### 2.2 One rollout — `CombatEngine.simulateOnce(state, rng): Outcome`

```
1. START-OF-COMBAT PHASE
   - Collect all start-of-combat sources (hero powers with startOfCombat=true,
     minions like Red Whelp / Prized Promoter / Deflect-o-Bot / Illidan).
   - Order = ascending tavern tier; WITHIN a tier the order is RANDOM (rng.shuffle).
     This is a first-class randomness node — sampled fresh each iteration.
   - Fire each via EffectRegistry.startOfCombat(handler). Resolve any deaths triggered.

2. PICK FIRST ATTACKER
   - side with more minions attacks first; tie => rng coin flip.

3. ATTACK LOOP  (until one/both boards empty, or attackNo > ATTACK_CAP=500)
   attacker side = alternates each iteration of the loop
   a. advance that side's nextAttacker pointer left-to-right, wrapping,
      skipping dead/0-atk minions. If none attackable -> that side is "done";
      if BOTH done -> break.
   b. choose target:
        if any enemy TAUNT (and not stealthed) -> uniform-random among taunts
        else -> uniform-random among all enemy minions
        forced-target overrides (Zapp Slywick -> lowest atk; tie random)
   c. resolve simultaneous strike:
        target.hp -= attacker.atk ; attacker.hp -= target.atk
        Divine Shield absorbs one instance (strip bit, damage=0 for that side)
        Poisonous/Venomous: if dealt >0 damage -> mark target PENDING_DEATH
        Cleave: also damage target's left+right neighbors
        fire onAttack / overkill / on-damage hooks
   d. if attacker has Windfury and hasn't used extra attack -> it attacks again
      (Mega-Windfury = up to 4 total); guarded by ATTACK_CAP
   e. DeathResolver: collect PENDING_DEATH + hp<=0 in board order, then:
        - fire Deathrattles (x2 if Baron Rivendare on that side), in board order
        - Reborn: resummon at 1 HP (once)
        - Avenge counters decrement; fire when they hit 0
        - after-a-friendly-dies chains; Scallywag pirate summons & attacks immediately
        - Monstrous Macaw: after a friendly attacks, re-trigger a friendly deathrattle
        - summon placement: tokens inserted adjacent to source; Khadgar doubles summons
        - deaths caused by deathrattles cascade (loop until stable)
   f. alternate attacker side; attackNo++

4. TERMINATION
   - both empty -> TIE
   - one empty -> other side WINS
   - ATTACK_CAP hit -> declared TIE, flag rollout "capped"

5. DAMAGE
   - winner deals = (sum of surviving minions' tavern tiers) + winner's hero tavern tier
   - Outcome{ result: WIN|TIE|LOSS, damage, capped }
```

`Outcome` is a value class packing (result 2 bits, damage int, flags) — zero allocation.

### 2.3 Aggregation across N iterations

```kotlin
class ResultAccumulator {
    var win=0; var tie=0; var loss=0; var capped=0
    val dmgHistFor = IntArray(MAX_DMG+1)   // damage dealt when YOU win
    val dmgHistAgainst = IntArray(MAX_DMG+1)
    fun add(o: Outcome) { … }
    fun toResult(n:Int): WinProbability {
        val pWin = win.toFloat()/n
        val ci = 1.96f * sqrt(pWin*(1-pWin)/n)   // 95% CI half-width, Wald
        // lethal: P(you die) = share of loss rollouts whose damage >= selfLife
        // P(opp dies) = share of win rollouts whose damage >= enemyLife
        …
    }
}
```

`WinProbability` output:
```kotlin
data class WinProbability(
    val winPct: Float, val tiePct: Float, val lossPct: Float,
    val ciHalfWidth: Float,          // "±2%"
    val expectedDamageDealt: Float, val expectedDamageTaken: Float,
    val histogramDealt: IntArray, val histogramTaken: IntArray,
    val pYouDie: Float, val pOpponentDies: Float,
    val summaryText: String,         // "you usually win by 4"
    val confidence: Confidence,      // OK | APPROXIMATE | ABSTAIN
    val coverageFlags: List<String>, // "uncommon card X modeled as vanilla"
    val iterations: Int, val cappedCount: Int, val elapsedMs: Long,
    val teamOutcome: DuosOutcome? = null
)
```

Statistics: stderr of a proportion `= sqrt(p(1-p)/N)`; N=1000 → ±1.5% @ p=0.5, N=2000 → ±1.1%. Ample for a HUD number.

---

## 3. Mechanics: modeled vs approximated (correctness-vs-scope table)

| Mechanic | v1 | v2 | Notes / hardest bits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attack order (more-minions-first, alternating, L→R pointer, wrap, skip 0-atk) | ✅ Full | | Core; well-specified |
| Target selection (taunt-first, uniform random, Zapp=lowest atk) | ✅ Full | | |
| Divine Shield (absorb one instance) | ✅ Full | | |
| Taunt / Stealth | ✅ Full | | Stealth removed on attack |
| Poisonous / Venomous | ✅ Full | | Venomous decays after one kill |
| Windfury / Mega-Windfury | ✅ Full | | Interacts with ATTACK_CAP |
| Reborn | ✅ Full | | Resummon at 1 HP, once |
| Cleave (target + neighbors) | ✅ Full | | Neighbor indices from live SoA layout |
| Deathrattles (board-order, cascade) | ✅ Registry | | Data-driven; unknown DR → flagged |
| Baron Rivendare (double DR) | ✅ Full | | |
| Avenge counters | ✅ Registry | | Per-side countdown in WorkState |
| Start-of-combat (hero powers + Red Whelp/Deflect-o-Bot/Prized Promoter/Illidan) | ✅ Registry | | **Tier-then-random ordering = major RNG node** |
| Scallywag pirate (summon + immediate attack) | ✅ Full | | Injects an out-of-turn attack |
| Monstrous Macaw (re-trigger friendly DR) | ✅ Full | | after-friendly-attacks hook; ordering-sensitive |
| Khadgar (double summons) | ✅ Full | | Multiplies token counts incl. Scallywag chains |
| Summon placement (adjacent to source) | ✅ Full | | SoA insert-with-shift, respect 7-slot cap |
| Adjacency / combat auras (e.g. Murozond, Whelp Smuggler on-attack) | ⚠️ Common ones | ✅ Full | Recompute on board change; v1 covers frequent cards |
| Blood gems | ✅ Static | | Already baked into displayed atk/hp; pending-only gems v2 |
| Hidden enchantments (secret +X/+X) | ❌ (invisible to recognition) | ⚠️ Manual-edit only | Recognition ceiling, not engine limit |
| Duos (shared life, teammate-support minions, cross-board portals) | ⚠️ Basic | ✅ Full | Own combat variant, not a bolt-on |
| Quest rewards / hero-power start effects (enemy) | ⚠️ if recognized | | Usually invisible pre-combat |
| Exotic new-set cards | Vanilla + FLAG | Registry update | Ships as data table, not engine edit |

**Honest caveat carried forward** (twanvl/Firestone/HDT all share it): exact simultaneous-death trigger ordering can differ a few % from live. Acceptable **only if disclosed** via the `APPROXIMATE` badge.

### Hardest mechanics (call-outs)
1. **Start-of-combat tier-then-random ordering** — dominant pre-combat RNG; must reshuffle within-tier each iteration or win% is biased.
2. **Macaw + Scallywag + Baron + Khadgar interaction** — nested re-triggers and summon-doubling; the DeathResolver must be a **fixpoint loop** over a work-queue, not a single pass, with the ATTACK_CAP as the infinite-chain guard.
3. **Windfury mirrors / Macaw loops** — can theoretically not terminate; hard `ATTACK_CAP=500` → declared TIE, flagged `capped`.
4. **Summon placement + SoA insertion** — shifting slots while pointers (nextAttacker) and Avenge indices are live; keep a stable id or recompute pointers after every structural change.

---

## 4. Off-thread execution plan

```kotlin
class CombatSimulator(
    private val engine: CombatEngine,
    private val detector: DeterminismDetector,
    private val defaultDispatcher: CoroutineDispatcher = Dispatchers.Default
) {
    suspend fun run(
        snapshot: CombatSnapshot,
        iterations: Int = 2000,
        budgetMs: Long = 250
    ): WinProbability = withContext(defaultDispatcher) {
        // 1. Determinism short-circuit
        if (detector.isDeterministic(snapshot)) {
            val o = engine.simulateOnce(freshState(snapshot), NoOpRng)
            return@withContext singleResult(o)   // stable, no jitter
        }
        // 2. Chunked Monte-Carlo with cancellation + wall-clock budget
        val acc = ResultAccumulator()
        val deadline = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() + budgetMs
        val work = WorkState()                    // reused across all iterations
        var i = 0
        while (i < iterations) {
            val end = min(i + CHUNK /*=128*/, iterations)
            while (i < end) {
                work.reset(snapshot)
                acc.add(engine.simulateOnce(work, rngFor(i)))
                i++
            }
            ensureActive()                         // cooperative cancellation
            if (SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() > deadline) {
                acc.markPartial(); break           // return partial, flag approximate
            }
            yield()                                // let dispatcher breathe
        }
        acc.toResult(i).withConfidence(snapshot)
    }
}
```

Integration discipline (protects the PDS zero-freeze / 99.99% mandate):

- **One debounced in-flight job.** The overlay owns a `Job?`; a new recognition frame or manual edit **cancels** the previous job (structured concurrency) rather than queueing. Debounce ~120 ms so rapid enemy-board re-reads don't thrash.
- **Dispatchers.Default only** — never `Main`. The engine module has no way to touch the UI thread by construction (no Android imports).
- **Chunked `yield()` + `ensureActive()`** so cancellation is prompt and the pool of Default threads never starves.
- **Hard caps**: `ATTACK_CAP=500` per rollout, `budgetMs≈250` wall-clock. A tripped cap returns the partial aggregate flagged `APPROXIMATE`; the sim **always returns**.
- **Fan-out (optional)**: split N across cores (`k` coroutines, N/k each), merge accumulators. Single-thread already meets budget (each rollout tens of µs when allocation-free), so this is a later knob, not v1.
- **N auto-tune**: start N=2000; if elapsed < ~40 ms and CI still wide, the orchestrator may raise N on the next run; on a thermally throttled device it lowers N to hold the 300 ms ceiling. Budget is the master; N is advisory.

---

## 5. Inputs from recognition + manual-correction fallback

### 5.1 Data flow
```
GameStateStore (StateFlow) ──► self BoardSnapshot        (PERFECT info: dbfId, atk/hp, keywords, DR, gems)
RecognitionResult ───────────► enemy BoardSnapshot        (per-minion + aggregate confidence)
ManualEditOverride ──────────► overrides enemy (or self)   (treated as PERFECT info, confidence=1)
                              └► SnapshotBuilder ──► CombatSnapshot ──► CombatSimulator
```

- **Your board** = read from `GameStateStore`, not the screen — exact. Includes buffs baked into atk/hp, keywords, tribe, golden/triple, blood-gem count, deathrattle/enchant provenance, your hero power.
- **Enemy board** = the hard part. Only fully visible in the ~1 s combat-preview window (exactly when the sim is wanted). Recognition reads per minion: identity (ML Kit OCR name + Gemini vision fallback), displayed atk/hp, tribe, visible keyword glyphs (DS gold border, Taunt frame, Poison/Venom drip, Reborn, Windfury, Stealth), and **position** (readable, and it matters).
- **Realistically unreadable** (bounds usefulness): hidden enchantments (secret +X/+X in tooltips), unsurfaced deathrattle/magnetic payloads, pending auras vs merged gems, the enemy hero power and their start-of-combat effects, ambiguous golden-vs-normal. These are recognition ceilings, **flagged**, never silently guessed.

### 5.2 Confidence → behavior
- Each `MinionSpec.confidence` and `CombatSnapshot.enemyConfidence` drive a threshold gate:
  - `enemyConfidence ≥ 0.85` → `OK`, show number.
  - `0.6 – 0.85` → `APPROXIMATE` badge ("~62% (±2%)").
  - `< 0.6` → `ABSTAIN` — **do not** show a confident-but-wrong number; show "board unclear — tap to edit".
- A **single misread keyword** (DS/Poison/Taunt/Reborn) or wrong HP can swing win% by tens of points. Abstention is the safety valve.

### 5.3 Manual board editor (Firestone-style, mandatory fallback)
- Compose UI: two 7-slot rows (yours pre-filled, enemy from recognition). Drag to reorder, tap a minion to set atk/hp, toggle keyword chips (Taunt/DS/Poison/Venom/Windfury/Reborn/Stealth), pick tribe, mark golden, add a deathrattle from a searchable card picker (bundled HearthstoneJSON, Spanish-first).
- Every edit produces a `ManualEditOverride`, rebuilds the `CombatSnapshot`, **cancels the in-flight job and re-runs live** (debounced). User corrects in seconds; the % updates.
- Recognition pre-highlights low-confidence minions ("this one's unsure — check it") so the user fixes the exact cells that matter.

---

## 6. Output rendering: overlay HUD + AI chat

### 6.1 Overlay HUD widget (`TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY`, drawn over the game)
- Compact pill during the combat-preview window:
  - **`62% W · 11% T · 27% L (±2%)`** — win/tie/loss with CI.
  - Lethal line, the single most decision-relevant number: **`☠ opp 34%`** / **`⚠ you 8%`** = P(opponent dies) / P(you die) given both life totals.
  - Mini bar chart from the damage histogram; averaged summary "usually win by 4".
  - Confidence chip: green `OK`, amber `~approx`, grey `abstain — tap to edit` (opens the manual editor).
  - If `coverageFlags` non-empty: small "modeled approximately (card X)" note. **Never imply false precision** — always rounded, always the CI, always label approximations.
- The HUD subscribes to a `StateFlow<WinProbability>`; the sim writes results off-thread and the widget just renders — no computation on the render path.

### 6.2 Grounded AI chat feed
- The latest `WinProbability` + both boards are injected as **structured context** into the Gemini chat prompt so the assistant answers grounded questions: "should I hero-power?", "sell the Scallywag or keep it?", "do I reposition my Taunt?".
- The chat can request a **counterfactual re-run**: the assistant proposes a board change (e.g. "move Baron left of your Ghoul"), calls the sim on a hypothetical `CombatSnapshot`, and reports the delta ("that raises win% from 47% to 58%"). This is the same off-thread `CombatSimulator.run`, just fed an edited snapshot.
- Markdown rendering follows the existing DeckView chat mandate: off-thread parse, virtualized `LazyColumn`, `PrecomputedText` — the sim result is small structured data, not a UI-thread hazard.

---

## 7. Testing & correctness harness
- **JVM unit tests** on `engine` (no Android): deterministic-RNG rollouts assert exact outcomes for hand-authored boards (DS absorption, Poison kill, Windfury count, Reborn, Cleave neighbors, Baron-doubled DR, Macaw/Scallywag/Khadgar chains).
- **Replay regression harness**: fixtures of known real combats (board in → known outcome distribution). Assert aggregate win% within CI + a fixed seed for reproducibility. **Gated on each patch bump** of the bundled card data.
- **Determinism detector test**: no-RNG combats must short-circuit to 1 rollout and produce a stable %.
- **Perf test**: N=2000 must complete < 100 ms on a mid-range reference device profile; loop must allocate ~0 bytes (allocation assertion in a JMH-style microbench).
- **EffectRegistry coverage report**: any `dbfId` hitting the vanilla fallback is logged so the coverage table can be maintained per patch. Unknown card → vanilla stats+keywords + `coverageFlags` entry, never a silent divergence.

---

## Bottom line (design honesty)
Compute is the easy part — 1–2k allocation-free rollouts finish in well under 100 ms off-thread, and the caps guarantee it never janks the overlay. The **real accuracy ceiling is the enemy-board read**, glimpsed for ~1 s with tiny atk/hp text, subtle keyword glyphs, and genuinely invisible hidden enchantments/hero powers. So the module's trustworthiness rests on three things it must ship with, not just the Monte-Carlo core: (1) per-minion **confidence + abstain** instead of confident-wrong numbers, (2) the **manual board editor** that lets the user correct in seconds and re-runs live, and (3) a **data-driven, patch-updatable EffectRegistry** with a replay regression harness so new cards degrade to flagged-approximate rather than silent error.

# DeckView — Consolidated Per-Mode Feature Matrix

Priorities: **must / should / could**. Recognition difficulty: **Low / Med / High** (how hard for our MediaProjection screen-capture + OCR/Gemini-vision stack). Compute type: **Deterministic** (ROI/state math), **Stats-DB** (external meta lookup), **Sim** (Monte Carlo), **Hybrid**, **CV** (on-device vision matching). Every recognizer honors **abstain-on-low-confidence** (PDS Gold Rule / STABILITY-FIRST).

The single load-bearing constraint everywhere: **Firestone/HDT read Hearthstone's local Power.log (perfect entity-level ground truth); DeckView sees only rendered pixels.** Anything depending on invisible/entity state (provenance, hidden triggers, shared pools, other players' full boards) is degraded or must abstain.

## Cross-cutting honesty summary (what screen-capture cannot deliver)

- **Card provenance / created-by / buffed-by / stolen / returned / mulliganed / "how long held"** — entity-level, invisible in pixels. Firestone's marquee "what created this card" is effectively **unsupportable**; only static class-generation hints.
- **Exact secret elimination** — hinges on which hidden triggers fired; fast animations missed on adaptive frame rates → **list candidates, abstain, never wrongly cross out**.
- **Fatigue / overdraw exact counts** — one missed draw/mill desyncs permanently → **approximate + empty-deck anchor**.
- **Lethal / optimal-attack** — needs every buffed stat/aura/keyword read → **abstain**.
- **BG enemy board** — glimpsed ~1s; tiny stats + subtle glyphs + hidden enchants/hero-power → **manual editor + confidence badge is what makes the sim trustworthy**.
- **BG shared minion pool** and **all-8 opponents' full boards / triples / leveling times** — unobservable; approximate or defer.
- **Reward-screen contents** (Arena/Brawliseum packs/gold/tickets) — unreliable OCR → best-effort.
- **HSReplay has no open data API** — stats must be mirrored server-side and shipped as offline bundles; DeckView cannot upload replays (no log). **Confirm licensing/ToS + any cost before ingesting** (LyAi rules).
- **All named stat sources (Firestone/HSReplay/HearthArena/wiki/HearthstoneJSON) are free-tier** — no ≥$0.10 authorization needed as specced.

=== BG SIM ENGINE ===
# DeckView — Battlegrounds Combat Simulator Module

**Module:** `dev.lyai.deckview.modes.bg.sim.*` · Pure Kotlin/JVM (no Android deps) · JVM-unit-testable · Off-thread only

---

## 0. Module layout

```
modes/bg/sim/
  model/          CombatSnapshot, BoardSnapshot, MinionSpec (immutable inputs)
  runtime/        MinionState (SoA pool), WorkBoard, WorkState (mutable, per-rollout)
  rng/            SplitMix64, RngSource
  engine/         CombatEngine (simulateOnce), AttackLoop, StartOfCombat, DeathResolver
  effects/        EffectRegistry, EffectHooks, handlers/ (data-driven card table)
  aggregate/      Outcome, ResultAccumulator, WinProbability, DamageHistogram, CI
  api/            CombatSimulator (coroutine orchestrator, cancellable, budgeted)
  detect/         DeterminismDetector
  test-fixtures/  replay combats (authored), regression harness
```

Boundary rule: `model` and `engine` never import Android or coroutines. Only `api/CombatSimulator` touches `kotlinx.coroutines`. Recognition, GameStateStore, and the overlay live outside this module and communicate only via the immutable `CombatSnapshot` in and `WinProbability` out.

---

## 1. Domain model

### 1.1 Immutable input types (built once per combat, shared read-only across all N rollouts)

```kotlin
// Identity + static description of one minion as it enters combat.
data class MinionSpec(
    val dbfId: Int,
    val name: String,
    val atk: Int,            // displayed atk (blood gems / on-board buffs already baked in)
    val hp: Int,             // displayed hp
    val tavernTier: Int,     // 1..6 ; used for damage calc + start-of-combat ordering
    val tribe: TribeMask,    // bitmask; a minion may be multi-tribe (e.g. All)
    val keywords: KeywordMask,
    val golden: Boolean,
    val bloodGems: Int,      // informational; already in atk/hp
    val deathrattleIds: IntArray,  // ordered effect ids (registry keys)
    val enchantIds: IntArray,      // known combat-relevant enchants (Avenge counters, auras)
    val provenance: Provenance,    // SELF_TRACKED | ENEMY_RECOGNIZED | MANUAL_EDIT
    val confidence: Float          // 0..1 per-minion recognition confidence
)

@JvmInline value class KeywordMask(val bits: Int) {
    companion object {
        const val TAUNT=1; const val DIVINE_SHIELD=2; const val POISONOUS=4
        const val VENOMOUS=8; const val WINDFURY=16; const val MEGA_WINDFURY=32
        const val REBORN=64; const val STEALTH=128; const val CLEAVE=256
    }
}

@JvmInline value class TribeMask(val bits: Int)  // MURLOC, DEMON, MECH, BEAST, DRAGON, PIRATE, ELEMENTAL, QUILBOAR, NAGA, UNDEAD, ALL

data class BoardSnapshot(val minions: List<MinionSpec>)   // left-to-right order preserved

data class HeroPowerSpec(val id: Int, val startOfCombat: Boolean, val payload: IntArray)

data class CombatSnapshot(
    val self: BoardSnapshot,
    val enemy: BoardSnapshot,
    val selfHero: HeroPowerSpec,
    val enemyHero: HeroPowerSpec,
    val startEffects: List<StartOfCombatEffect>,   // hero + minion SoC, tier-ordered lazily at runtime
    val selfLife: Int,
    val enemyLife: Int,
    val selfTavernTier: Int,     // for damage-taken calc
    val enemyTavernTier: Int,
    val mode: BgMode,            // SOLO | DUOS
    val duosContext: DuosContext? = null,
    val enemyConfidence: Float   // aggregate; drives abstain badge
)
```

### 1.2 Mutable runtime state (allocation-free, pooled, reset — never reallocated per rollout)

To hit the perf budget the hot loop must not allocate. Represent the working board as **struct-of-arrays** indexed by slot, one buffer reused across all N sims:

```kotlin
class WorkBoard(maxSlots: Int = 7) {           // 7 board slots per side, +overflow for summons (cap 7 real)
    val dbfId = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val atk   = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val hp    = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val maxHp = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val kw    = IntArray(maxSlots)              // live keyword bits (DS can be stripped mid-combat)
    val tribe = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val tier  = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val flags = IntArray(maxSlots)              // GOLDEN, ATTACKED_THIS_TURN, PENDING_DEATH, WINDFURY_USED
    val drIdx = Array(maxSlots){ EMPTY_INT }    // pointer into a shared deathrattle-id arena
    var count = 0
    var nextAttacker = 0                        // left-to-right pointer
    fun reset(src: BoardSnapshot) { … }         // fill from immutable spec, count set, pointers zeroed
}

class WorkState {
    val a = WorkBoard(); val b = WorkBoard()
    var attackNo = 0
    // per-side counters that persist across the combat:
    var aAvenge = IntArray(...); var bAvenge = ...   // Avenge trigger countdowns
    fun reset(snap: CombatSnapshot) { a.reset(snap.self); b.reset(snap.enemy); attackNo=0 … }
}
```

`MinionState` as an object exists only for the EffectRegistry handler API (a thin cursor `(board, slot)` view) so card handlers read like game text without the hot loop paying object-allocation cost.

---

## 2. Monte-Carlo simulation loop

### 2.1 RNG

`SplitMix64` seeded per rollout from a master seed + iteration index. **Never** `java.util.Random` (synchronized, slow, allocates). One `RngSource` instance reused; `nextInt(bound)` via Lemire's bounded-multiply. Seeding per-iteration deterministically (`masterSeed xor mix(i)`) makes any single rollout reproducible for debugging ("replay rollout #843").

### 2.2 One rollout — `CombatEngine.simulateOnce(state, rng): Outcome`

```
1. START-OF-COMBAT PHASE
   - Collect all start-of-combat sources (hero powers with startOfCombat=true,
     minions like Red Whelp / Prized Promoter / Deflect-o-Bot / Illidan).
   - Order = ascending tavern tier; WITHIN a tier the order is RANDOM (rng.shuffle).
     This is a first-class randomness node — sampled fresh each iteration.
   - Fire each via EffectRegistry.startOfCombat(handler). Resolve any deaths triggered.

2. PICK FIRST ATTACKER
   - side with more minions attacks first; tie => rng coin flip.

3. ATTACK LOOP  (until one/both boards empty, or attackNo > ATTACK_CAP=500)
   attacker side = alternates each iteration of the loop
   a. advance that side's nextAttacker pointer left-to-right, wrapping,
      skipping dead/0-atk minions. If none attackable -> that side is "done";
      if BOTH done -> break.
   b. choose target:
        if any enemy TAUNT (and not stealthed) -> uniform-random among taunts
        else -> uniform-random among all enemy minions
        forced-target overrides (Zapp Slywick -> lowest atk; tie random)
   c. resolve simultaneous strike:
        target.hp -= attacker.atk ; attacker.hp -= target.atk
        Divine Shield absorbs one instance (strip bit, damage=0 for that side)
        Poisonous/Venomous: if dealt >0 damage -> mark target PENDING_DEATH
        Cleave: also damage target's left+right neighbors
        fire onAttack / overkill / on-damage hooks
   d. if attacker has Windfury and hasn't used extra attack -> it attacks again
      (Mega-Windfury = up to 4 total); guarded by ATTACK_CAP
   e. DeathResolver: collect PENDING_DEATH + hp<=0 in board order, then:
        - fire Deathrattles (x2 if Baron Rivendare on that side), in board order
        - Reborn: resummon at 1 HP (once)
        - Avenge counters decrement; fire when they hit 0
        - after-a-friendly-dies chains; Scallywag pirate summons & attacks immediately
        - Monstrous Macaw: after a friendly attacks, re-trigger a friendly deathrattle
        - summon placement: tokens inserted adjacent to source; Khadgar doubles summons
        - deaths caused by deathrattles cascade (loop until stable)
   f. alternate attacker side; attackNo++

4. TERMINATION
   - both empty -> TIE
   - one empty -> other side WINS
   - ATTACK_CAP hit -> declared TIE, flag rollout "capped"

5. DAMAGE
   - winner deals = (sum of surviving minions' tavern tiers) + winner's hero tavern tier
   - Outcome{ result: WIN|TIE|LOSS, damage, capped }
```

`Outcome` is a value class packing (result 2 bits, damage int, flags) — zero allocation.

### 2.3 Aggregation across N iterations

```kotlin
class ResultAccumulator {
    var win=0; var tie=0; var loss=0; var capped=0
    val dmgHistFor = IntArray(MAX_DMG+1)   // damage dealt when YOU win
    val dmgHistAgainst = IntArray(MAX_DMG+1)
    fun add(o: Outcome) { … }
    fun toResult(n:Int): WinProbability {
        val pWin = win.toFloat()/n
        val ci = 1.96f * sqrt(pWin*(1-pWin)/n)   // 95% CI half-width, Wald
        // lethal: P(you die) = share of loss rollouts whose damage >= selfLife
        // P(opp dies) = share of win rollouts whose damage >= enemyLife
        …
    }
}
```

`WinProbability` output:
```kotlin
data class WinProbability(
    val winPct: Float, val tiePct: Float, val lossPct: Float,
    val ciHalfWidth: Float,          // "±2%"
    val expectedDamageDealt: Float, val expectedDamageTaken: Float,
    val histogramDealt: IntArray, val histogramTaken: IntArray,
    val pYouDie: Float, val pOpponentDies: Float,
    val summaryText: String,         // "you usually win by 4"
    val confidence: Confidence,      // OK | APPROXIMATE | ABSTAIN
    val coverageFlags: List<String>, // "uncommon card X modeled as vanilla"
    val iterations: Int, val cappedCount: Int, val elapsedMs: Long,
    val teamOutcome: DuosOutcome? = null
)
```

Statistics: stderr of a proportion `= sqrt(p(1-p)/N)`; N=1000 → ±1.5% @ p=0.5, N=2000 → ±1.1%. Ample for a HUD number.
