=== BG SIM ENGINE ===
# DeckView — Battlegrounds Combat Simulator Module

**Module:** `dev.lyai.deckview.modes.bg.sim.*` · Pure Kotlin/JVM (no Android deps) · JVM-unit-testable · Off-thread only

---

## 0. Module layout

```
modes/bg/sim/
  model/          CombatSnapshot, BoardSnapshot, MinionSpec (immutable inputs)
  runtime/        MinionState (SoA pool), WorkBoard, WorkState (mutable, per-rollout)
  rng/            SplitMix64, RngSource
  engine/         CombatEngine (simulateOnce), AttackLoop, StartOfCombat, DeathResolver
  effects/        EffectRegistry, EffectHooks, handlers/ (data-driven card table)
  aggregate/      Outcome, ResultAccumulator, WinProbability, DamageHistogram, CI
  api/            CombatSimulator (coroutine orchestrator, cancellable, budgeted)
  detect/         DeterminismDetector
  test-fixtures/  replay combats (authored), regression harness
```

Boundary rule: `model` and `engine` never import Android or coroutines. Only `api/CombatSimulator` touches `kotlinx.coroutines`. Recognition, GameStateStore, and the overlay live outside this module and communicate only via the immutable `CombatSnapshot` in and `WinProbability` out.

---

## 1. Domain model

### 1.1 Immutable input types (built once per combat, shared read-only across all N rollouts)

```kotlin
// Identity + static description of one minion as it enters combat.
data class MinionSpec(
    val dbfId: Int,
    val name: String,
    val atk: Int,            // displayed atk (blood gems / on-board buffs already baked in)
    val hp: Int,             // displayed hp
    val tavernTier: Int,     // 1..6 ; used for damage calc + start-of-combat ordering
    val tribe: TribeMask,    // bitmask; a minion may be multi-tribe (e.g. All)
    val keywords: KeywordMask,
    val golden: Boolean,
    val bloodGems: Int,      // informational; already in atk/hp
    val deathrattleIds: IntArray,  // ordered effect ids (registry keys)
    val enchantIds: IntArray,      // known combat-relevant enchants (Avenge counters, auras)
    val provenance: Provenance,    // SELF_TRACKED | ENEMY_RECOGNIZED | MANUAL_EDIT
    val confidence: Float          // 0..1 per-minion recognition confidence
)

@JvmInline value class KeywordMask(val bits: Int) {
    companion object {
        const val TAUNT=1; const val DIVINE_SHIELD=2; const val POISONOUS=4
        const val VENOMOUS=8; const val WINDFURY=16; const val MEGA_WINDFURY=32
        const val REBORN=64; const val STEALTH=128; const val CLEAVE=256
    }
}

@JvmInline value class TribeMask(val bits: Int)  // MURLOC, DEMON, MECH, BEAST, DRAGON, PIRATE, ELEMENTAL, QUILBOAR, NAGA, UNDEAD, ALL

data class BoardSnapshot(val minions: List<MinionSpec>)   // left-to-right order preserved

data class HeroPowerSpec(val id: Int, val startOfCombat: Boolean, val payload: IntArray)

data class CombatSnapshot(
    val self: BoardSnapshot,
    val enemy: BoardSnapshot,
    val selfHero: HeroPowerSpec,
    val enemyHero: HeroPowerSpec,
    val startEffects: List<StartOfCombatEffect>,   // hero + minion SoC, tier-ordered lazily at runtime
    val selfLife: Int,
    val enemyLife: Int,
    val selfTavernTier: Int,     // for damage-taken calc
    val enemyTavernTier: Int,
    val mode: BgMode,            // SOLO | DUOS
    val duosContext: DuosContext? = null,
    val enemyConfidence: Float   // aggregate; drives abstain badge
)
```

### 1.2 Mutable runtime state (allocation-free, pooled, reset — never reallocated per rollout)

To hit the perf budget the hot loop must not allocate. Represent the working board as **struct-of-arrays** indexed by slot, one buffer reused across all N sims:

```kotlin
class WorkBoard(maxSlots: Int = 7) {           // 7 board slots per side, +overflow for summons (cap 7 real)
    val dbfId = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val atk   = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val hp    = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val maxHp = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val kw    = IntArray(maxSlots)              // live keyword bits (DS can be stripped mid-combat)
    val tribe = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val tier  = IntArray(maxSlots)
    val flags = IntArray(maxSlots)              // GOLDEN, ATTACKED_THIS_TURN, PENDING_DEATH, WINDFURY_USED
    val drIdx = Array(maxSlots){ EMPTY_INT }    // pointer into a shared deathrattle-id arena
    var count = 0
    var nextAttacker = 0                        // left-to-right pointer
    fun reset(src: BoardSnapshot) { … }         // fill from immutable spec, count set, pointers zeroed
}

class WorkState {
    val a = WorkBoard(); val b = WorkBoard()
    var attackNo = 0
    // per-side counters that persist across the combat:
    var aAvenge = IntArray(...); var bAvenge = ...   // Avenge trigger countdowns
    fun reset(snap: CombatSnapshot) { a.reset(snap.self); b.reset(snap.enemy); attackNo=0 … }
}
```

`MinionState` as an object exists only for the EffectRegistry handler API (a thin cursor `(board, slot)` view) so card handlers read like game text without the hot loop paying object-allocation cost.

---

## 2. Monte-Carlo simulation loop

### 2.1 RNG

`SplitMix64` seeded per rollout from a master seed + iteration index. **Never** `java.util.Random` (synchronized, slow, allocates). One `RngSource` instance reused; `nextInt(bound)` via Lemire's bounded-multiply. Seeding per-iteration deterministically (`masterSeed xor mix(i)`) makes any single rollout reproducible for debugging ("replay rollout #843").

### 2.2 One rollout — `CombatEngine.simulateOnce(state, rng): Outcome`

```
1. START-OF-COMBAT PHASE
   - Collect all start-of-combat sources (hero powers with startOfCombat=true,
     minions like Red Whelp / Prized Promoter / Deflect-o-Bot / Illidan).
   - Order = ascending tavern tier; WITHIN a tier the order is RANDOM (rng.shuffle).
     This is a first-class randomness node — sampled fresh each iteration.
   - Fire each via EffectRegistry.startOfCombat(handler). Resolve any deaths triggered.

2. PICK FIRST ATTACKER
   - side with more minions attacks first; tie => rng coin flip.

3. ATTACK LOOP  (until one/both boards empty, or attackNo > ATTACK_CAP=500)
   attacker side = alternates each iteration of the loop
   a. advance that side's nextAttacker pointer left-to-right, wrapping,
      skipping dead/0-atk minions. If none attackable -> that side is "done";
      if BOTH done -> break.
   b. choose target:
        if any enemy TAUNT (and not stealthed) -> uniform-random among taunts
        else -> uniform-random among all enemy minions
        forced-target overrides (Zapp Slywick -> lowest atk; tie random)
   c. resolve simultaneous strike:
        target.hp -= attacker.atk ; attacker.hp -= target.atk
        Divine Shield absorbs one instance (strip bit, damage=0 for that side)
        Poisonous/Venomous: if dealt >0 damage -> mark target PENDING_DEATH
        Cleave: also damage target's left+right neighbors
        fire onAttack / overkill / on-damage hooks
   d. if attacker has Windfury and hasn't used extra attack -> it attacks again
      (Mega-Windfury = up to 4 total); guarded by ATTACK_CAP
   e. DeathResolver: collect PENDING_DEATH + hp<=0 in board order, then:
        - fire Deathrattles (x2 if Baron Rivendare on that side), in board order
        - Reborn: resummon at 1 HP (once)
        - Avenge counters decrement; fire when they hit 0
        - after-a-friendly-dies chains; Scallywag pirate summons & attacks immediately
        - Monstrous Macaw: after a friendly attacks, re-trigger a friendly deathrattle
        - summon placement: tokens inserted adjacent to source; Khadgar doubles summons
        - deaths caused by deathrattles cascade (loop until stable)
   f. alternate attacker side; attackNo++

4. TERMINATION
   - both empty -> TIE
   - one empty -> other side WINS
   - ATTACK_CAP hit -> declared TIE, flag rollout "capped"

5. DAMAGE
   - winner deals = (sum of surviving minions' tavern tiers) + winner's hero tavern tier
   - Outcome{ result: WIN|TIE|LOSS, damage, capped }
```

`Outcome` is a value class packing (result 2 bits, damage int, flags) — zero allocation.

### 2.3 Aggregation across N iterations

```kotlin
class ResultAccumulator {
    var win=0; var tie=0; var loss=0; var capped=0
    val dmgHistFor = IntArray(MAX_DMG+1)   // damage dealt when YOU win
    val dmgHistAgainst = IntArray(MAX_DMG+1)
    fun add(o: Outcome) { … }
    fun toResult(n:Int): WinProbability {
        val pWin = win.toFloat()/n
        val ci = 1.96f * sqrt(pWin*(1-pWin)/n)   // 95% CI half-width, Wald
        // lethal: P(you die) = share of loss rollouts whose damage >= selfLife
        // P(opp dies) = share of win rollouts whose damage >= enemyLife
        …
    }
}
```

`WinProbability` output:
```kotlin
data class WinProbability(
    val winPct: Float, val tiePct: Float, val lossPct: Float,
    val ciHalfWidth: Float,          // "±2%"
    val expectedDamageDealt: Float, val expectedDamageTaken: Float,
    val histogramDealt: IntArray, val histogramTaken: IntArray,
    val pYouDie: Float, val pOpponentDies: Float,
    val summaryText: String,         // "you usually win by 4"
    val confidence: Confidence,      // OK | APPROXIMATE | ABSTAIN
    val coverageFlags: List<String>, // "uncommon card X modeled as vanilla"
    val iterations: Int, val cappedCount: Int, val elapsedMs: Long,
    val teamOutcome: DuosOutcome? = null
)
```

Statistics: stderr of a proportion `= sqrt(p(1-p)/N)`; N=1000 → ±1.5% @ p=0.5, N=2000 → ±1.1%. Ample for a HUD number.

---

## 3. Mechanics: modeled vs approximated (correctness-vs-scope table)

| Mechanic | v1 | v2 | Notes / hardest bits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attack order (more-minions-first, alternating, L→R pointer, wrap, skip 0-atk) | ✅ Full | | Core; well-specified |
| Target selection (taunt-first, uniform random, Zapp=lowest atk) | ✅ Full | | |
| Divine Shield (absorb one instance) | ✅ Full | | |
| Taunt / Stealth | ✅ Full | | Stealth removed on attack |
| Poisonous / Venomous | ✅ Full | | Venomous decays after one kill |
| Windfury / Mega-Windfury | ✅ Full | | Interacts with ATTACK_CAP |
| Reborn | ✅ Full | | Resummon at 1 HP, once |
| Cleave (target + neighbors) | ✅ Full | | Neighbor indices from live SoA layout |
| Deathrattles (board-order, cascade) | ✅ Registry | | Data-driven; unknown DR → flagged |
| Baron Rivendare (double DR) | ✅ Full | | |
| Avenge counters | ✅ Registry | | Per-side countdown in WorkState |
| Start-of-combat (hero powers + Red Whelp/Deflect-o-Bot/Prized Promoter/Illidan) | ✅ Registry | | **Tier-then-random ordering = major RNG node** |
| Scallywag pirate (summon + immediate attack) | ✅ Full | | Injects an out-of-turn attack |
| Monstrous Macaw (re-trigger friendly DR) | ✅ Full | | after-friendly-attacks hook; ordering-sensitive |
| Khadgar (double summons) | ✅ Full | | Multiplies token counts incl. Scallywag chains |
| Summon placement (adjacent to source) | ✅ Full | | SoA insert-with-shift, respect 7-slot cap |
| Adjacency / combat auras (e.g. Murozond, Whelp Smuggler on-attack) | ⚠️ Common ones | ✅ Full | Recompute on board change; v1 covers frequent cards |
| Blood gems | ✅ Static | | Already baked into displayed atk/hp; pending-only gems v2 |
| Hidden enchantments (secret +X/+X) | ❌ (invisible to recognition) | ⚠️ Manual-edit only | Recognition ceiling, not engine limit |
| Duos (shared life, teammate-support minions, cross-board portals) | ⚠️ Basic | ✅ Full | Own combat variant, not a bolt-on |
| Quest rewards / hero-power start effects (enemy) | ⚠️ if recognized | | Usually invisible pre-combat |
| Exotic new-set cards | Vanilla + FLAG | Registry update | Ships as data table, not engine edit |

**Honest caveat carried forward** (twanvl/Firestone/HDT all share it): exact simultaneous-death trigger ordering can differ a few % from live. Acceptable **only if disclosed** via the `APPROXIMATE` badge.

### Hardest mechanics (call-outs)
1. **Start-of-combat tier-then-random ordering** — dominant pre-combat RNG; must reshuffle within-tier each iteration or win% is biased.
2. **Macaw + Scallywag + Baron + Khadgar interaction** — nested re-triggers and summon-doubling; the DeathResolver must be a **fixpoint loop** over a work-queue, not a single pass, with the ATTACK_CAP as the infinite-chain guard.
3. **Windfury mirrors / Macaw loops** — can theoretically not terminate; hard `ATTACK_CAP=500` → declared TIE, flagged `capped`.
4. **Summon placement + SoA insertion** — shifting slots while pointers (nextAttacker) and Avenge indices are live; keep a stable id or recompute pointers after every structural change.

---

## 4. Off-thread execution plan

```kotlin
class CombatSimulator(
    private val engine: CombatEngine,
    private val detector: DeterminismDetector,
    private val defaultDispatcher: CoroutineDispatcher = Dispatchers.Default
) {
    suspend fun run(
        snapshot: CombatSnapshot,
        iterations: Int = 2000,
        budgetMs: Long = 250
    ): WinProbability = withContext(defaultDispatcher) {
        // 1. Determinism short-circuit
        if (detector.isDeterministic(snapshot)) {
            val o = engine.simulateOnce(freshState(snapshot), NoOpRng)
            return@withContext singleResult(o)   // stable, no jitter
        }
        // 2. Chunked Monte-Carlo with cancellation + wall-clock budget
        val acc = ResultAccumulator()
        val deadline = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() + budgetMs
        val work = WorkState()                    // reused across all iterations
        var i = 0
        while (i < iterations) {
            val end = min(i + CHUNK /*=128*/, iterations)
            while (i < end) {
                work.reset(snapshot)
                acc.add(engine.simulateOnce(work, rngFor(i)))
                i++
            }
            ensureActive()                         // cooperative cancellation
            if (SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() > deadline) {
                acc.markPartial(); break           // return partial, flag approximate
            }
            yield()                                // let dispatcher breathe
        }
        acc.toResult(i).withConfidence(snapshot)
    }
}
```

Integration discipline (protects the PDS zero-freeze / 99.99% mandate):

- **One debounced in-flight job.** The overlay owns a `Job?`; a new recognition frame or manual edit **cancels** the previous job (structured concurrency) rather than queueing. Debounce ~120 ms so rapid enemy-board re-reads don't thrash.
- **Dispatchers.Default only** — never `Main`. The engine module has no way to touch the UI thread by construction (no Android imports).
- **Chunked `yield()` + `ensureActive()`** so cancellation is prompt and the pool of Default threads never starves.
- **Hard caps**: `ATTACK_CAP=500` per rollout, `budgetMs≈250` wall-clock. A tripped cap returns the partial aggregate flagged `APPROXIMATE`; the sim **always returns**.
- **Fan-out (optional)**: split N across cores (`k` coroutines, N/k each), merge accumulators. Single-thread already meets budget (each rollout tens of µs when allocation-free), so this is a later knob, not v1.
- **N auto-tune**: start N=2000; if elapsed < ~40 ms and CI still wide, the orchestrator may raise N on the next run; on a thermally throttled device it lowers N to hold the 300 ms ceiling. Budget is the master; N is advisory.

---

## 5. Inputs from recognition + manual-correction fallback

### 5.1 Data flow
```
GameStateStore (StateFlow) ──► self BoardSnapshot        (PERFECT info: dbfId, atk/hp, keywords, DR, gems)
RecognitionResult ───────────► enemy BoardSnapshot        (per-minion + aggregate confidence)
ManualEditOverride ──────────► overrides enemy (or self)   (treated as PERFECT info, confidence=1)
                              └► SnapshotBuilder ──► CombatSnapshot ──► CombatSimulator
```

- **Your board** = read from `GameStateStore`, not the screen — exact. Includes buffs baked into atk/hp, keywords, tribe, golden/triple, blood-gem count, deathrattle/enchant provenance, your hero power.
- **Enemy board** = the hard part. Only fully visible in the ~1 s combat-preview window (exactly when the sim is wanted). Recognition reads per minion: identity (ML Kit OCR name + Gemini vision fallback), displayed atk/hp, tribe, visible keyword glyphs (DS gold border, Taunt frame, Poison/Venom drip, Reborn, Windfury, Stealth), and **position** (readable, and it matters).
- **Realistically unreadable** (bounds usefulness): hidden enchantments (secret +X/+X in tooltips), unsurfaced deathrattle/magnetic payloads, pending auras vs merged gems, the enemy hero power and their start-of-combat effects, ambiguous golden-vs-normal. These are recognition ceilings, **flagged**, never silently guessed.

### 5.2 Confidence → behavior
- Each `MinionSpec.confidence` and `CombatSnapshot.enemyConfidence` drive a threshold gate:
  - `enemyConfidence ≥ 0.85` → `OK`, show number.
  - `0.6 – 0.85` → `APPROXIMATE` badge ("~62% (±2%)").
  - `< 0.6` → `ABSTAIN` — **do not** show a confident-but-wrong number; show "board unclear — tap to edit".
- A **single misread keyword** (DS/Poison/Taunt/Reborn) or wrong HP can swing win% by tens of points. Abstention is the safety valve.

### 5.3 Manual board editor (Firestone-style, mandatory fallback)
- Compose UI: two 7-slot rows (yours pre-filled, enemy from recognition). Drag to reorder, tap a minion to set atk/hp, toggle keyword chips (Taunt/DS/Poison/Venom/Windfury/Reborn/Stealth), pick tribe, mark golden, add a deathrattle from a searchable card picker (bundled HearthstoneJSON, Spanish-first).
- Every edit produces a `ManualEditOverride`, rebuilds the `CombatSnapshot`, **cancels the in-flight job and re-runs live** (debounced). User corrects in seconds; the % updates.
- Recognition pre-highlights low-confidence minions ("this one's unsure — check it") so the user fixes the exact cells that matter.

---

## 6. Output rendering: overlay HUD + AI chat

### 6.1 Overlay HUD widget (`TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY`, drawn over the game)
- Compact pill during the combat-preview window:
  - **`62% W · 11% T · 27% L (±2%)`** — win/tie/loss with CI.
  - Lethal line, the single most decision-relevant number: **`☠ opp 34%`** / **`⚠ you 8%`** = P(opponent dies) / P(you die) given both life totals.
  - Mini bar chart from the damage histogram; averaged summary "usually win by 4".
  - Confidence chip: green `OK`, amber `~approx`, grey `abstain — tap to edit` (opens the manual editor).
  - If `coverageFlags` non-empty: small "modeled approximately (card X)" note. **Never imply false precision** — always rounded, always the CI, always label approximations.
- The HUD subscribes to a `StateFlow<WinProbability>`; the sim writes results off-thread and the widget just renders — no computation on the render path.

### 6.2 Grounded AI chat feed
- The latest `WinProbability` + both boards are injected as **structured context** into the Gemini chat prompt so the assistant answers grounded questions: "should I hero-power?", "sell the Scallywag or keep it?", "do I reposition my Taunt?".
- The chat can request a **counterfactual re-run**: the assistant proposes a board change (e.g. "move Baron left of your Ghoul"), calls the sim on a hypothetical `CombatSnapshot`, and reports the delta ("that raises win% from 47% to 58%"). This is the same off-thread `CombatSimulator.run`, just fed an edited snapshot.
- Markdown rendering follows the existing DeckView chat mandate: off-thread parse, virtualized `LazyColumn`, `PrecomputedText` — the sim result is small structured data, not a UI-thread hazard.

---

## 7. Testing & correctness harness
- **JVM unit tests** on `engine` (no Android): deterministic-RNG rollouts assert exact outcomes for hand-authored boards (DS absorption, Poison kill, Windfury count, Reborn, Cleave neighbors, Baron-doubled DR, Macaw/Scallywag/Khadgar chains).
- **Replay regression harness**: fixtures of known real combats (board in → known outcome distribution). Assert aggregate win% within CI + a fixed seed for reproducibility. **Gated on each patch bump** of the bundled card data.
- **Determinism detector test**: no-RNG combats must short-circuit to 1 rollout and produce a stable %.
- **Perf test**: N=2000 must complete < 100 ms on a mid-range reference device profile; loop must allocate ~0 bytes (allocation assertion in a JMH-style microbench).
- **EffectRegistry coverage report**: any `dbfId` hitting the vanilla fallback is logged so the coverage table can be maintained per patch. Unknown card → vanilla stats+keywords + `coverageFlags` entry, never a silent divergence.

---

## Bottom line (design honesty)
Compute is the easy part — 1–2k allocation-free rollouts finish in well under 100 ms off-thread, and the caps guarantee it never janks the overlay. The **real accuracy ceiling is the enemy-board read**, glimpsed for ~1 s with tiny atk/hp text, subtle keyword glyphs, and genuinely invisible hidden enchantments/hero powers. So the module's trustworthiness rests on three things it must ship with, not just the Monte-Carlo core: (1) per-minion **confidence + abstain** instead of confident-wrong numbers, (2) the **manual board editor** that lets the user correct in seconds and re-runs live, and (3) a **data-driven, patch-updatable EffectRegistry** with a replay regression harness so new cards degrade to flagged-approximate rather than silent error.

=== MASTER ROADMAP ===
# DeckView — Master Roadmap: All-Modes Feature Parity on the v1 Backbone

## Framing

The v1 backbone already ships the shared spine (MediaProjection capture, phase/mode classifier, anchor-ROI normalization, GameStateStore, bundled HearthstoneJSON, deck-code decode, anti-jank Markdown chat, overlay HUD) **and Standard/Wild constructed**. This roadmap layers the remaining modes as value-ordered epics. Two hard constraints drive every sequencing call:

1. **Recognition honesty.** Firestone/HDT read `Power.log` (perfect entity truth); we read pixels. Value is gated by how readable a mode's surface is, not by how hard the compute is.
2. **STABILITY-FIRST / PDS Gold Rule.** Every epic re-certifies zero-crash/zero-freeze **before ship**, not after.

**Fact-check correction to the suggested epic list:** the task's example named "E4 Twist" and "E5 Mercenaries." **Twist was removed (Patch 35.4, ~May 5 2026) — there is NO Twist epic.** Duels (Apr 2024) and Classic (Jun 2023) are also gone. Mercenaries is playable but frozen in permanent maintenance since Feb 2023 → lowest-priority "could." Epics are renumbered to reflect the real 2026 mode census.

---

## Cross-cutting gate: the Stability Re-Certification Checklist (every epic runs this before ship)

A mode epic is **not** "done" until:
- **Zero-freeze proof:** no new work on the UI/render thread. All parse/sim/OCR off-thread (Dispatchers.Default), overlay only renders `StateFlow`. Frame-time regression run against the `spike` harness (the very tool that caught the original long-markdown main-thread freeze); no `inter_ms` freeze regression vs. baseline.
- **Abstain-on-low-confidence wired:** the mode's recognizers show "unclear — tap to edit" rather than a confident-wrong overlay.
- **Mode-gate correct:** the phase/mode classifier fires this mode's overlays *only* in this mode (no constructed tracker leaking onto un-trackable decks).
- **Practice-mode regression harness** (see E1) green for any recognition stack the epic touches.
- **Cost/licensing sign-off** for any external data added (see the data section).

---

## Phased epics (value- and recognition-ordered)

### E0 — Shared platform hardening (prerequisite, small)
**Goal:** make the backbone's shared services multi-mode-ready before adding modes.
**Scope:** extend the phase/mode classifier to emit the full 2026 mode enum (Constructed/BG/Arena/Brawl/Practice/Friendly/Mercs/menu/mulligan/combat/draft/end); add the **End-of-game result reader** (Victory/Defeat/placement/rank medal) and the **local Room stats DB** (session, streaks, history, MMR/placement time-series) as shared services; formalize the **generic observed-card overlay** ("seen," never "remaining") as a reusable component.
**Acceptance:** classifier ≥ target accuracy on a labeled mode-transition set with abstain fallback; result reader + stats DB feed a live counter across ≥2 modes; stability checklist green.

### E1 — Constructed parity completion + QA harness (highest value, lowest recognition risk)
**Goal:** close the gap between v1's basic Standard/Wild tracker and full HDT-class constructed parity, and stand up the regression harness the whole product leans on.
**Scope (must/should first):** opponent played-card log + hand/deck counts; turn/mana tracker; own cards-left + hypergeometric next-draw math; **opponent archetype/MetaDetector** (Stats-DB); **mulligan advisor** (Stats-DB); deck win-rate/matchup + local match history; deck import/export management. **Ship the Practice-vs-AI full-support build as the zero-risk regression harness for every recognizer** (ordinary decks, offline, deterministic).
**Deliberately deferred to "could":** secrets helper, fatigue/overdraw, attack/lethal, created-by oracle — all abstain-heavy pixel-ceiling features; ship as flagged/abstaining, not confident.
**Acceptance:** on Practice harness, tracker reconstructs a known decklist's draw sequence within tolerance; archetype + mulligan overlays read fixed layouts or abstain; stability checklist green. **Rationale for going first:** reuses the backbone almost entirely, delivers the most-used mode, and the Practice harness de-risks every later epic.

### E2 — Battlegrounds core + Combat Simulator (flagship value, hardest recognition — sequenced honestly)
**Goal:** BG parity including the required first-class combat win-% simulator.
**Two-stage sequencing — this is the key honesty call:**
- **E2a — Static/high-reliability BG first (ship early):** Hero Pick Advisor (large static portraits → highest-reliability BG feature), Trinket advisor, Anomaly/Buddy panel, tavern odds by tier, tier-list/minion-pool browser, triple tracking (your own), MMR/placement. These are readable, static-screen, Stats-DB features that deliver BG value *before* the hard part. **Quests are removed in 2026 — do not build.**
- **E2b — Combat simulator (the crown jewel, gated behind the enemy-board read):** ship the `modes/bg/sim` module (pure Kotlin/JVM, SoA allocation-free Monte-Carlo, N≈2000, <100 ms off-thread, ATTACK_CAP=500, budget≈250 ms, determinism short-circuit, structured-concurrency single debounced job). **The compute is the easy part; trustworthiness rests on three ship-blockers:** (1) per-minion **confidence + abstain** (≥0.85 OK / 0.6–0.85 approximate / <0.6 abstain), (2) the **manual board editor** (two 7-slot rows, keyword chips, DR picker) that re-runs live on edit, (3) the **data-driven patch-updatable EffectRegistry** with a **replay regression harness** so unknown cards degrade to flagged-vanilla, never silent error.
**Acceptance:** JVM unit tests pass for DS/Poison/Windfury/Reborn/Cleave/Baron/Macaw-Scallywag-Khadgar chains; replay fixtures land within CI; N=2000 <100 ms with ~0-byte allocation; determinism detector short-circuits; enemy-board low-confidence path shows abstain + editor, never a confident-wrong %; the sim **always returns** (cap/budget flagged APPROXIMATE); stability checklist green.
**Explicitly deferred:** shared 8-player pool depletion (unobservable → "seen so far" approximation or defer), opponents' triples/leveling times (infeasible), **Duos → v2** (teammate board *is* visible; model as its own combat variant, not a bolt-on).

### E3 — Arena + The Underground (high value, recognition-fragile draft screen)
**Goal:** Arena parity with the live draft pick helper as the make-or-break feature.
**Scope:** **Live draft pick helper** (read 3 or 4-in-Legendary-Group offered cards, handle Dual-Class banners + Legendary Groups, on-device ranking over *refreshed* tier scores) → in-run deck tracker assembled from 30 captured picks (then reuse the constructed pipeline) → synergy/curve hints, hero/class pick helper, run record + mode-context (Arena vs Underground), tier-list freshness. **Underground Re-Draft-on-Loss assistant** is a "could" (distinct screen + extra state machine).
**Acceptance:** pick helper reads the offer set or **abstains** (gated strictly to the draft screen, robust to seasonal reskins); captured 30-pick decklist drives the in-run tracker; reward-contents OCR is best-effort/flagged; stability checklist green.
**Rationale for after BG:** high value but UI-fragile across seasonal reskins, and its in-run tracker *reuses* E1's constructed pipeline — so E1 must land first.

### E4 — Tavern Brawl / Friendly (moderate value, mostly reuse — NOT Twist)
**Goal:** honest brawl-lane parity. **Reference trackers do almost nothing brawl-specific; a per-brawl decklist DB is not a real parity gap — do not build it.**
**Scope:** the **mode gate** (stops the constructed tracker firing on unknowable/prebuilt decks — a *stability* feature); brawl-type auto-classification (prebuilt/deckbuild/PvE → abstain + show nothing rather than garbage); **Brawliseum/Heroic Brawl run tracking** (player brings a real constructed deck → full tracker + Arena-style W/L scoreboard — the highest-value brawl feature); Friendly Challenge support; weekly-brawl info card in chat (fuzzy-match bundled catalog, may lag a brand-new brawl).
**Acceptance:** prebuilt/PvE brawls correctly produce **no** confident overlay; Brawliseum reuses the constructed tracker end-to-end; stability checklist green.
**Note:** Twist's experimental-format role folded into rotating brawls; if Blizzard revives it, it arrives here as brawl content — no separate epic.

### E5 — Mercenaries (lowest priority — defer unless Ignacio asks)
**Goal:** optional support for a frozen, low-population, non-deck RPG mode.
**Rationale:** maintenance-mode since Feb 2023 (data won't drift, so a one-time build stays valid, but audience is shrinking); icon-dense bespoke UI is materially harder than card OCR; needs a **separate community Mercs DB** (not in HearthstoneJSON). All features "could," abstain-heavy (speed ties + hidden opponent abilities are irreducibly probabilistic). **Recommendation: defer** past E4 unless the product owner explicitly wants it.

### E6 — v2 depth (after parity)
BG **Duos** (shared-life combat variant), BG shared-pool depletion, secrets/fatigue/lethal "could" features graduating from abstain to approximate where a better read is proven, Underground re-draft, richer provenance hints. Not parity-blocking.

---

## Recommended build order + rationale

**E0 → E1 → E2a → E2b → E3 → E4 → (E5 deferred) → E6**

- **E1 before everything mode-specific:** most-played mode, near-total backbone reuse, and it ships the **Practice regression harness** that de-risks every subsequent recognizer. Highest value / lowest risk = go first.
- **BG split E2a/E2b is the central honesty move:** BG is the flagship and the combat sim is a *must*, but the sim's accuracy is capped by a ~1 s enemy-board glimpse (tiny atk/hp, subtle glyphs, invisible enchants/hero-powers). Shipping E2a (static, highly-readable hero/trinket/odds/tier features) first delivers real BG value immediately; E2b then ships the sim **with its three trust ship-blockers**, so users never see a confident-wrong number. Compute is easy and fast; the enemy read is the risk, so the editor + abstain + registry are the actual deliverable, not the Monte-Carlo core.
- **E3 after E1 + E2:** high value but its in-run tracker depends on E1's constructed pipeline, and its draft-screen read is seasonally fragile — worth doing once the harness and abstain patterns are mature.
- **E4 mostly reuse; its mode-gate is really a stability feature** protecting earlier epics from firing on un-trackable brawl decks — cheap, high-safety.
- **E5 deferred** on ROI (frozen mode, separate DB, hardest UI, shrinking audience).

---

## External meta-stats data — dependency, cost & licensing flags

Several features are **Stats-DB** and cannot be computed on-device; they need an external meta corpus mirrored server-side and shipped as **periodic offline bundles** through the **LyAi backend proxy** (never live per-query):

| Feature (epic) | External source | Flag |
|---|---|---|
| Opponent archetype / MetaDetector, mulligan win-rates, deck win-rate/matchup, discover stats (E1) | HSReplay-style meta corpus | **HSReplay has no open data API.** Stats must be mirrored server-side and shipped as offline bundles; DeckView **cannot upload replays** (no Power.log). |
| BG hero/trinket/minion tier data, comp tier lists (E2) | Firestone / HSReplay / wiki | Free-tier as specced. |
| Arena draft tier scores (E3) — **must refresh, not bundle statically** | HSReplay / HearthArena / Firestone Arena scores | Freshness is load-bearing for the pick helper; refresh cadence via proxy. |
| BG anomalies/buddies/tavern-odds, brawl catalog (E2/E4) | Wiki (no official API) | Fuzzy-match bundled catalog; can lag brand-new content. |
| Mercs DB (E5) | Community Mercs datasets | **Not in HearthstoneJSON** — separate bundled DB required. |

**Cost/licensing posture (LyAi rules):** all named sources (HSReplay, Firestone, HearthArena, wiki, HearthstoneJSON) are **free-tier → no ≥$0.10 authorization needed as specced**. **BUT:** before ingesting HSReplay/Firestone/HearthArena data server-side, **confirm each source's ToS/licensing for redistribution as offline bundles** — that's a legal gate, not a cost gate, and must clear before E1 (archetype/mulligan) and E3 (Arena scores) ship. Gemini 2.5-flash (chat + vision fallback) stays free-tier; any move off free tier needs Ignacio's authorization.

---

## One-line summary
Ship **E1 constructed parity + Practice harness** first (highest value, lowest risk, de-risks everything after), then **BG in two honest stages** — static advisors before the recognition-hard combat sim, which ships only with confidence/abstain + manual editor + patch-updatable registry — then **Arena** (reuses E1, fragile draft read), then the mostly-reuse **Brawl lane**; **defer Mercenaries**, and **do not build Twist/Duels/Classic (removed)**. Every epic clears the stability re-cert gate before it ships, and every Stats-DB feature routes through the LyAi proxy as free-tier offline bundles pending a redistribution-licensing check.

### **Claude** `01:38`

# DeckView — All-Modes Feature Plan

**Audience:** Ignacio (product owner) · **Status:** Proposal, extends the approved v1 backbone · **Date:** 2026-07-14 · **Package:** `dev.lyai.deckview.*`

This plan layers **all-modes feature parity** onto the already-approved v1 backbone. It does **not** re-describe backbone internals — it builds on them by name: MediaProjection capture service, phase/mode classifier, anchor-ROI normalization, `GameStateStore` (StateFlow), bundled HearthstoneJSON, deck-code decode, the anti-jank Markdown AI chat, the overlay HUD, and the shipped Standard/Wild constructed tracker. v1 covered constructed only; everything below is what we add.

---

## 0. Reading this plan — the honesty frame that governs every feature

Two constraints override every priority call. Read them first; they are why some "obvious" Firestone/HDT features are labeled abstain, flag, or non-goal rather than "must."

**A. We read pixels, not `Power.log`.** Firestone and Hearthstone Deck Tracker read Hearthstone's local `Power.log` — perfect, entity-level ground truth (provenance, hidden triggers, every board, every zone). DeckView sees only rendered frames. Four consequences that the rest of this document treats as law:

1. **There is no "perfect info" source — not even your own board.** Your board is *higher-confidence* than the enemy's (bigger render, stable, you control timing, and `GameStateStore` carries it across turns) but it is still **pixel-derived inference**. Hidden self-enchants, exact keyword state, and deathrattle identity all ride on recognition. Any claim of "self = exact, enemy = the only hard part" is `Power.log` thinking we cannot do. **Both sides are estimates**; we attach a confidence to each.
2. **Two different recognition primitives, not one.** *Named surfaces* — hand, mulligan, draft, shop, played-card animation — carry a text banner and are read by **ML Kit OCR** (offline). *In-play board minions carry no name banner* — only art + stat numbers — so board identity is **CV artwork-matching** against a bundled art index (hundreds of minions × golden variants, small render, buff/animation overlays), never OCR. The BG combat board is the CV-hardest surface we have.
3. **Gemini vision is a static-screen tool only.** A network round-trip returns *after* the ~1 s BG combat-preview window is gone. Vision usefully assists non-time-critical static screens (hero pick, draft, shop) and never the live board read where we need it most. On-device CV is the only thing fast enough for combat.
4. **Nothing is "exact."** "Cards-left" and "hypergeometric next-draw" are only as good as a lossy pixel inference that a single missed card-into-hand frame, off-turn draw, tutor, shuffle/mill, or mulligan swap can desync permanently. We label these **inferred**, expose a confidence, and offer manual correction — we never print a false-precision number.

The universal safety valve is **abstain-on-low-confidence**: show "unclear — tap to edit," never a confident-wrong overlay. This is the PDS Gold Rule applied to recognition.

**B. STABILITY-FIRST / PDS Gold Rule — zero crash, zero freeze, 99.99%.** On a phone this is *harder* than on PC, and the backbone's fix for the original long-Markdown main-thread freeze is necessary but not sufficient. This plan adds mobile-specific hardening that PC trackers never needed: thermal/contention governance (we share the phone's CPU/GPU with the running game), GC-pause control at real device resolution (production is 1080p+, not the 800×360 spike harness), MediaProjection lifecycle recovery (Android 14/15 kill capture on app-switch/call/background), self-capture exclusion (the overlay must not be captured and CV-matched as if it were the game), non-interactive overlay (must never steal a touch from Hearthstone), and streaming-chat re-render throttling. These live in §4 and are gating items in every epic's stability re-certification (§6).

**What "parity" honestly means here.** We match Firestone/HDT on everything a read-only pixel observer *can* deliver, and we are explicit about the residue that a pixels-only mobile tool *cannot* — those ship as abstain, flag, or declared non-goal (§2.7), not as silent gaps or over-promises.

## 2. Per-mode feature matrix

**Legend.** **Prio:** must / should / could. **Recog:** recognition difficulty for our capture+OCR/CV/vision stack — **Low** (fixed high-contrast ROI, numbers/glyphs, no card ID), **Med** (named-surface OCR or large static art), **High** (in-play CV art-matching and/or invisible modifiers → abstain-heavy). **Compute:** Deterministic / Stats-DB / Sim / Hybrid / CV. Reliability labels are recalibrated to the honesty frame in §0 — no feature is "exact" or "perfect."

### 2.1 Constructed — Standard + Wild (identical pipeline)

| Feature | Prio | Recog | Compute | Honest can / can't-do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Own deck / cards-left tracker | must | Med | Deterministic | Works **only** with an imported deck code (no `Power.log` to reconstruct the list). Draws are **inferred** from card-into-hand motion; **can desync permanently** on a missed frame, off-turn draw, tutor, shuffle/mill, or mulligan swap. Expose confidence + "resync" affordance; **not** billed as exact. |
| Turn / mana-crystal tracker | must | Low | Deterministic | Fixed high-contrast ROI, no card ID. The one genuinely reliable constructed read. |
| Opponent played-card log + hand/deck counts | must | Med | Deterministic | Logs **visibly-played** cards (played animation is a named surface) + card-back fan count. **No** created-by/provenance tags (invisible in pixels). |
| Opponent archetype / MetaDetector | should | Med | Stats-DB | Needs only class + visible cards. **Blocked on a redistribution-licensed meta corpus (§5) — not free.** |
| Mulligan advisor + kept-% | should | Med | Stats-DB | Reads 3–4 mulligan cards (named surface); abstain if unreadable. **Same licensing gate as archetype.** |
| Card-draw / next-draw probability | should | Low | Deterministic | Correct hypergeometric math, but its accuracy is **inherited from the inferred cards-left count** above — presented with that caveat, not as certainty. |
| Deck win-rate & matchup stats | should | Low | Stats-DB | Data/sync feature. **Licensing gate (§5).** |
| Local deck stats & match history | should | Low | Deterministic | Victory/Defeat splash ROI + local Room DB. On-device, no licensing issue. |
| Deck import / export / management | should | Low | Deterministic | User-pasted code; HearthstoneJSON decode. Anchor for all deck tracking. Fully supportable. |
| **Persistent gameplay counters** (DK Corpse/Rune, Galakrond Invoke, C'Thun pieces, Spell-damage, Excavate progress, Elemental-played, Overload, etc.) | should | Med–High | Deterministic (fragile) | **New — closes a real HDT/Firestone gap.** *Degrades by counter:* on-screen counters (Corpse) are directly readable; **cross-turn tallies** (Invokes, Elementals-played-this-game, C'Thun assembly) need a running count we must accumulate from every observed turn — **one missed turn desyncs them**, so they ship **flagged "inferred"** with abstain, never authoritative. |
| **Questline / sidequest progress** | should | Med | Hybrid | **New.** Questline card + progress pips are on-screen when active; track progress from observed plays, abstain if steps missed. |
| Secrets helper (list + cross out disproven) | could | High | Hybrid | List candidate secrets reliably; **eliminations hinging on fast/near-frame triggers are error-prone → abstain, never wrongly cross out.** |
| Discover / draft-choice stats overlay | could | Med | Stats-DB | 3 on-screen options are a named surface; abstain if any unreadable. Licensing gate. |
| Fatigue / overdraw tracking | could | High | Deterministic (fragile) | Desyncs permanently on one missed draw/mill → **approximate only, anchored to the empty-deck visual.** |
| Attack / lethal helper | could | High | Deterministic | Needs every buffed stat/aura/keyword read correctly → **abstain unless confident.** |
| Created-by / buffed-by "oracle" | could | High | Lookup (hints only) | **Largely unsupportable** — true provenance is a `Power.log` feature. Only generic "this class generates X" hints. |
| Tavern Brawl support | could | Med | Reuse constructed | See §2.4 — disable own-deck tracker on prebuilt/random-deck brawls. |

### 2.2 Battlegrounds (Solo + Duos)

| Feature | Prio | Recog | Compute | Honest can / can't-do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Combat win-% simulator** (win/tie/loss, exp. dmg, P(lethal)) | **must** | **High** | **Sim** | See §3. Compute is easy; the ceiling is the **~1 s enemy-board CV read** plus invisible modifiers (trinkets, tavern-spell buffs, hero powers, hidden enchants). **Manual editor + per-minion confidence + abstain are mandatory ship-blockers** — the sim is only as good as the read, and **both boards are estimates.** |
| Hero Pick Advisor | must | Med | Stats-DB | Large static portraits on a fixed screen → **highest-reliability BG feature.** Stats licensing gate (§5). |
| Trinket Pick Advisor (Lesser T6 / Greater T9) | should | Med | Stats-DB | Fixed choice screen; context-ranked by warband. **Also must feed the sim (below), not just advise the pick.** |
| **Tavern Spell advisor** | should | Med | Stats-DB | **New.** Tavern spells are a live 2024→2026 mechanic; advise on the buy screen. |
| **Anomaly context panel** | should | Med | Static/Stats-DB | Anomaly banner is fixed at game start (live per §1). **Buddies panel dropped — removed from the game.** |
| Tavern odds by tier | should | Low | Static lookup | Read the tier number only; pure lookup. |
| Tavern-tier minion browser (pool) | should | Low | Static filter | Read active tribe set to filter; degrades to "all tribes." |

| **Battlegrounds Duos** | **must** (for parity) | High | Extends BG state model | **Reclassified from v1's "could/v2."** Duos is a co-equal permanent mode; we do **not** claim "BG parity" without it. Teammate board **is** visible (unlike Solo opponents) → model shared HP + the pass/portal mechanics as a first-class combat variant (E2c, §6). |

### 2.3 Arena + The Underground

| Draft synergy & composition hints | should | — | On-device | Derived from captured picks; no extra screen reading. |
| Hero / class pick helper | should | Med | Hybrid | Per-class win rates + local history; fragile across reskins → gate + abstain. |
| Run record, rewards & Arena-vs-Underground context | should | Med | On-device | Win/loss reliable; **exact reward contents (packs/gold/tickets) = unreliable OCR → best-effort/flagged.** |
| Arena tier-list / current-set freshness | should | — | Backend proxy | Pure data-freshness; **scores must refresh via the proxy, not ship statically** — and see the licensing gate. |
| Underground Re-Draft-on-Loss assistant | could | High | Hybrid | Distinct re-draft screen; surface the weakest 5 and reconcile swaps into the tracked list — an extra state machine. |

### 2.4 Tavern Brawl / Practice / Friendly

**Honest parity note:** Firestone/HDT do almost nothing brawl-specific (brawls rotate weekly, often prebuilt/random decks). A per-brawl decklist DB is **not** a real parity gap — do not build it. Our mode-gate + Brawliseum reuse + generic observed overlay **is** at parity.

| Feature | Prio | Recog | Compute | Honest can / can't-do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mode gate: Brawl / Practice / Friendly detection | must | Med | On-device | **Stability feature** — stops the constructed tracker firing on unknowable decks (else confidently-wrong overlays). |
| Brawl-type auto-classification (prebuilt / deckbuild / PvE) | should | High | Hybrid | Decides which overlay (if any). **Abstain + show nothing rather than garbage.** |
| Brawliseum / Heroic run tracking | should | Low | Deterministic | Player brings a real constructed deck → full tracker + Arena-style W/L scoreboard. **Highest-value brawl feature.** |
| Practice (vs AI) full support + **QA harness** | should | Low | On-device | Ordinary decks, offline, deterministic → **the zero-risk regression harness for the whole recognition stack (E1).** |
| Friendly Challenge support | should | Low | On-device | Own deck importable; opponent via generic overlay. |
| Weekly-brawl info card in chat | could | Med | Hybrid | OCR title → fuzzy-match a bundled catalog; can lag a brand-new brawl. |
| Ranked-vs-Casual awareness + rank medal read | could | Med | On-device | Recognition-identical to constructed; additive context only. |

> Prebuilt-deck and PvE/random brawls are **fundamentally untrackable** (the deck is not the player's and not knowable) → abstain, don't guess.

### 2.5 Mercenaries — DEFER (frozen since Feb 2023)

Not a deck game (RPG party combat); reference trackers do little; icon-dense bespoke UI is materially harder than card OCR; needs a **separate community Mercs DB** (not in HearthstoneJSON). Upside: the data set is frozen, so a one-time build stays valid. **Recommendation: defer past E4** unless you want the shrinking audience. If built, every feature is a "could," abstain-heavy — speed ties resolve randomly and opponent abilities are hidden until revealed, so initiative/cooldown prediction is **irreducibly probabilistic, never certain.** Full sub-matrix available on request; omitted here to keep scope honest.

### 2.6 Shared / cross-mode services (build once, reuse everywhere)

Extends the backbone's shared spine. New or expanded here:

| Service | Prio | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| End-of-game result reader (Victory/Defeat splash, placement, rank medal) | should | Feeds all session/history/MMR stats across modes. |
| Local Room/SQLite stats DB (session, streaks, match history, MMR/placement time-series) | should | On-device, StateFlow-backed; one store for all modes. No licensing issue. |
| Generic observed-card / opponent play-log overlay | should | Reused as the opponent tracker in every mode; surfaces "seen," **never "remaining."** |
| **Rewards Track XP / daily-weekly quests / achievement progress** | could | **New — flagged, not silently dropped.** A Firestone marquee. Partly readable from on-screen reward/quest panels; **account-level history is recognition-hard and un-reconstructable from one screen → best-effort, "unknown until seen," abstain-heavy.** |
| LyAi backend proxy for external stat bundles | must | All third-party feeds route here as periodic offline bundles — **subject to the licensing/ToS gate in §5.** |

### 2.7 Explicit non-goals & unsupportable-on-pixels (declared, not omitted)

These are Firestone/HDT features we will **not** promise, to avoid over-scoping. Declaring them is the honest-parity posture (confirm in §7).

| Item | Why | Posture |
|---|---|---|
| **Card provenance / created-by / buffed-by / stolen / returned / "held for N turns"** | Entity-level, invisible in pixels — a pure `Power.log` feature. | Non-goal; only generic class-generation hints. |
| **Collection / pack-opening / dust / set-rotation manager** | Screen-capture cannot read a collection database. | **Unsupportable — declared non-goal**, not a silent gap. |
| **Twitch / streaming overlay integration** | Both PC references ship it; on Android it's out of scope and architecturally different. | **Explicit non-goal.** |
| **Full per-turn match replay / board history review** | Firestone rebuilds this from the log; we have no log. | We can offer a **limited observed-state timeline** (turns/boards we actually saw, flagged "as observed"); a complete replay is a non-goal. |
| **Exact secrets elimination, exact fatigue/overdraw, optimal-lethal** | Hinge on hidden triggers / single missed events / every buffed stat. | Abstain/approximate only (see §2.1). |
| **All-8 BG opponents' full boards / triples / leveling times, shared minion pool** | Unobservable on screen capture. | Approximate "seen so far" or defer. |

## 3. Battlegrounds combat simulator (the win-% feature)

Module `dev.lyai.deckview.modes.bg.sim.*` — **pure Kotlin/JVM, no Android deps, JVM-unit-testable, off-thread only.** The engine and model never import Android or coroutines; only `api/CombatSimulator` touches `kotlinx.coroutines`. It communicates with the rest of the app solely via an immutable `CombatSnapshot` in and a `WinProbability` out.

**The one thing to internalize:** the Monte-Carlo core is the *easy* part — 1–2k allocation-free rollouts finish in well under 100 ms off-thread, and the caps guarantee it never janks. **Trustworthiness rests entirely on the board read and on refusing to show a confident-wrong number.**

### 3.1 Domain model (immutable in, pooled runtime, immutable out)

- **Inputs** built once per combat, shared read-only across all N rollouts: `MinionSpec` (dbfId, displayed atk/hp with gems/buffs already baked in, tavernTier, `TribeMask`, `KeywordMask`, golden, ordered `deathrattleIds`, `enchantIds`, **`provenance` ∈ {SELF_TRACKED, ENEMY_RECOGNIZED, MANUAL_EDIT}`**, and a per-minion **`confidence` 0..1**), `BoardSnapshot` (order preserved), `HeroPowerSpec`, and a top-level `CombatSnapshot` (self/enemy boards, both hero powers, `startEffects`, both life totals and tavern tiers, `mode ∈ {SOLO, DUOS}`, optional `duosContext`, and an aggregate `enemyConfidence`).
- **Runtime** is **struct-of-arrays** (`WorkBoard`: parallel `IntArray`s for dbfId/atk/hp/maxHp/live-keyword-bits/tribe/tier/flags + a deathrattle-id arena, `count`, `nextAttacker`), **one buffer reused across all N sims** — the hot loop allocates ~0 bytes. `MinionState` exists only as a thin `(board, slot)` cursor so card handlers read like game text without per-slot object allocation.
- **Output** `WinProbability`: winPct/tiePct/lossPct + 95% CI half-width, expected damage dealt/taken + histograms, **P(you die) / P(opponent dies)** given both life totals, a plain-language summary ("usually win by 4"), a **`confidence ∈ {OK, APPROXIMATE, ABSTAIN}`**, **`coverageFlags`** (e.g. "trinket effect not modeled," "unknown card modeled as vanilla"), iteration/capped counts, elapsedMs, and an optional `teamOutcome` for Duos.

### 3.2 Monte-Carlo approach

- **RNG:** `SplitMix64` seeded per rollout as `masterSeed xor mix(i)` — never `java.util.Random` (synchronized, allocates). Deterministic per-iteration seeding makes any single rollout replayable for debugging.
- **One rollout** (`CombatEngine.simulateOnce`): (1) **start-of-combat phase** — collect hero-power and minion SoC sources (Red Whelp / Deflect-o-Bot / Prized Promoter / Illidan, **plus trinket and tavern-spell start-of-combat effects, see §3.5**), order **ascending tavern tier with within-tier order sampled fresh by RNG each iteration** (this is the dominant pre-combat randomness node — reshuffle every iteration or win% is biased); (2) **pick first attacker** — more minions attacks first, tie = coin flip; (3) **attack loop** (L→R wrapping pointer, skip dead/0-atk; taunt-first uniform-random targeting, Zapp = lowest-atk; simultaneous strike; Divine Shield absorbs one instance; Poison/Venom mark on any damage; Cleave hits neighbors; Windfury/Mega-Windfury extra attacks; then the **DeathResolver as a fixpoint work-queue** — deathrattles in board order, Baron doubling, Reborn once, Avenge countdowns, Scallywag summon-and-immediate-attack, Monstrous Macaw re-trigger, Khadgar summon-doubling, adjacent SoA insert with pointer/Avenge-index fixup, cascading until stable), all guarded by **`ATTACK_CAP = 500`**; (4) **termination** — both empty = tie, one empty = other wins, cap hit = declared tie flagged `capped`; (5) **damage** = (Σ surviving minions' tavern tiers) + winner's hero tier. `Outcome` is a value class (result 2 bits + damage + flags) — zero allocation.
- **Aggregation:** `ResultAccumulator` tallies win/tie/loss/capped + damage histograms; 95% CI half-width = `1.96·√(p(1−p)/N)`. **N = 2000 → ±1.1 % @ p=0.5**, ample for a HUD number.

### 3.3 Off-thread performance (protects the zero-freeze mandate)

`CombatSimulator.run(snapshot, iterations=2000, budgetMs=250)` on `Dispatchers.Default` (never Main; the module has no Android imports, so it *cannot* touch the UI thread by construction):

1. **Determinism short-circuit** — a `DeterminismDetector` runs no-RNG combats once and returns a stable %, no jitter.
2. **Chunked Monte-Carlo** — reset the single reused `WorkState`, run in chunks of 128 with `ensureActive()` (prompt cooperative cancellation) + `yield()` (let the dispatcher breathe); a wall-clock **deadline returns a partial aggregate flagged APPROXIMATE** rather than overrunning. **The sim always returns.**
3. **One debounced in-flight job** — the overlay owns a `Job?`; each new recognition frame or manual edit **cancels** the previous run (structured concurrency), debounced ~120 ms so rapid enemy re-reads don't thrash.
4. **Thermal-aware N auto-tune** — budget is master, N advisory: raise N when there's headroom and the CI is wide; lower N under thermal throttling to hold the ceiling (ties into the §4 governor). Optional core fan-out is a later knob — single-thread already meets budget.

### 3.4 Recognition inputs + manual-correction fallback

```
GameStateStore  ──► self  BoardSnapshot   (HIGH-confidence, but pixel-derived — NOT exact)
Recognition     ──► enemy BoardSnapshot   (per-minion + aggregate confidence; CV, not OCR)
ManualEditOverride ─► overrides either side (treated as confidence = 1)
                     └► SnapshotBuilder ─► CombatSnapshot ─► CombatSimulator
```

- **Your board is the *better* read, not a perfect one.** It comes from `GameStateStore` (accumulated across turns, bigger render, you control timing), so per-minion confidence is high — but hidden self-enchants, exact live keyword state, golden-vs-normal, and deathrattle identity still ride on recognition. We carry a self-confidence too; we do not assert "self = exact."
- **The enemy board is the accuracy ceiling.** It's fully visible only in the ~1 s combat-preview window — exactly when the sim is wanted. Identity is **CV artwork-matching** (in-play minions have **no name banner** — OCR cannot read a name that isn't rendered), against hundreds of BG minions × golden variants at small render under buff/animation overlays. Stats and visible keyword glyphs (DS gold border, Taunt frame, Poison/Venom drip, Reborn, Windfury, Stealth) plus position are read per minion. **Gemini vision does not help here** — the network round-trip returns after the preview is gone; vision is reserved for static screens (hero pick, draft, shop). Enemy **deathrattle/keyword** reads compound *two* ceilings — art-only ID **and** invisible modifiers (magnetize-merged mechs, added deathrattles, hidden +X/+X) — so they force **abstain far more often** than a naive "Med" would suggest; enemy-board recognition is **High**.
- **Confidence → behavior:** `enemyConfidence ≥ 0.85` → `OK`, show the number; `0.6–0.85` → `APPROXIMATE` badge ("~62 % ±2 %"); `< 0.6` → **`ABSTAIN`** — "board unclear — tap to edit." A single misread keyword (DS/Poison/Taunt/Reborn) or wrong HP can swing win% by tens of points; abstention is the safety valve.
- **Manual board editor (mandatory, Firestone-style):** two 7-slot Compose rows (yours pre-filled, enemy from recognition), drag to reorder, tap to set atk/hp, keyword chips, tribe, golden, add a deathrattle/trinket from a searchable HearthstoneJSON picker (Spanish-first). Recognition **pre-highlights low-confidence minions** so the user fixes exactly the cells that matter. Every edit rebuilds the snapshot, cancels the in-flight job, and re-runs live (debounced). Correcting takes seconds; the % updates.
- **Self-capture exclusion (hard requirement):** the overlay HUD and this editor are `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY` windows that MediaProjection would otherwise capture — the recognizer must **exclude the overlay layer from capture** (or capture a display region that omits it) so it never CV-matches its own HUD as if it were the game board. Handled in §4; called out here because it corrupts the very read the sim depends on.

### 3.5 Honest accuracy ceiling — the disclosed biases

The Monte-Carlo core matches twanvl/Firestone/HDT to within a few %; that residual (simultaneous-death trigger ordering) is acceptable **only because we disclose it** via the `APPROXIMATE` badge. On top of that, screen-capture adds structured, **flagged** biases that PC log-readers don't have:

| Hidden-info source | Effect on the sim | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| **Trinkets (Lesser/Greater)** | Carry **start-of-combat and ongoing combat effects invisible on the combat board** — a *larger* hidden-info source than hero powers. Omitting them **systematically biases** win%. | **Modeled in the EffectRegistry** when the trinket is recognized (from its own screen/HUD) or manually entered; when unknown/unseen → **`coverageFlags` entry + widened CI + lowered confidence**, never silently ignored. |
| **Tavern-spell combat buffs** | Several 2024→2026 tavern spells apply combat-relevant buffs not obvious on the board. | Registry coverage as data; unknown → flagged vanilla. |
| **Enemy hero power / enemy start-of-combat** | Usually invisible pre-combat. | Modeled only if recognized; otherwise flagged. |
| **Hidden enchantments (secret +X/+X)** | Invisible in tooltips-only. | Recognition ceiling — manual-edit only, flagged. |
| **Unknown/exotic cards** | New-set minions not yet in the registry. | **Vanilla stats+keywords + `coverageFlags`**, never a silent divergence; the `EffectRegistry` is a **patch-updatable data table**, so new cards degrade to flagged-approximate rather than an engine edit. |

**Duos** is modeled as its own combat variant (shared HP, teammate-support minions, cross-board pass/portal) — **not a Solo bolt-on** — and lands in E2c so the "BG parity" claim is truthful (§6).

The module ships with three things that are the *actual* deliverable, more than the Monte-Carlo core: (1) per-minion **confidence + abstain**, (2) the **manual editor** that re-runs live, (3) the **data-driven patch-updatable registry** with a **replay regression harness** (fixtures of known real combats → known outcome distributions, asserted within CI at a fixed seed, gated on each card-data bump).
