## 4. Mode-integration architecture — plugin per mode, crash-isolated, off-thread

The backbone is the **platform**; each mode is a **plugin**. Plugins never own the capture thread, the render thread, or global state — they subscribe to immutable snapshots and publish results. This is what makes zero-crash/zero-freeze achievable with N modes, and it directly answers the mobile-specific stability risks below.

### 4.1 The plugin contract

```kotlin
interface ModePlugin {
    val mode: HsMode
    // Called only when the classifier says THIS mode is active. Pure, off-thread,
    // receives immutable snapshots — never a live bitmap it can retain, never Main.
    suspend fun onFrame(frame: FrameSnapshot, state: GameState): PluginOutput
    fun overlays(): List<OverlayComponent>   // render StateFlow only; zero compute on the render path
    fun onModeExit()                          // release everything; must not throw
}
```

- **Shared services** (capture, phase/mode classifier, anchor-ROI, `GameStateStore`, HearthstoneJSON, overlay host, AI chat, Room stats DB, backend proxy) are injected singletons. Plugins depend on interfaces, not each other — **no plugin can reach into another's state**, so a bug in one mode cannot corrupt another.
- **The BG sim module (§3) is a library a plugin calls**, not a plugin itself — pure Kotlin/JVM, reused by both the Solo and Duos plugins.

### 4.2 Crash isolation (a bad recognizer must never take down the app or the game)

- **Supervisor per plugin.** Each plugin runs under its own `SupervisorJob` child scope of the capture spine. A plugin failure cancels *only that plugin's* work, never siblings or the capture/render pipeline.
- **Catch-and-abstain boundary.** Every `onFrame` is wrapped: any exception → log telemetry, **disable that plugin for the session with backoff**, and show the abstain state in its overlay. Exceptions never propagate to the capture `HandlerThread` or Main. (This is abstain-on-low-confidence generalized to "abstain-on-fault.")
- **Per-plugin frame-budget watchdog.** If a plugin's `onFrame` exceeds its budget, it is throttled or suspended — protecting the game's frame rate first, the feature second.
- **Single hot plugin.** The classifier gates exactly **one** mode plugin as active at a time (plus shared services). This is both correctness (no constructed tracker leaking onto a BG board) **and** the primary defense against CPU/GPU/thermal contention — we never run every mode's recognizer at once.

### 4.3 Off-thread by construction

- Plugins run on `Dispatchers.Default`; the capture pipeline runs on its dedicated `HandlerThread`; **overlays render only from `StateFlow`** — no computation on the render path.
- The BG sim module has **no Android imports**, so it *cannot* touch Main. Recognition/CV likewise runs off the render thread. The render thread's only job is to draw the latest published result.

### 4.4 Thermal & contention governor (mobile-only; PC trackers never face this)

Sustained MediaProjection capture + on-device CV art-matching + periodic Gemini vision + Monte-Carlo, running **concurrently with a GPU-heavy game on one phone**, competes for CPU/GPU and generates heat — which can jank *the game itself* and throttle the device, degrading recognition in a feedback loop. A **global ResourceGovernor** closes this:

- Subscribes to `PowerManager` thermal status, a rolling frame-time/CPU budget, and battery state.
- Under pressure it dials back, in order: capture cadence (lean harder on the adaptive-idle + motion-burst logic), CV frequency, **sim N** (ties into §3.3 auto-tune), and vision-call rate — degrading gracefully to on-device-only, never dropping to zero mid-match.
- Single-hot-plugin (§4.2) plus adaptive cadence plus the governor is the whole answer: we spend the phone's thermal budget on the one mode the user is in.

### 4.5 GC / memory at real device resolution

Production runs at **1080p+**, not the 800×360 spike harness. Bitmap churn through ImageReader/bitmap-pool at that resolution is a **new freeze vector (GC pauses)** distinct from the fixed Markdown one:

- **Downscale-on-capture** to the recognizer's ROI-normalized working resolution before any per-frame work; bounded ImageReader buffers; strict bitmap-pool reuse (backbone) with **no per-frame allocation**.
- **The spike harness is extended to production resolution** and made a gating stability test: frame-time regression **and** an allocation assertion at 1080p+, not just 800×360.

### 4.6 MediaProjection lifecycle & self-capture (Android 14/15 realities)

- **Foreground-service-type** `mediaProjection` (Android 14 requirement); handle **Android 15 re-consent** and stricter start rules.
- **Capture-loss recovery state machine.** Projection dies on app-switch, incoming call, or backgrounding — i.e. mid-match capture loss. On the stop callback we surface "capture paused" in the overlay, **auto-request re-consent on return, and resume without crashing.** Graceful degrade, never a crash and never a confidently-stale overlay.
- **Self-capture exclusion + non-interactive overlay (hard requirements).** The overlay must be **excluded from the projected surface** (exclude the overlay layer / capture a region that omits it) so the recognizer never CV-matches its own HUD; and the overlay window is **strictly non-interactive** (`FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE | FLAG_NOT_TOUCHABLE`) so it can **never steal a touch from Hearthstone.** Both are ship-blockers — the first corrupts recognition, the second corrupts gameplay.

### 4.7 Streaming AI-chat re-render (beyond the original Markdown fix)

The backbone's off-thread parse + virtualized `LazyColumn` + `PrecomputedText` fixed the *static* long-Markdown freeze, but **streaming** re-parse can still thrash and `PrecomputedText` application still lands on Main. We add: **token coalescing** (buffer and render every N ms, not per-token), off-thread parse into `PrecomputedText`, batched application on Main, and a **streaming-render stress test** in the stability gate — the streaming path is validated, not assumed.

---

## 5. External data, cost & licensing (LyAi ≥ $0.10 flags)

**This section is a gate, not a footnote.** Several headline features are **Stats-DB** — they cannot be computed on-device and depend on external corpora. The v1 draft treated these as "free-tier, no authorization needed." That is **wrong on three counts** (licensing, cost-at-scale, and product-level ToS) and each must clear before the dependent epic ships.

### 5.1 Dependency register

| Dependency | Used by | Cost | Licensing / ToS reality | LyAi flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **HearthstoneJSON** (dbfId-keyed card DB, locale packs) | Everything — decode, secret pools, candidate sets, sim card names | Free | **Genuinely open/redistributable.** The only external data we can safely bundle. **No Mercs data** — Mercenaries needs a separate community DB. | **None.** |
| **HSReplay-style meta corpus** (archetype/MetaDetector, mulligan %, deck win-rate/matchup, discover stats) — **E1** | Constructed advisors | Potentially paid | **HSReplay has no open data API.** "Mirror server-side and ship as offline bundles" **is scraping a proprietary corpus** with Blizzard/HSReplay ToS exposure. **"Free to view" ≠ "free to scrape and rebundle in a competing app."** And **DeckView gives nothing back** — with no `Power.log` it cannot upload replays, so there is **no fallback if the source blocks us.** This is an **existential dependency for E1 (archetype/mulligan).** | **LEGAL GATE — must clear before E1.** Possible cost if licensed. |
| **HearthArena Arena scores** — **E3** | Live draft pick helper | **Likely paid** | HearthArena is a **freemium/proprietary** service; **Arena draft scores are its core product.** Mirroring and redistributing them inside DeckView is a **licensing violation and potentially a paid dependency — not free.** Scores must also **refresh, not bundle statically**, so it's an ongoing feed, not a one-time copy. | **LEGAL + COST GATE — must clear before E3.** |
| **Firestone / HSReplay / wiki** BG hero-trinket-tavern-spell-minion tier data, comp lists; anomaly/odds/brawl catalogs — **E2/E4** | BG & brawl advisors | Potentially paid | Aggregated Firestone/HSReplay stats are **not automatically free to redistribute** in a competing app — same "free to view ≠ free to rebundle" problem. Wiki content has its own attribution/license terms. | **LEGAL GATE per source before E2/E4.** |
| **Gemini 2.5-flash** (AI chat + static-screen vision fallback) | Chat, non-time-critical vision | Free tier **that does not survive scale** | Per-screen/per-combat vision + chat **across a real user base blows free-tier RPM/RPD quotas.** At that point it is a **paid dependency that trips LyAi's ≥ $0.10 rule** and needs your authorization **before launch, not after.** | **COST GATE — projected paid; authorization required pre-launch.** |
| **Community Mercs DB** — E5 | Mercenaries (deferred) | Free | Not in HearthstoneJSON; separate bundled DB, community-sourced, check attribution. | Low (mode deferred). |

### 5.2 Structural sustainability risk (this outlasts any one license)

**DeckView has no data-contribution pipeline.** Without `Power.log` it can **never upload games**, so — unlike Firestone, which grows its own corpus from its users' logs — DeckView can **never build its own meta-stats corpus.** It is **permanently dependent on scraping third parties.** This **caps the entire Stats-DB feature class** (archetype, mulligan, matchup, tier scores, Arena scores) and is a strategic/sustainability risk, not merely a per-source licensing one. Options for §7: license properly (cost), build a weak opt-in pixel-derived corpus, drop Stats-DB features to a manual/community tier, or partner with a data provider.

### 5.3 Product-level Blizzard ToS (the whole app's standing)

PC HDT/Firestone enjoy a **tolerated "read-only overlay" status.** A **mobile app that screen-captures a live match and renders real-time win-% advice over the game is a grayer case** and could be actioned (user account risk, app takedown). Points in our favor to document: we are **read-only** (no input automation, no memory reading — pixels only), the overlay is **strictly non-interactive** (§4.6), and we perform **no ToS-violating log upload** (we can't). Points against: real-time in-match advisory on mobile is closer to the line than a passive PC overlay. **This risk was absent from the v1 plan; it belongs on the decision table (§7) and likely warrants a legal read before public launch.**

### 5.4 Posture

- **Bundle only HearthstoneJSON** with confidence.
- **Every meta-stats feed is gated** on a written per-source redistribution/ToS check (legal gate) plus any cost. None ship on "assumed free."
- **Gemini stays free-tier by design** — on-device CV is primary, vision is event-gated to static-screen transitions only, results cached, per-user vision calls capped, with a hard budget that degrades to on-device-only. But the **projected paid ceiling at scale needs authorization now** (≥ $0.10 rule).

---

## 6. Master roadmap

**Build order:** **E0 → E1 → E2a → E2b → E2c → E3 → E4 → (E5 deferred) → E6.**

### Stability re-certification checklist (every epic clears this *before* ship — not after)

- **Zero-freeze proof:** no new work on UI/render thread; all parse/sim/OCR/CV off-thread (`Dispatchers.Default`); overlays render `StateFlow` only. **Frame-time + allocation regression run against the spike harness at production resolution (1080p+, §4.5)** — no `inter_ms` freeze regression vs. baseline.
- **Thermal/contention:** ResourceGovernor (§4.4) verified to protect the *game's* frame rate under sustained load; single-hot-plugin confirmed.
- **Lifecycle:** MediaProjection capture-loss/recovery (§4.6) survives app-switch/call/background mid-match without crash; Android 14/15 FGS + re-consent handled.
- **Self-capture exclusion + non-interactive overlay** verified (§4.6).
- **Streaming-chat re-render** stress test green (§4.7).
- **Abstain-on-low-confidence wired:** the mode shows "unclear — tap to edit," never a confident-wrong overlay.
- **Mode-gate correct:** this mode's overlays fire *only* in this mode.
- **Practice-mode regression harness (E1)** green for any recognizer the epic touches.
- **Cost/licensing sign-off** for any external data added (§5).

### E0 — Shared platform hardening (prerequisite)

Extend the phase/mode classifier to the full 2026 enum (Constructed/BG-Solo/BG-Duos/Arena/Underground/Brawl/Practice/Friendly/Mercs + menu/mulligan/in-game/combat/draft/end). Ship the **End-of-game result reader** and **Room stats DB** as shared services; formalize the **generic observed-card overlay**. **Land the mobile stability spine: ResourceGovernor, projection-lifecycle recovery, self-capture exclusion, production-resolution GC validation, streaming-chat throttling.**
**Acceptance:** classifier ≥ target accuracy on a labeled mode-transition set with abstain fallback; result reader + stats DB feed a live counter across ≥ 2 modes; **stability spine demonstrably holds the game's frame rate under sustained capture at 1080p+ with an induced thermal load**; checklist green.

### E1 — Constructed parity completion + Practice QA harness (highest value, lowest recognition risk)

Close the gap to HDT-class constructed: opponent played-card log + hand/deck counts; turn/mana; own cards-left + next-draw math (labeled **inferred**, not exact); **archetype/MetaDetector**; **mulligan advisor**; deck win-rate/matchup + local history; deck import/export. **New:** **persistent counters** (Corpse/Rune/Invoke/C'Thun/Spell-damage/Excavate/Elemental — flagged by which degrade) and **questline progress.** Ship the **Practice-vs-AI full build as the zero-risk regression harness** for every recognizer. Deferred to abstaining "could": secrets, fatigue, lethal, created-by oracle.
**Gate:** archetype/mulligan/win-rate are **blocked on the §5.1 HSReplay licensing decision.**
**Acceptance:** on the Practice harness, the tracker reconstructs a known decklist's draw sequence within tolerance (and **flags desync** when a draw is missed rather than silently drifting); archetype/mulligan read fixed layouts or abstain; counters degrade-and-flag correctly; checklist green.

### E2a — Static / high-reliability Battlegrounds (ship BG value early)

Hero Pick Advisor (highest-reliability BG feature), Trinket advisor, **Tavern-Spell advisor**, **Anomaly context panel**, tavern odds by tier, tier-list/minion-pool browser, your-own triple tracking, MMR/placement. **Buddies panel is not built (removed from the game); BG Quests not built (removed).**
**Gate:** tier/hero/trinket stats subject to the §5.1 Firestone/HSReplay licensing check.
**Acceptance:** static advisors read their fixed screens or abstain; no dead Buddies/Quests content; checklist green.

### E2b — Battlegrounds combat simulator (crown jewel, gated behind the enemy read)

Ship `modes/bg/sim` (§3): SoA allocation-free Monte-Carlo, N ≈ 2000 < 100 ms off-thread, ATTACK_CAP=500, budget ≈ 250 ms, determinism short-circuit, single debounced job. **Three ship-blockers:** (1) per-minion confidence + abstain (≥ 0.85 OK / 0.6–0.85 approximate / < 0.6 abstain), (2) the manual board editor that re-runs live, (3) the patch-updatable EffectRegistry + replay regression harness. **Registry must cover trinket and tavern-spell combat effects**, with unrecognized/invisible ones producing `coverageFlags` + widened CI, not silent bias. **Framing corrected:** both boards are pixel estimates (self higher-confidence, not exact); enemy identity is CV art-matching (no OCR on the board); vision is not used in the combat window.
**Acceptance:** JVM unit tests pass for DS/Poison/Windfury/Reborn/Cleave/Baron/Macaw-Scallywag-Khadgar chains; replay fixtures land within CI at a fixed seed; N=2000 < 100 ms with ~0-byte allocation; determinism detector short-circuits; **low-confidence enemy read shows abstain + editor, never a confident-wrong %**; trinket/tavern-spell absence is flagged; the sim **always returns** (cap/budget → APPROXIMATE); checklist green.

### E2c — Battlegrounds **Duos** (required for a truthful "BG parity" claim)

Model Duos as a **first-class combat variant** (shared HP, teammate-support minions, cross-board pass/portal) in the sim and the state model. Duos is a co-equal permanent mode; **we do not advertise "BG parity" until this ships.**
**Acceptance:** Duos combat variant passes its own replay fixtures; teammate-board read (which *is* visible, unlike Solo opponents) wired with confidence/abstain; checklist green. **Sequencing decision for §7:** hold the "BG parity" claim until E2c, or ship BG labeled "Solo only — Duos in progress."

### E3 — Arena + The Underground (high value, recognition-fragile draft)

Live draft pick helper (read 3 / 4-in-Legendary-Group, Dual-Class banners, Legendary Groups; on-device ranking over **refreshed** tier scores; gated strictly to the draft screen, robust to seasonal reskins, abstain when unsure) → in-run tracker assembled from 30 captured picks (reuses E1's constructed pipeline, inherits its caveats) → synergy/curve hints, hero/class pick helper, run record + Arena-vs-Underground context, tier-list freshness. Underground Re-Draft-on-Loss is a "could."
**Gate:** the pick helper's tier scores are **blocked on the §5.1 HearthArena/Firestone licensing-and-cost decision** — no fallback if refused.
**Acceptance:** pick helper reads the offer set or abstains; captured 30-pick decklist drives the in-run tracker; reward-contents OCR flagged best-effort; checklist green.

### E4 — Tavern Brawl / Friendly (mostly reuse — NOT Twist)

The **mode gate** (a *stability* feature — stops the constructed tracker firing on unknowable/prebuilt decks); brawl-type auto-classification (abstain + show nothing rather than garbage); **Brawliseum/Heroic run tracking** (highest-value brawl feature — real constructed deck → full tracker + W/L scoreboard); Friendly Challenge; weekly-brawl info card. **No per-brawl decklist DB** (not a real parity gap). **Twist's role folded here** if ever revived — no separate epic.
**Acceptance:** prebuilt/PvE brawls produce **no** confident overlay; Brawliseum reuses the constructed tracker end-to-end; checklist green.

### E5 — Mercenaries (defer unless you ask)

Frozen mode, shrinking audience, icon-dense bespoke UI, needs a separate community DB. All "could," abstain-heavy (speed ties + hidden abilities are irreducibly probabilistic). **Recommendation: defer past E4.**

### E6 — v2 depth (post-parity)

BG shared-pool "seen so far" depletion; secrets/fatigue/lethal graduating from abstain to approximate where a better read is proven; Underground re-draft; richer provenance hints; a limited observed-state match timeline. Not parity-blocking.

---

## 7. Open decisions for Ignacio (modes/features-specific)

1. **Blizzard product-level ToS posture (existential).** A mobile screen-capture app rendering real-time in-match win-% advice is grayer than a PC read-only overlay and could be actioned. **Accept the risk with our read-only/non-interactive/no-upload mitigations, or commission a legal read before public launch?** This gates the whole product. *(§5.3)*

2. **Meta-stats sourcing & licensing (gates E1 archetype/mulligan and E3 Arena scores — no fallback if blocked).** HSReplay has no open API and HearthArena's Arena scores are its paid core product; "free to view" is not "free to rebundle." **Which path:** (a) license properly (possible cost + your ≥ $0.10 authorization), (b) build a weak opt-in pixel-derived corpus (slow, no `Power.log`), (c) drop these to a manual/community tier, or (d) partner with a data provider? *(§5.1–5.2)*

3. **Gemini cost at scale (authorization needed pre-launch, not after).** Free-tier RPM/RPD does not survive a real user base. **Authorize the projected paid tier for vision/chat, or hard-cap to on-device-CV + free-tier ceiling with graceful degrade** (accepting reduced static-screen vision assistance)? *(§5.1, §5.4)*

4. **Duos timing & the "BG parity" claim.** Duos is co-equal and permanent; claiming BG parity without it is inaccurate. **Hold the "BG parity" claim until E2c ships, or launch BG labeled "Solo only — Duos in progress"?** *(§1, §2.2, E2c)*

5. **Honest-parity posture (public messaging).** Some Firestone/HDT marquee features are unsupportable on pixels — created-by oracle, collection/dust/pack manager, full match replay, exact secrets/fatigue/lethal, all-8 BG boards, shared-pool counts, Twitch overlay. **Confirm we ship these as abstain/flag/declared-non-goal and message "parity on everything a read-only pixel observer can deliver"** rather than implying total parity. *(§2.7)*

6. **Structural sustainability.** DeckView can never contribute data back (no `Power.log`), so it is permanently dependent on third-party stats. **Accept permanent dependence, or fund an opt-in pixel-derived corpus / data partnership as a longer-term hedge?** *(§5.2)*

7. **Mercenaries.** **Defer (recommended) or build?** Building requires a separate bundled community Mercs DB and is abstain-heavy on a frozen, shrinking mode. *(§2.5, E5)*

8. **Locale scope.** Spanish-first is set. **Any additional HearthstoneJSON locale packs to prioritize** for OCR/CV name matching and the card pickers? *(shared services)*

---

*Every epic clears the stability re-certification gate before it ships; every Stats-DB feature clears a written per-source licensing/ToS check before it ships; and no external dependency is treated as "free" without that check. The compute is the easy part — the deliverable is the honesty: abstain over confident-wrong, manual correction where the pixels run out, and a phone that never janks the game it's watching.*

### **Claude** `05:59`

Basado en la documentación oficial de Claude Code, aquí va la respuesta técnica a tus 4 puntos:

---

## 1. **Slash commands de la TUI en modo `-p` (headless)**

**SÍ funcionan** la mayoría, pero con matices:

- ✅ **Funciones OK en `-p`** (v2.1.205+):
  - `/model sonnet` — cambiar modelo (incluyes en el prompt: `"Tu prompt aquí /model opus"`)
  - `/effort high` — nivel de effort
  - `/fast`, `/color`, `/rename` — flags de sesión
  - `/config thinking=false` — cambiar settings por sesión
  - `/mcp` — status de MCP servers (sin args, imprime texto)
  - **Skills custom** (`/nombre-skill args`) — se expanden igual que en TUI

- ❌ **NO funcionan en `-p`**:
  - `/login` — puramente de TUI interactivo
  - Otros comandos UI-only no están documentados, pero `/login` es el caso claro

**Fuente**: [Headless.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md) — *"User-invoked skills and custom commands work in `-p` mode... Built-in commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as `/login`, aren't available in `-p` mode."*

---

## 2. **Flags de línea de comandos equivalentes para `-p`**

Sí existen y son la forma **recomendada** para headless (más portable):

```bash
# Modelo
--model claude-sonnet-5         # opus, sonnet, haiku, fable

# Effort
--effort high                   # low, medium, high, xhigh, max

# Permisos
--permission-mode bypassPermissions  # plan, default, auto, bypassPermissions
--allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit"

# System prompt
--append-system-prompt "Instrucciones..."
--system-prompt "Reemplazar por completo"

# Output estructurado
--output-format json
--json-schema '{"type":"object"...}'

# Contexto/velocidad
--bare                          # Omite hooks, skills, MCP, memory
```

**NO hay flags directos** para `/fast`, `/color`, `/rename` vía CLI — esos sólo van como slash commands en el prompt.

**Fuente**: [CLI Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference.md)

---

## 3. **Skills custom en modo `-p`**

✅ **SÍ funcionan igual**. Incluye `/nombre-skill args` en el prompt:

```bash
claude -p "Mi prompt. /code-review --high" --permission-mode bypassPermissions
```

Claude expande `/code-review` antes de ejecutar, igual que en TUI interactivo. No hay diferencia siempre que el skill esté en `.claude/skills/` o cargado vía plugin.

**Fuente**: Mismo párrafo headless.md citado arriba.

---

## 4. **Listar programáticamente comandos disponibles**

⚠️ **No existe un CLI nativo para esto.** La documentación no menciona:
- No hay `claude --list-commands`
- No hay `claude --list-skills`
- No hay flag JSON que dumpee comandos disponibles

**Workarounds actuales:**

1. **En TUI**: `/help` muestra lista interactiva (pero no programable).
2. **Grep manual**: Inspeccionar `.claude/skills/` en disco:
   ```bash
   ls -1 ~/.claude/skills/ | grep -E '\.md$|\.txt$'
   # o en proyecto
   ls -1 .claude/skills/ 2>/dev/null
   ```
3. **Parsear CLAUDE.md**: Si documenta skills disponibles (como hace tu `CLAUDE.md` de lyai-ski).

**Para tu bot TG**: Lo más robusto es **mantener un catálogo hardcodeado** en el bridge que refleje los skills del proyecto (`.claude/skills/` + skills de plugins en `settings.json`), y ofrecerlo como menú. No hay reflexión automática.

---

**Resumen para el bridge**: Usa `claude -p --resume <sid> --permission-mode bypassPermissions "texto /skill args"` — funciona igual que TUI, pero los slash commands van **en el prompt de texto**, no como flags. Los flags (`--model`, `--effort`, `--allowedTools`) son para config de sesión, no para comandos interactivos.

## Backbone DeckView — resumen ejecutivo

**La apuesta central (versión honesta que el crítico forzó):**
- El **deckstring** te da la **lista autoritativa de 30 cartas, 100% offline** — lo único garantizable sin visión.
- Los **contadores en vivo (cartas restantes) NO son autoritativos**: dependen de reconocer cada robo/juego, es best-effort, y cuando la visión duda **abstiene** (no inventa) → se marca "incierto" en pantalla. Nunca se afirma precisión que no tenemos.

**Decisiones de arquitectura clave:**
- **Overlay HUD sobre el juego** (`TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY`) — el crítico detectó que sin esto la app es inservible mientras juegas (Hearthstone está en primer plano). Promovido a **core de v1**.
- **Captura off-thread** (HandlerThread + ImageReader + bitmap pool + `close()` en `finally`) con ritmo **adaptativo** (1-2 fps en reposo, ráfaga al detectar movimiento para no perder animaciones <1s).
- **Reconocimiento**: ML Kit OCR (offline) + Gemini 2.5-flash visión (gratis, vía **proxy LyAi** que oculta la key), **restringido a las cartas del mazo**, con normalización de ROIs por *anchors* (funciona en cualquier resolución, no un dispositivo fijo).
- **Chat anti-freeze**: las 5 reglas que matan el jank diagnosticado (parse markdown off-thread, lista virtualizada, streaming ≤1 update/frame, `PrecomputedText`, imágenes async).

**Hitos** (M-neg1 → M6): arranca validando **legibilidad real sobre los JPGs del spike que ya tienes** (¿se lee una carta a 800×360? se decide la resolución mínima con datos, no suponiendo), reutiliza tu harness `spike` como base de captura, y cierra con certificación de estabilidad (soak 1h, cero crashes/ANR, telemetría de campo).

**Las decisiones que te tocan a ti (Ignacio)** — las 4 que bloquean:

2. **Proxy LyAi para las API keys** (recomendado) — confirma que montamos ese backend fino.
3. **Postura de contadores en vivo**: ¿aceptas "lista autoritativa + contadores best-effort con confianza", o exiges contadores fiables (mueve el reconocimiento a la ruta crítica → mucho más grande y arriesgado)?
4. **El repo Android**: no existe → confirmar dónde se crea para arrancar M-neg1/M0 adaptando el `spike`.

# Sí, ahora lo tengo claro — y la tesis honesta es esta

**DeckView lee píxeles, no el `Power.log`.** Firestone/HDT (en PC) leen el log del juego → verdad perfecta. Nosotros solo vemos la pantalla renderizada. Por eso el plan alcanza **paridad en todo lo que un observador de píxeles puede entregar**, y declara como **no-goal** lo que es físicamente imposible desde píxeles — sin huecos silenciosos ni promesas falsas.

## Modos (censo 2026, fact-checked)
- **Sí:** Standard, Wild, **Battlegrounds Solo + Duos** (Duos es co-igual y permanente → obligatorio para poder decir "paridad BG"), Arena + **The Underground**, Tavern Brawl/Brawliseum, Practice/Friendly.
- **Retirados (NO se especan):** Duels (2024), Classic (2023), **Twist (may-2026)**. Dentro de BG: **Buddies y Quests eliminados** (no se construyen); Anomalies, Tavern Spells y Trinkets vivos.
- **Mercenaries:** congelado desde 2023 → **se pospone** (E5).

## El simulador de Battlegrounds (el % de victoria)
Módulo Kotlin puro, off-thread. **El cómputo es lo fácil:** Monte-Carlo, ~2000 rollouts sin asignaciones **< 100 ms**, siempre devuelve (con presupuesto de 250 ms). **El techo es leer el tablero enemigo** (visible solo ~1 s, sin banner de nombre → CV de arte, no OCR; y trinkets/hechizos de taberna con efectos invisibles). Por eso son **ship-blockers**: confianza por esbirro + **abstención** (si duda: "tablero poco claro — toca para editar") + **editor manual** estilo Firestone que re-simula en vivo. El entregable real no es el motor, es la **honestidad**: abstenerse antes que dar un % confiadamente-equivocado.

## Arquitectura y roadmap
Cada modo = **plugin aislado** (un supervisor propio; un modo roto no tumba a los demás ni al juego), un solo plugin activo a la vez (defensa térmica), todo off-thread, overlay no-interactivo que **no roba toques** al juego. Roadmap **E0→E6**: E0 spine de estabilidad móvil → E1 Constructed completo (+ arnés QA en modo Práctica) → E2a BG estático → **E2b simulador** → E2c Duos → E3 Arena → E4 Brawl → E5 Mercs (pospuesto) → E6 profundidad. Cada epic re-certifica estabilidad **antes** de shipear.

## ⚠️ Lo que te bloquea a ti (Ignacio) — decisiones nuevas y serias

El análisis de modos destapó tres bloqueadores que no estaban en el radar:

1. **ToS de Blizzard (existencial).** Un overlay móvil que captura la partida y da consejo de win% **en vivo** es más gris que un overlay de PC read-only — riesgo de baneo de cuenta / retirada de la app. ¿Asumimos el riesgo con nuestras mitigaciones (solo lectura, sin automatización, sin subir logs) o lectura legal antes de lanzar?
2. **Datos de meta-stats (licencia + coste).** Archetype/mulligan (E1) y scores de Arena (E3) dependen de HSReplay/HearthArena, que **no son libres de re-empaquetar**. Y como no hay `Power.log`, **DeckView nunca puede aportar datos de vuelta** → dependencia permanente de terceros. ¿Licenciar / corpus propio débil / bajar esas features a manual / partner?
3. **Coste de Gemini a escala (regla ≥$0.10).** La capa gratis no sobrevive a una base de usuarios. ¿Autorizas capa de pago para visión/chat, o tope duro a solo-on-device?

**B) Captura `spike` a 800×360** con **DATASET (VOLCADO 2 FPS) ON** de una partida — para ver qué ve *realmente* el pipeline actual. Es la comparación clave: full-res vs los 800×360 de ahora.

## Cómo hacer la captura

### Track A — Screenshots a resolución nativa (lo más valioso, sin el spike)
Con Hearthstone abierto, haz una **captura de pantalla normal del móvil** (Power + Volumen-abajo, o el gesto de tu móvil) en cada pantalla de la tabla de prioridad. Se guardan en Galería/DCIM/Screenshots. Esto es el *límite superior* de legibilidad — si a plena resolución no se lee, no se lee nunca.

### Track B — Captura spike a 800×360 (lo que ve el pipeline real)
1. Abre la app **DeckView Spike**.
2. Pulsa **DATASET ON/OFF (VOLCADO 2 FPS)** hasta que el panel diga **`dump: true`** (así vuelca jpgs a 2 fps).
3. Pulsa **INICIAR CAPTURA** → Android pedirá permiso de *grabar/proyectar pantalla* → **acepta**.
4. **CLAVE:** sal de la app (home) y **abre Hearthstone**. Sigue grabando de fondo.
5. Juega ~2-4 min pasando por: **mulligan → jugar un par de cartas → un combate de Battlegrounds con ambos tableros** (lo más importante) → tienda/héroe de BG si puedes.
6. Vuelve a la app spike y pulsa **PARAR CAPTURA**.

**Verifica mientras graba** (panel del spike): `running: true`, `dump: true`, `captura: 800x360`, `volcados:` subiendo, y una **`sesion:` con id nuevo**.

### Entregarme el resultado
- Los frames quedan en `.../Android/data/dev.lyai.deckview.spike/files/spike-logs/session_<id_nuevo>/` — **igual que sacaste `spike-logs.zip`**.
- Mete esa carpeta de sesión **+ tus screenshots nativos** en un zip → súbelo a `/opt/lyai/deckview/inbox/` (p.ej. `hs-capture.zip`) → dime **"subido"** y corro el test de legibilidad M-neg1.

Buenas noticias: **la premisa de captura+visión queda validada para lo crítico**, y confirma el plan en vez de romperlo. Probé sobre Battlegrounds real (lo que grabaste, ~13 min). Resumen por superficie:

## Cómo funcionaría el overlay de win% en tiempo real

El overlay en sí (la barra V2 encima del juego) es lo **fácil**: una ventana `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY` (permiso `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`) dibujada sobre Hearthstone. Lo difícil es **de dónde sacamos el número**. La cadena real es:

```
MediaProjection (captura continua de pantalla)
      │
      ▼
Detector de FASE  ──►  "¿estamos en el preview de combate de BG?"
      │  (sí)
      ▼
Leer los DOS tableros del frame  ← ⚠️ EL CUELLO DE BOTELLA
   · 7 esbirros tuyos + 7 del rival
   · por cada uno: ataque/vida (OCR) · tribu/keywords (iconos/bordes) · identidad de carta (arte)
      │
      ▼
Simulador Monte-Carlo de combate  → juega el combate miles de veces (el combate tiene azar:
      │                              a quién ataca cada esbirro es aleatorio)
      ▼
% victoria / empate / derrota  →  pinta la barra V2 ANTES de que el combate se anime
```

## Lo honesto: qué es fácil y qué es el techo

- **El simulador es lo FÁCIL.** Miles de iteraciones corren en **<100 ms fuera del main thread**. Es un problema resuelto (existe simulador open-source de combate BG). El cómputo **no** es el problema.
- **Leer el tablero enemigo por píxeles ES el problema.** En PC los trackers leen `Power.log`; en Android **no hay acceso** (sandbox) → todo sale de **visión sobre la captura**:
  - **stats (atk/vida)** → OCR, fiable (validé que a 800×360 los números se leen).
  - **tribu/keywords** (divine shield, taunt, veneno, reborn…) → clasificar iconos/bordes, más duro pero viable.
  - **identidad de la carta** (para deathrattles/efectos) → **matching de arte = ESTE es el techo** (ya lo marqué en M-neg1). Si la visión confunde un esbirro, el % sale mal.
- **La ventana de tiempo:** BG te da unos **~5 s de "preview"** con los dos tableros visibles antes de animar el combate. Ahí hay que: coger frame → leer ambos tableros → simular → pintar, en **~1–2 s**. Ajustado pero factible.

Por eso el plan tiene como **bloqueadores de release**: *confianza + corrección manual + abstención*. Si la visión no está segura, la barra muestra "?" o te deja **tocar para corregir**, en vez de enseñarte un número seguro-pero-falso. Y ojo: overlay en vivo sobre un juego móvil es **zona gris de la ToS de Blizzard** (bloqueador que dejé para ti).

**Resumen en una frase:** el overlay y el simulador son sencillos; **el trabajo real es la visión que lee el tablero rival rápido y bien** — y ese es exactamente el riesgo que M-neg1/M0 van a de-riesgar antes de gastar en nada.

## Tu pregunta: "¿como la app deck tracker para Windows?"

Te refieres a **HDT (Hearthstone Deck Tracker)**, el de PC. **El objetivo es el mismo; el mecanismo NO puede serlo** — y esa es la diferencia clave de todo el proyecto:

| | **HDT (Windows)** | **DeckView (Android)** |
|---|---|---|
| De dónde saca los datos | Lee el **`Power.log`** que HS escribe en el PC | **No puede** (sandbox de Android) → **captura de pantalla + visión** |
| Precisión del dato | **Perfecta** (sabe la carta exacta) | Depende de OCR + reconocer el arte |
| Win% de Battlegrounds | Sim con tablero **exacto** del log | Sim con tablero **leído de píxeles** |
| Overlay sobre el juego | Trivial y estable (escritorio) | Ventana de sistema + **zona gris ToS** |

En una frase: **HDT tiene un "superpoder" que en Android no existe** — leer el fichero de log del juego. Nosotros perseguimos **el mismo resultado** (tracker + overlay + win% de BG), pero reconstruyendo esa info **desde la pantalla**. El cálculo (el simulador) es igual de fácil que el suyo; **lo difícil es leer el tablero bien**, y ahí el techo es el reconocimiento de la carta por su arte.

Por eso M0 es lo que es: **primero probamos que podemos capturar la pantalla de forma estable** (sin los freezes del spike). Si el CSV de tu móvil sale limpio, el siguiente paso (M1/reconocimiento) ya ataca la parte de visión que nos acerca a HDT.

**Dos proyectos distintos** dan el mismo *"your project has been denied access"*. Cuando **varios** proyectos de la **misma cuenta** dan "denied access", el problema no es de un proyecto suelto: es que **Google ha marcado/suspendido la cuenta** (típicamente por **billing sin verificar, un pago rechazado, o una revisión de política**). Crear otra key del mismo sitio dará lo mismo.

## Lo bueno: hay una pista aprovechable

La tercera key (`AQ.…K4g`) da un error **diferente** — *"method blocked"*, NO "denied access". Eso significa que **ese proyecto NO está suspendido**; solo tiene la **API de Gemini sin habilitar** (o la key con restricciones). Ese es el arreglo **más rápido y probable**:

**Camino A (rápido, ese proyecto):**
1. Ve a https://console.cloud.google.com → selecciona el proyecto de la key `…K4g`.
2. Habilita **"Generative Language API"** (APIs y servicios → Habilitar API → buscar "Generative Language").
3. Si la key tiene "restricciones de API", quítalas o añade Generative Language.
4. Me pasas esa key otra vez y la testeo — si da **200**, lista.

**Camino B (si A falla — cuenta marcada):**
- Mira en https://console.cloud.google.com si hay un **banner rojo de billing/verificación** en los proyectos "denied". Suele ser: añadir/verificar tarjeta, o apelar la suspensión. Eso lo tienes que resolver tú con Google.
- Alternativa limpia: sacar una key desde una **cuenta Google distinta** con billing propio.

## Arreglo (en la key, 1 minuto)

   - Deja "Restringir" pero **añade "Generative Language API"** a la lista de APIs permitidas.
5. **Guardar.** Tarda 1–5 min en propagar.

*(Nota: puede que también tenga "Restricciones de aplicación" por IP/referrer — si las tiene, o las quitas, o añades la IP del server `178.63.165.87`, porque la llamada sale desde ahí.)*

El puente hoy llama a **Gemini vía AI Studio**, que se autentica con una **API key simple** (`?key=…`), no con cuenta de servicio. Las **cuentas de servicio** son para **Vertex AI**, que es otro endpoint (`aiplatform.googleapis.com`) y otra forma de auth. Son dos caminos distintos:

## Cómo funciona hoy (BEFORE)

- **Workdir:** `bridge.py:52` → `WORKDIR = env("BRIDGE_WORKDIR", "/opt/lyai/app/lyai-ski")`. Es **global y fijo**, se lee una vez al arrancar. `run_claude` lanza `claude -p` con `cwd=WORKDIR` (línea 803). Por eso siempre trabajo en lyai-ski.
- **Sesión:** dict `sessions[chat_id] = session_id` en `session.json`. Cada mensaje hace `claude -p --resume <sid>`. 
- **Ya existe** `/reset` (línea 900) → borra tu sid → el siguiente mensaje arranca **sesión nueva**. O sea, "sesión nueva" ya lo tienes; lo que falta es **cambiar de directorio**.

## Propuesta (AFTER) — comando `/proj`

**1. Registro de proyectos** (arriba del archivo):
```python
PROJECTS = {
    "ski":      "/opt/lyai/app/lyai-ski",
    "deckview": "/opt/lyai/deckview",
    "online":   "/opt/lyai/app/lyai.online",
    "mcp":      "/opt/lyai/app/lyai-mcp",
}
```

**2. Workdir por-chat** (en vez del global): `workdirs[chat_id]`, persistido junto a `session.json`. En `run_claude`:
```python
workdir = workdirs.get(str(chat_id), WORKDIR)
proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=workdir, ...)
```

**3. Clave de sesión por (chat + proyecto)** — esto es **necesario**, no cosmético: una sesión de Claude está atada a su cwd (carga el `CLAUDE.md` y la memoria de esa carpeta). Resumir el sid de *ski* dentro de *deckview* cargaría el contexto equivocado o daría error. Solución:
```python
key = f"{chat_id}:{workdir}"     # sessions[key] = sid
```
Así **cada proyecto guarda su propio hilo** y al volver a él retomas donde lo dejaste.

**4. Comandos nuevos** en `handle_command()`:
| Comando | Efecto |
|---|---|
| `/proj` | Lista proyectos + muestra el actual |
| `/proj deckview` | Cambia tu cwd a `/opt/lyai/deckview` y **resume su hilo** (o nuevo si no hay) |
| `/cd /ruta/abs` | Igual pero ruta libre — **validada**: existe, es dir, y **dentro de `/opt/lyai`** (evita escapes) |
| `/new` | Sesión nueva en el proyecto **actual** (alias claro de `/reset`) |
| `/where` | Muestra cwd + sid actuales |

Cada cambio responde confirmando: *"📁 deckview · /opt/lyai/deckview · retomando sesión abc123"*.

## Ventaja clave
Desde el mismo chat de Telegram saltas ski ↔ deckview ↔ online, y **cada uno mantiene su conversación y su memoria** por separado. Resuelve de paso el problema que ya sufrimos con deckview ("no me acuerdo de la sesión anterior") — porque ahora sí arrancaría en su carpeta con su `CLAUDE.md`.

- **B) Multi-bridge:** un servicio systemd por proyecto con `BRIDGE_WORKDIR` distinto y otro bot token. Cero código, pero son varios bots y no cambias en caliente.

## Ya implementados en el bridge (nivel bridge, no llegan a Claude)

| Comando | Qué hace |
|---|---|
| `/help`, `/start` | ayuda |
| `/reset` | olvida la sesión → hilo nuevo |
| `/status` | ocupado/libre + session id + cola + estado voz |
| `/voz on\|off` | respuesta hablada automática (propio del bridge, no existe en CLI) |
| `/stop` | mata la tarea en curso + vacía cola |
| `/imagen <desc>` | (solo modo invitado) genera imagen |

## Candidatos a añadir (pasarían tal cual como texto a `claude -p`)

| Comando | Equivalente CLI | Riesgo/nota |
|---|---|---|
| `/model opus\|sonnet\|haiku\|fable` | selector de modelo | Con argumento explícito no debería requerir picker interactivo — **a verificar si persiste entre mensajes**, porque cada mensaje del bridge lanza un `claude -p --resume` nuevo (proceso distinto), no una sesión viva |
| `/effort low\|medium\|high\|xhigh\|max` | nivel de esfuerzo | mismo caveat de persistencia que `/model` |
| `/config <clave>=<valor>` | settings de sesión | igual, a probar persistencia |
| `/nginx`, `/code-review`, `/save-session`, etc. | skills del proyecto | deberían funcionar igual que en esta sesión, son solo prompts que se expanden |
| `/clear` | limpiar contexto | redundante con `/reset` del bridge — mejor no duplicar |

## Lo que NO añadiría

- **`/memory`** — en TUI abre un editor (`$EDITOR`/`$VISUAL`, como acabas de ver en esta sesión). En headless sin terminal esto es un riesgo real: si el proceso intenta lanzar un editor que no existe, podría quedarse colgado hasta el timeout de 30 min del bridge. No lo probaría sin antes revisar cómo se comporta `-p` ante ese comando.
- Comandos puramente de shell interactivo (`/login`, atajos de teclado, etc.) — no tienen sentido headless.

## Punto abierto que hay que probar en vivo

El bridge crea un **subproceso nuevo por cada mensaje** (`--resume <sid>`, no un proceso persistente). No tengo certeza de si `/model`/`/effort` dejan su efecto grabado en la sesión resumible o si se resetean en el siguiente mensaje — habría que probarlo con un mensaje real y comprobar si el segundo mensaje conserva el cambio.

# Schedule Cloud Agents

You are helping the user schedule, update, list, or run **cloud** Claude Code agents. These are NOT local cron jobs — each routine spawns a fully isolated cloud session (CCR) in Anthropic's cloud infrastructure, either on a recurring cron schedule or once at a specific time. The agent runs in a sandboxed environment with its own git checkout, tools, and optional MCP connections.

## First Step

The user has already told you what they want (see User Request at the bottom). Skip the initial question and go directly to the matching workflow.


## What You Can Do

Use the `RemoteTrigger` tool (load it first with `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger`; auth is handled in-process — do not use curl):

- `{action: "list"}` — list all routines
- `{action: "get", trigger_id: "..."}` — fetch one routine
- `{action: "create", body: {...}}` — create a routine
- `{action: "update", trigger_id: "...", body: {...}}` — partial update
- `{action: "run", trigger_id: "..."}` — run a routine now

(Note: the API uses `trigger_id` as the parameter name, but the user-facing term is "routine".)

You CANNOT delete routines. If the user asks to delete, direct them to: https://claude.ai/code/routines

## Create body shape

For a recurring schedule:

```json
{
  "name": "AGENT_NAME",
  "cron_expression": "CRON_EXPR",
  "enabled": true,
  "job_config": {
    "ccr": {
      "environment_id": "ENVIRONMENT_ID",
      "session_context": {
        "model": "claude-sonnet-5",
        "sources": [
          {"git_repository": {"url": "https://github.com/LyAi-labs/lyai-ski"}}
        ],
        "allowed_tools": ["Bash", "Read", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep"]
      },
      "events": [
        {"data": {
          "uuid": "<lowercase v4 uuid>",
          "session_id": "",
          "type": "user",
          "parent_tool_use_id": null,
          "message": {"content": "PROMPT_HERE", "role": "user"}
        }}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

For a one-time run, replace `"cron_expression": "CRON_EXPR"` with `"run_once_at": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ"` (RFC3339 UTC, must be in the future). Everything else is identical.

Generate a fresh lowercase UUID for `events[].data.uuid` yourself.

## API Field Reference

### Create Routine — Required Fields
- `name` (string) — A descriptive name
- Exactly ONE of:
  - `cron_expression` (string) — 5-field cron in UTC. **Minimum interval is 1 hour.**
  - `run_once_at` (string) — RFC3339 UTC timestamp. Must be in the future. Fires once, then auto-disables.
- `job_config` (object) — Session configuration (see structure above)

### Create Routine — Optional Fields
- `enabled` (boolean, default: true)
- `mcp_connections` (array) — MCP servers to attach:
  ```json
  [{"connector_uuid": "uuid", "name": "server-name", "url": "https://..."}]
  ```

### Update Routine — Optional Fields
All fields optional (partial update):
- `name`, `cron_expression`, `run_once_at`, `enabled`, `job_config`
- `mcp_connections` — Replace MCP connections
- `clear_mcp_connections` (boolean) — Remove all MCP connections

### Cron Expression Examples

The user's local timezone is **UTC**. Cron expressions and `run_once_at` timestamps are always in UTC. When the user says a local time, convert it to UTC but confirm with them: "9am UTC = Xam UTC, so the cron would be `0 X * * 1-5`." For one-time runs, the same conversion applies — "run this at 3pm" → `"run_once_at": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00:00Z"` with their 3pm converted to UTC.

- `0 9 * * 1-5` — Every weekday at 9am **UTC**
- `0 */2 * * *` — Every 2 hours
- `0 0 * * *` — Daily at midnight **UTC**
- `30 14 * * 1` — Every Monday at 2:30pm **UTC**
- `0 8 1 * *` — First of every month at 8am **UTC**

Minimum interval is 1 hour. `*/30 * * * *` will be rejected.

### Current Time (for one-off runs)

When /schedule was invoked it was **Tue, Jul 14, 2026, 08:51 AM** (UTC) / **2026-07-14T08:51:40.420Z** UTC. Treat this as an approximate anchor only — the conversation may have been running for a while since then.

**Before computing any `run_once_at` value, you MUST re-check the current time** by running `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` via the Bash tool. Do not guess or infer today's date from conversation context. Resolve relative requests ("tomorrow at 9am", "in 3 hours", "next Monday") against the freshly fetched time, then echo the resolved local time AND the UTC timestamp back to the user for confirmation before creating the routine. If the resolved time is already in the past, ask the user to clarify rather than silently rolling forward.

## Workflow

### CREATE a new routine:

1. **Understand the goal** — Ask what they want the cloud agent to do. What repo(s)? What task? Remind them that the agent runs in the cloud — it won't have access to their local machine, local files, or local environment variables.
2. **Craft the prompt** — Help them write an effective agent prompt. Good prompts are:
   - Specific about what to do and what success looks like
   - Clear about which files/areas to focus on
   - Explicit about what actions to take (open PRs, commit, just analyze, etc.)
3. **Set the schedule** — Ask when and how often. The user's timezone is UTC. When they say a time (e.g., "every morning at 9am"), assume they mean their local time and convert to UTC for the cron expression. Always confirm the conversion: "9am UTC = Xam UTC." If they want a one-time run (e.g., "once at 3pm", "tomorrow morning", "remind me to check X later"), use `run_once_at` instead of `cron_expression` — same timezone conversion applies. **First re-check the current time with `date -u` via Bash** (the reference time above may be stale in a long conversation), resolve the relative phrase against that fresh value, and confirm the resulting absolute timestamp with the user.
4. **Choose the model** — Default to `claude-sonnet-5`. Tell the user which model you're defaulting to and ask if they want a different one.
5. **Validate connections** — Infer what services the agent will need from the user's description. For example, if they say "check Datadog and Slack me errors," the agent needs both Datadog and Slack MCP connectors. Cross-reference with the connectors list above. If any are missing, warn the user and link them to https://claude.ai/customize/connectors to connect first. The default git repo is already set to `https://github.com/LyAi-labs/lyai-ski`. Ask the user if this is the right repo or if they need a different one.
6. **Review and confirm** — Show the full configuration before creating. Let them adjust.
7. **Create it** — Call `RemoteTrigger` with `action: "create"` and show the result. The response includes the routine ID. Always output a link at the end: `https://claude.ai/code/routines/{ROUTINE_ID}`

### UPDATE a routine:

1. List routines first so they can pick one
2. Ask what they want to change
3. Show current vs proposed value
4. Confirm and update

### LIST routines:

1. Fetch and display in a readable format
2. Show: name, schedule (human-readable), enabled/disabled, next run, repo(s)

### RUN NOW:

1. List routines if they haven't specified which one
2. Confirm which routine
3. Execute and confirm

## Important Notes

- These are CLOUD agents — they run in Anthropic's cloud, not on the user's machine. They cannot access local files, local services, or local environment variables.
- Always convert cron to human-readable when displaying
- When listing routines, `ended_reason: "run_once_fired"` means a one-shot already ran (shows as "Ran" in the web UI). The user can re-arm it by updating with a new `run_once_at`.
- Default to `enabled: true` unless user says otherwise
- Accept GitHub URLs in any format (https://github.com/org/repo, org/repo, etc.) and normalize to the full HTTPS URL (without .git suffix)
- The prompt is the most important part — spend time getting it right. The cloud agent starts with zero context, so the prompt must be self-contained.
